constraints.reasoningTemp: Reasoning models use a fixed temperature of 1.0. This parameter will be ignored by the API.

tooltips.temperature: Controls randomness in responses. Low (0-0.3): precise, deterministic outputs. High (0.7-1.0): more creative and varied responses.
tooltips.topP: Alternative to temperature. Only considers tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds this threshold. 0.1 = very focused, 1.0 = full vocabulary.
tooltips.frequencyPenalty: Reduces repetition by penalizing tokens already frequent in the output. Positive (0.5-1.0) discourages verbatim repetition. Range: -2 to 2.
tooltips.presencePenalty: Encourages topic diversity. Penalizes each token that has appeared, regardless of frequency. Positive = explores more topics. Range: -2 to 2.
tooltips.maxTokens: Maximum number of output tokens. Limits the length of the generated response. Optimal value depends on the agent type.
tooltips.timeout: Maximum wait time in seconds before aborting the API call. Leave empty to use the provider's default.
tooltips.reasoningEffort: Controls the model's internal thinking intensity. Higher = better accuracy but increased latency and cost. Lower = fast responses for simple tasks.
tooltips.effort: Global effort control (Anthropic): trades response thoroughness for token efficiency across text, tool calls, and thinking. Lower = cheaper and faster. Default = high.

skills.delete_admin_confirm_description: Skill "{{name}}" will be permanently deleted from the system. This action cannot be undone.
skills.edit_description_hint: Write the description in your language. It will be automatically translated to English (stored in SKILL.md) and all 6 interface languages.
skills.guide_modal_subtitle: Learn how to create skills to customize and extend LIA's capabilities.
skills.guide_modal_what_body: A skill is a SKILL.md file that gives the assistant expert instructions for a specific domain. The assistant reads these instructions and applies them automatically when relevant — without you having to repeat the context each time. Skills can include reference documents, Python scripts, and templates.
skills.guide_archetype_prompt_expert_desc: Expert instructions the assistant follows for a domain (coaching, writing, methodology…). No specific tools — the assistant applies its conversational expertise.
skills.guide_archetype_advisory_desc: A structured methodology where the assistant uses available tools organically (calendar, emails, contacts…). It decides which tools to call based on context.
skills.guide_archetype_plan_template_desc: A deterministic workflow with predefined tool calls, executed in sequence or in parallel. Ideal for recurring routines (briefings, reports, audits…).
skills.guide_activation_body: Skills use a 3-tier loading model to optimize token consumption:
skills.guide_tier_l1: Catalogue — Name and description loaded at session start (~50 tokens/skill)
skills.guide_tier_l2: Instructions — Full SKILL.md body loaded when the skill is activated (< 5000 tokens)
skills.guide_tier_l3: Resources — Individual files (references/, scripts/, assets/) loaded on demand
skills.guide_modal_tip_1: Write the description in English, third person: "Generates...", "Provides...", "Guides..."
skills.guide_modal_tip_2: The description should state what the skill does AND when to use it (the trigger).
skills.guide_modal_tip_3: Keep instructions concise and structured — prefer numbered lists.
skills.guide_modal_tip_4: Name your skill in kebab-case: my-skill (lowercase, hyphens, no spaces).
skills.guide_modal_tip_5: List available resources at the end of SKILL.md with their relative path and a description.
skills.guide_modal_tip_6: Test with simple queries before making the skill more complex.
skills.guide_modal_format_intro: A SKILL.md file starts with a YAML header (between ---) containing metadata, followed by a Markdown body with the detailed instructions.
skills.guide_field_category: UI grouping (quotidien, recherche, communication, organisation, productivite, developpement)
skills.guide_field_always_loaded: Always inject instructions (costs tokens every conversation)
skills.guide_field_outputs: Declared output channels (text, frame, image) — only for Visualizer / Generator skills
skills.guide_field_compatibility: Prerequisites shown in the catalogue (e.g. "Requires Calendar connector")
skills.guide_runtime_intro: When your skill uses a Python script, the LIA platform auto-provides several behaviors — here is what to know to produce skills that blend in naturally.
skills.guide_runtime_autoparams_body: Every run_skill_script call receives the user's language (_lang) and timezone (_tz) in its parameters. Use _lang to localize your labels via inline translation tables.
skills.guide_runtime_autoparams_hint: Do not rely on locale.setlocale — slim container images don't ship system locales, so strftime silently falls back to English.
skills.guide_runtime_theme_body: Use html[data-theme="dark"] CSS selectors rather than @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). A runtime snippet injected by LIA applies the data-theme attribute and the lang on <html>, kept in sync with the app.
skills.guide_runtime_resize_body: Iframes self-resize to match the content height. The aspect_ratio you declare is only the initial skeleton before measurement. Keep html/body margins default, style your own inner containers.
skills.guide_runtime_example_qr: Generator example (QR code via segno, localized caption):
skills.guide_runtime_interactive_note: Recommended pattern for any interactive frame: client JS with crypto.getRandomValues and addEventListener — inline onclick is blocked by CSP on user skills.
skills.guide_example_simple_desc: The simplest type — pure instructions the assistant follows when the topic comes up. No tools or plan needed.
skills.guide_example_advisory_desc: The assistant follows a methodology and uses available tools (calendar, emails, contacts) organically as needed.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_intro: Skills can emit interactive iframes and generated images by writing a JSON object on stdout. The skill decides what to render — all three channels (text, frame, image) are independent and can coexist.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_text_label: Always required — caption used for voice, LLM context, and accessibility.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_frame_label: Optional interactive iframe (inline HTML via srcDoc or external HTTPS URL).
skills.guide_rich_outputs_image_label: Optional image artifact (data: URI or HTTPS URL) with required alt text.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_example_map: Visualizer example — interactive Google Maps embed:
skills.guide_rich_outputs_example_qr: Generator example — QR code image generated from text:
skills.guide_rich_outputs_sandbox: All frames render inside an iframe sandbox without allow-same-origin — parent cookies and storage are unreachable regardless of the frame content.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_csp: When a user-owned skill emits frame.html, LIA automatically injects a strict Content Security Policy that blocks outbound fetch/XHR (connect-src none) and nested iframes (frame-src none). System skills are trusted and skip CSP injection.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_csp_warning: Consequence: user-skill inline frames cannot call external APIs. For external data, use frame.url instead (the remote site controls its own headers).
skills.guide_rich_outputs_tip_1: Write only the JSON on stdout — put logs and progress on stderr.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_tip_2: frame.html and frame.url are mutually exclusive — a frame has one source.
skills.guide_rich_outputs_tip_3: Always set image.alt for accessibility and voice fallback.
skills.guide_modal_struct_body: For complex skills, import a .zip file containing SKILL.md and optional sub-folders:
skills.guide_struct_scripts: Python scripts executed in a sandbox
skills.guide_resource_references_desc: Text documents (.md, .txt) the assistant can read on demand via read_skill_resource. Ideal for storing detailed guides, templates, or reference data too large for the SKILL.md.
skills.guide_resource_references_usage: Usage: mention the file in the "Available Resources" section of your SKILL.md — the assistant will read them automatically.
skills.guide_resource_scripts_desc: Python scripts (.py) executed in an isolated sandbox via run_skill_script. They receive data as JSON on stdin and return results as JSON on stdout.
skills.guide_resource_scripts_usage: Usage: describe the script and its parameters in SKILL.md. The assistant will execute it when needed.
skills.guide_resource_assets_desc: Static files (images, HTML/CSV templates, JSON data) accessible for reading. Useful for output templates, logos, or configurations.
skills.guide_resource_assets_usage: Usage: reference them in the instructions. The assistant can read and use them to format responses.
skills.guide_import_body: Import a single SKILL.md file for a simple skill, or a .zip file containing the complete folder (SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/ + assets/). Use the "Import" button above. Limits: 100 KB for SKILL.md, 50 KB per resource file, 20 skills max per user.
skills.guide_modal_plan_body: The plan_template defines a sequence of tools executed automatically, bypassing the LLM planner. Ideal for recurring, predictable workflows. Steps without depends_on run in parallel.
skills.guide_modal_plan_field_agent_name: Agent name to use (see catalogue below)
skills.guide_modal_plan_field_step_type: Type: TOOL (default), CONDITIONAL, PARALLEL or RESPONSE
skills.guide_autotrigger_body: Skills with plan_template are auto-triggered when the user's query covers ALL domains in the template. E.g., a skill with event_agent + weather_agent triggers when the user asks for both their schedule and the weather.
skills.guide_tools_intro: Complete reference of agents and their tools with parameters and types. Use exact names in the plan_template's agent_name and tool_name. Parameters marked * are required.
skills.guide_tools_note: Tools marked "Connector" work with Google, Microsoft, or Apple depending on the connected provider. MCP agents (external servers) are dynamic and cannot be used in static plan_templates.
skills.param_content_instruction: AI instruction to compose the body
skills.param_color: Color (red, blue, warm_white… or CIE x,y)
skills.param_source_image: UUID of the source image to edit
skills.guide_scripts_body: Skills can include Python scripts executed in an isolated sandbox. Scripts receive data via stdin (JSON) and return results via stdout (JSON). Useful for calculations, data transformations, or custom processing.
skills.guide_scripts_rule_1: Only .py files in the scripts/ folder are allowed
skills.guide_scripts_rule_2: Scripts run in a sandbox with a limited timeout
skills.guide_scripts_rule_3: Communication via stdin/stdout in JSON format
skills.guide_skill_tools_body: The assistant has 3 special tools to interact with activated skills. These tools are called automatically — you don't need to reference them in your instructions.
skills.guide_skilltool_activate: Loads the full instructions (L2) of a skill
skills.guide_skilltool_read: Reads a reference or asset file from the skill
skills.guide_skilltool_run: Executes a Python script from the scripts/ folder
skills.guide_modal_compat_body: Skills are 100% compatible with the agentskills.io ecosystem — the same format is used by Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot and 30+ other products. Import skills from marketplaces like skillsmp.com.
skills.guide_modal_link: Learn more about the agentskills.io standard

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find answers to the most common questions about LIA

intro.title: How LIA Works
intro.description: LIA is a next-generation AI assistant that combines advanced technologies to offer you an intelligent, secure, and personalized experience. Answers are generated server-side independently of your connection: you can leave the page mid-response and find it — or resume it live — when you come back.

architecture.title: 🏗️ LangGraph Multi-Agent Architecture
architecture.description: LIA uses LangGraph, a state graph framework for AI agent orchestration. 19+ specialized domain agents (contacts, email, calendar, drive, tasks, weather, wikipedia, perplexity, brave, web_search, web_fetch, places, routes, reminders, hue, browser, health, context, query) + dynamic MCP agents, each with conditional transitions and state persistence via PostgreSQL checkpointing. Dynamic MCP agents extend capabilities without limit.

queryAnalyzer.title: 🧭 Query Analyzer v3.2
queryAnalyzer.description: Unified LLM query analysis (P95 < 800ms): intent detection (action/conversation), multi-domain routing with confidence, English normalization, temporal/contextual reference resolution. Smart risk detection: mutation_intent, cardinality_risk, for_each_detected. Automatic semantic expansion of related domains via the type registry.

routing.title: 🧭 Semantic Routing & AI-Powered Embeddings
routing.description: Intelligent router with multilingual semantic embeddings (100+ languages). Automatic semantic expansion of related domains (weather → location, calendar → contacts). Dynamically filtered capabilities catalog (96% token reduction). Adaptive HARD/SOFT/FALLBACK thresholds for optimal precision.

query.title: 🔍 Query Analysis
query.description: Semantic query analysis engine: intent extraction, named entity identification, temporal and spatial constraint detection, and action type classification (read, create, modify, delete). Support for ambiguous queries with automatic clarification requests.

planning.title: 📋 Intelligent Planning & FOR_EACH
planning.description: Advanced planner with execution DSL. FOR_EACH pattern for bulk iterations ('Send an email to all my contacts in group X'). Dependency graphs with automatic parallel execution. PANIC mode with adaptive retry. Golden Patterns (~100 pre-trained models) for optimal planning from the first try. Each FOR_EACH iteration keeps its own results: an enrichment fetched for one appointment can no longer be overwritten by another sharing the same place and day, and every result keeps a stable identity when a run is replayed or resumed after an interruption.

semanticTypes.title: 📦 Semantic Type System
semanticTypes.description: 100 semantic types organized in DAG hierarchy (inspired by schema.org/RDF/SKOS). Categories: Identity, Location, Temporal, ResourceID, Content, Measurement, Status. Central TypeRegistry with O(1) lookups, Wu & Palmer distance calculation, subsumption validation. Type↔tool links are the union of the editorial ontology and the semantic_type annotations carried by tool manifests (live, rename-proof source that also covers MCP tools), with 5 test-enforced integrity locks preventing any drift (real tool names, domain vocabulary, taxonomy↔types coherence). These links feed the planner, the proactive initiative and ReAct mode (ADR-090). Manifests are deeply annotated (event attendees, email sender, route destination…), enabling cross-domain chains, an execution guardrail (a person's name can never be used where an address or email is expected) and evidence-driven expansion: a referenced entity (person, meeting, place, email) automatically brings in the tools able to provide the missing data (ADR-120, ADR-121).

semanticValidation.title: ✅ Semantic Plan Validation
semanticValidation.description: LLM detection of 15 types of anomalies before execution: incomplete plan, missing tool, wrong parameters, logical incoherence, impossible constraint, temporal paradox, excessive cost, empty result, missing dependency, conflict between steps, ambiguous reference, unsupported format, exceeded capacity, unjustified privilege escalation, circular dependency. Criticality analysis (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) based on reversibility. Bayesian Pattern Learning integration (bypass >90% confidence). P95 < 2s with short-circuit for trivial plans.

semantic.title: 🎯 Semantic Validation & Pivot
semantic.description: Semantic validation of plans before execution to detect logical inconsistencies. Semantic pivot system allowing automatic reformulation of failed queries with alternative strategies (synonyms, criteria broadening, decomposition).

context.title: 🧠 Advanced Context Management
context.description: LIA resolves explicit references ('the first email') and implicit ones ('send him a message') through an entity resolution engine. The system maintains a typed data registry (emails, contacts, events) for automatic disambiguation with user suggestions when needed. When an exchange calls no tool, the answer is re-anchored on the entities actually retrieved in earlier turns — age-bounded, and never taking precedence over current-turn data: LIA quotes the time it read, not the one it remembers. And when a piece of information was never retrieved, it says so plainly instead of reconstructing it.

memory.title: 💾 Dual Short/Long-Term Memory
memory.description: Short-term: sliding message window with automatic conversation-context summarization. The summary is resilient — per-chunk and global timeouts, exponential-backoff retries, explicit truncation fallback if the LLM fails; a visual toast surfaces while it runs and the input is locked for the duration, while a pill in the chat header continuously shows the tokens/threshold ratio. Long-term: extraction of facts about you (preferences, relationships, habits) stored with semantic embeddings. Hybrid BM25 + semantic search for optimal recall: both exact keywords AND meaning are used to retrieve your relevant memories.

interests.title: ✨ Smart Interest Learning
interests.description: Automatic learning of your interests through LLM conversation analysis. Interests are grouped into subjects by batch LLM clustering, and notification selection draws with two-level rarity (subject cooldown + priority to the least-served subjects) — one passion never monopolizes. Content via Perplexity, Brave, Wikipedia or AI reflection, with clickable source links appended deterministically. Bayesian weighting with temporal decay, nightly merge of near-duplicate topics. Full control: feedback, blocking, configurable time window and frequency.

summarization.title: 📝 Automatic Summarization
summarization.description: Intelligent summarization system for long conversations to maintain context without exceeding token limits. Key information extraction, semantic compression, and contextual injection into prompts to preserve conversational continuity.

hitl.title: 👤 Advanced Human-in-the-Loop
hitl.description: 8 intelligent interaction types: clarification, entity disambiguation (ENTITY_DISAMBIGUATION), plan approval, tool confirmation, draft critique, edit confirmation (EDIT_CONFIRMATION), bulk operation confirmation (FOR_EACH), and destructive validation (mass deletions ≥3 items). Configurable thresholds and item preview before execution. Review loops are replay-safe (ADR-092): one interrupt per node execution with loop state flowing through the checkpointed graph state — each LLM modification runs exactly once and the confirmed content is guaranteed identical to the last content displayed.

connectors.title: 🔌 Connectors & Registry
connectors.description: Modular architecture with connector registry (Google Calendar, Gmail, People, Tasks, Drive, Places, Routes, Apple iCloud Mail/Calendar/Contacts, Microsoft Outlook/Calendar/Contacts/To Do, OpenWeatherMap, Wikipedia, Perplexity, Brave Search). Each connector has declarative manifests, JSON schemas auto-generated from Python types, and unified OAuth/API-key/credential management.

streaming.title: ⚡ Streaming & Real-Time
streaming.description: SSE (Server-Sent Events) streaming responses with typed events: tokens, tool states, HITL requests, execution metadata. The frontend displays each execution step in real time (routing, planning, validation, tool calls) with accumulated progress, then streams the response token by token.

llm.title: 🤖 Multi-Provider LLM & Pattern Learning
llm.description: Support for OpenAI (GPT-5.4, o3), Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Perplexity, and local Ollama. Bayesian learning of planning patterns (≥90% confidence → LLM bypass). Average 89% token savings. Configurable profiles per task with real-time cost tracking.

security.title: 🔐 Multi-Layer Security
security.description: Defence in depth, from sign-in to data. Strong authentication (ADR-143): WebAuthn passkeys (Face ID, fingerprint — phishing-resistant), TOTP second factor with single-use backup codes, and step-up re-authentication for sensitive actions. My devices (ADR-144): every live session is visible and revocable, with deliberately bounded metadata (browser/OS families, truncated IP) and an alert on any sign-in from an unrecognized device. Underneath: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for Google services, distributed locking for token refresh, PII filtering in logs and traces, per-user/endpoint rate limiting, complete user isolation, Fernet encryption of sensitive data. Full GDPR export (ADR-145): a Markdown + JSON + files archive with secret material unexportable by construction. Automated daily backups with three-tier rotation and one-command tested restore (ADR-109).

resilience.title: 🛡️ Performance & Token Optimization
resilience.description: Text Compaction (~97% reduction per entity after Jinja templates). Circuit Breaker for external APIs. Multi-level Redis cache. Message windowing (93% token reduction). OAuth Proactive Refresh (tokens refreshed in background). Distributed rate limiting with exponential retry.

voice.title: 🎙️ Full Voice Mode
voice.description: Bidirectional system. TTS is catalogue-driven (admin-configured): three providers seeded — Edge (Microsoft neural voices, free, default), OpenAI (tts-1 / tts-1-hd) and ElevenLabs (eleven_multilingual_v2 / eleven_turbo_v2_5 / eleven_flash_v2_5). Sentence-level streaming starts the first audio in ~1 s. STT defaults to free, on-server Sherpa-onnx Whisper (99+ languages, audio never leaves the server); each user can opt into remote ElevenLabs Scribe ($0.22/h) for higher accuracy on conversational speech. Per-message cost badges (🎤 user / 🔊 assistant) for paid voice calls; admin-side kill switch and 5-min duration cap protect against cost spikes. Activate with "OK Guy" wake word or microphone button; auto end-of-speech detection (VAD). The spoken text is systematically stripped of markup (formatting HTML, decorative icons) so the voice reads the sentence and nothing else.

reminders.title: 🔔 Reminders & Push Notifications
reminders.description: Personal reminder system with multi-device FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging) push notifications. Natural language creation, automatic timezone conversion, intelligent reference resolution ('next one', number, content match). Messages personalized with active personality and user memories.

personalities.title: 🎭 14 Dynamic Personalities
personalities.description: 14 pre-configured personalities (Normal, Enthusiastic, Professor, Friend, Influencer, Philosopher, Cynic, Poet, Coach...) with prompts translated in 6 languages. Each personality defines the assistant's tone, style and behavior. Full CRUD system: administrators can create, edit, enable/disable personalities. Per-user selection with automatic translation into their language.

geolocation.title: 📍 Smart Geolocation
geolocation.description: Dual location system: configurable home address in preferences and real-time position via browser Geolocation API. Used for place searches, local weather, and distance calculations. Consent management and automatic fallback.

i18n.title: 🌍 Complete Internationalization
i18n.description: 6 supported languages (FR, EN, ES, DE, IT, ZH) with: interface translation (i18next), localized dates (relative and absolute formats), agent responses in user language, gettext translations for backend, and automatic browser language detection.

observability.title: 📊 Production-Ready Observability
observability.description: Full stack: Prometheus metrics (tokens, latency, errors, costs), 25 Grafana dashboards, Tempo distributed tracing, Loki centralized logs, and Langfuse integration for LLM performance analysis. Active email alerting: a 13-alert vital core with per-environment thresholds and a linked runbook on every alert. Dedicated liveness (/health) and readiness (/ready) probes separate “the process is up” from “PostgreSQL and Redis can actually serve you”.

tools.title: 🔧 75+ Typed Tools
tools.description: Over 75 native tools with JSON schemas auto-generated from Python/Pydantic, infinitely extensible via MCP servers. Declarative manifests with semantic_keywords for intelligent routing. Unified StandardToolOutput with registry updates for contextual references.

costTransparency.title: 💰 Cost Transparency
costTransparency.description: Optional real-time display: input/output/cache tokens, EUR cost per message and conversation total. Dashboard statistics: messages, tokens, and costs for current cycle. User control via 💲 icon in title bar.

scheduledActions.title: 📅 Scheduled Actions
scheduledActions.description: Recurring actions executed automatically by the assistant on a defined schedule. Configure days of the week and a time, attach a prompt instruction and LIA will execute it automatically. Results archived in conversation and notified via push. Auto-disable after 5 consecutive failures. The notification body carries the final post-processed text — the same one archived in the conversation — flattened to plain text before truncation.

mcp.title: 🔌 MCP (Model Context Protocol)
mcp.description: Full MCP protocol support with admin and per-user servers. 4 authentication types (none, API key, bearer token, OAuth 2.1). Automatic tool discovery at connection test, LLM-generated domain descriptions for intelligent routing, and read_me content injection into the planner prompt for context-aware tool usage.

mcpApps.title: 📱 Interactive MCP Apps
mcpApps.description: Sandboxed HTML widgets rendered directly in the conversation via secure iframes. JSON-RPC PostMessage bridge for bidirectional communication. Built-in XSS protection and COEP credentialless policy for safe loading of external resources.

excalidraw.title: 🎨 Excalidraw Generation
excalidraw.description: LLM-driven diagram generation with structured intent mode: the planner generates a high-level intent (components, connections, layout), then dedicated LLM calls produce all Excalidraw elements (shapes and arrows). Supports architecture diagrams, workflows, org charts and more. Cheat sheet injected for format accuracy. Configurable dedicated LLM (MCP_EXCALIDRAW_LLM_*).

multichannel.title: 📲 Multi-Channel (Telegram)
multichannel.description: Generic multi-channel messaging architecture with Telegram as first implementation. Telegram bot with OTP binding for secure account linking. Voice message support with automatic transcription. Async webhook processing for reliable message handling.

heartbeatAutonome.title: 💓 Autonomous Heartbeat
heartbeatAutonome.description: LLM-driven proactive contextual notifications with 8 parallel data sources aggregated in real-time. 2-phase approach: structured decision (skip/notify via cheap model) then personality-aware message rewrite. Topics rotate through a varied interest sample and a content-level anti-repetition window (10 notifications / 7 days), so the same theme never comes back day after day. When a notification centers on an interest, real facts are fetched (Perplexity, Brave, Wikipedia) and clickable source links appended. Weather change detection (rain start/end, temperature drops, wind alerts). Configurable time windows and per-user push control. Every source is independently failable, and a source that drops out is counted and timed rather than silently missing: health indicators are read as per-day aggregates computed in the database (about fifty times lighter) and no longer vanish from notifications.

webFetch.title: 🌐 Intelligent Web Fetch
webFetch.description: Dedicated web content retrieval and extraction tool from any public URL, no API key required. Clean Markdown extraction via readability.js (articles, documentation, data). Multi-layer SSRF protection: DNS validation, post-redirect verification, content size limits, per-user rate limiting. Ideal for importing articles, documentation pages, or structured data directly into the conversation.

knowledgeEnrichment.title: 📰 Brave Search Contextual Enrichment
knowledgeEnrichment.description: Automatic response enrichment via Brave Search (Web + News). Before formulating its response, LIA searches for up-to-date data to contextualize and complement its knowledge. Smart Redis caching with global fallback to optimize API calls. Personal per-user Brave API key (configured in Settings > Connectors). Enables always up-to-date responses: news, prices, schedules, ongoing events, and more.

adaptiveReplanner.title: 🔄 Adaptive Replanning
adaptiveReplanner.description: Intelligent autonomous recovery from execution failures (empty results, partial failures, dependency errors, semantic mismatches). Rule-based analysis without additional LLM calls for speed. Recovery strategies: retry with adjusted parameters, skip non-critical steps, full re-planning if necessary. PANIC mode with exponential backoff. Users always receive the best possible response, even with partial failures.

semanticLeakDefense.title: 🛡️ Indexable vs Semantic criteria distinction
semanticLeakDefense.description: Universal validation layer that distinguishes indexable criteria (date, identifier, sender, status, location — passed as a tool parameter) from semantic criteria (category, urgency, quality, priority — filtered downstream by the response LLM). When the planner tries to filter a conceptual word like « medical » or « urgent » directly inside the search of a literal-search tool (Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion-like…), the layer detects the leak via word-boundary matching against the hint produced by the query analyzer, and emits a dedicated Prometheus counter. Universal mechanism: no current connector or future MCP server requires modification — declarative opt-out via ToolManifest.text_search_mode (« semantic » / « hybrid »). Operator control via PLANNER_SEMANTIC_LEAK_MODE=observe|autocorrect|off.

parallelExecution.title: ⚡ Wave-by-Wave Parallel Execution
parallelExecution.description: Native parallel execution engine built on asyncio.gather(), replacing LangGraph's broken Command+Send pattern. Automatic execution wave calculation via dependency graph: independent steps run simultaneously, dependent steps wait for prerequisites. Result: complex multi-domain plans (weather + routes + places + calendar) executed in seconds instead of sequentially.

dataRegistry.title: 🗂️ Data Registry & Rich Rendering
dataRegistry.description: Unified structured data system for rich display in conversations. 15+ registry types (Contact, Email, Event, Task, File, Place, Route, Weather, MCP App...). Immutable items with metadata, TTL, and deterministic IDs. Sent via SSE before the LLM response for instant card rendering. HTML template engine with multi-domain, hierarchical support, and automatic correlation between related results (e.g., event + route grouped together).

qualityAssurance.title: 🎯 LLM-as-Judge Quality Assurance
qualityAssurance.description: Automated response quality evaluation pipeline. Three specialized LLM evaluators: relevance (query/response adequacy), hallucination (fabricated content detection), latency (performance SLA compliance). Metrics exported to Prometheus and Langfuse for production monitoring. Real-time identification and correction of quality degradations.

attachments.title: 📎 Photos & File Attachments
attachments.description: Photo and PDF document upload via 📎 button or drag & drop, with automatic client-side compression. Visual analysis via configurable vision LLM (gpt-4.1-mini by default). PDF text extraction via PyMuPDF. Inline thumbnails in messages, accessible lightbox. Strict per-user isolation, automatic cleanup (conversation reset + 24h TTL). "Reference + Late Resolution" architecture for lightweight checkpoints.

skills.title: Skills (with interactive maps & mini-apps)
skills.description: Supercharge LIA with custom expert skills for your business or personal needs. Create your own skills in natural language with the built-in Skill Generator — installed instantly, ready to use — or import from agentskills.io-compatible marketplaces. Since v1.16.8, a skill can also return an interactive HTML frame (map, dashboard, calendar, converter...) or an image (QR code, chart) alongside text, with automatic theme and locale sync. Compatible with 30+ tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and VS Code.

ragSpaces.title: 📚 RAG Knowledge Spaces
ragSpaces.description: Create personal knowledge spaces and upload your own documents (PDF, TXT, MD, DOCX). Documents are automatically processed (text extraction, chunking, OpenAI embedding). Active spaces enrich assistant responses via hybrid search combining semantic similarity (pgvector cosine) and BM25 keyword matching. Full cost transparency with per-document and per-query embedding tracking. Admin reindexation endpoint for embedding model changes.

subAgents.title: Sub-Agents
subAgents.description: Delegate complex tasks to specialized ephemeral experts working in parallel. The assistant orchestrates and synthesizes their findings transparently.

browserControl.title: 🌐 Browser Control
browserControl.description: Interactive web browsing with autonomous navigation: search products on e-commerce sites, fill forms, extract data from JavaScript-rendered pages. The browser agent handles multi-step interactions through the site's own controls (search boxes, autocomplete, forms), re-checks the page after each action, and — on transactional flows — stops at the login / payment step and reports a summary; it never enters credentials or submits a payment.

psycheEngine.title: 🧠 Psyche Engine
psycheEngine.description: Dynamic psychological state that evolves with every exchange. Mood (22 emotions), energy, relationship with the user, personality traits (Big Five). The assistant organically adapts its tone, vocabulary and behavior — it never says it, it shows it. Built-in emotional safety: memories with strong negative charge trigger an automatic protective mode. And this life shows: the mood avatar animates on the current reply.

personalJournals.title: 📓 Personal Journals (stratified consciousness)
personalJournals.description: LIA keeps its own reflections in personal journals organized along four abstraction levels — L0 raw observation, L1 operational directive (WHEN→DO BECAUSE), L2 transversal pattern, L3 portrait facet — and an epistemic status (confidence, evidence/contradiction counters). A deferred self-evaluation loop measures, at the next turn, whether each injected directive was confirmed or contradicted by the user — at zero added LLM cost. The same consolidation call also compiles a user-model portrait (full ~200 tokens, brief ~60 tokens) diffused across eight flows where LIA speaks: conversation, planner, ReAct, voice, reminders, heartbeat, proactive interest, fallback. The user retains full control: read entries grouped by theme or level, edit level/confidence, signal a problem on the portrait, trigger a manual consolidation. The portrait itself is a synthesis voice — never directly edited.

healthMetrics.title: 🩺 iPhone health data (polymorphic batch upsert)
healthMetrics.description: Token-authenticated ingestion (SHA-256 hash stored, raw value shown once, display prefix hm_) over two per-kind endpoints (/ingest/health/steps, .../heart_rate). Client contract: an array of self-timestamped samples [{date_start, date_end, value, o}, …], UTC-normalized and second-truncated. Flexible parser accepting 4 envelope shapes (array, NDJSON, {data:[…]}, iOS "Dictionary" wrapping). Polymorphic single-table storage health_samples(kind, date_start, date_end, value) with PostgreSQL UPSERT ON CONFLICT … RETURNING (xmax = 0) splitting insert/update counts in a single round-trip. Intra-batch dedupe with per-kind arbitrage: MAX for steps, rounded AVG for heart_rate — absorbs overlapping Apple Watch + iPhone samples without SQL error. Mixed per-sample validation (out-of-range → individual rejection with index + bounded reason), polymorphic aggregator (AVG/MIN/MAX HR + SUM steps per bucket), gaps preserved for honest charting. Rate limit 60 req/h/token, 1000-sample batch cap.

imageGeneration.title: 🎨 Image Generation & Editing
imageGeneration.description: Generate images from text descriptions and edit existing images with natural language instructions. Multi-provider factory architecture, per-user quality/size/format preferences, cost tracking with database-cached pricing, attachment-based storage with cascade cleanup.

reactMode.title: ⚡ ReAct Execution Mode
reactMode.description: Alternative mode to the pipeline where the assistant reasons step by step: it calls a tool, analyzes the result, then autonomously decides what to do next. 4 custom nodes in the parent LangGraph graph with native HITL support via interrupt(). Pipeline mode (default) consumes 4 to 8× fewer tokens thanks to smart planning and parallel execution. Users switch between the two via a toggle in the chat header. Every conversation turn starts from a clean data registry (strict turn isolation), and the agent receives the cross-domain semantic type map with a precision rule: fetch the exact value (a contact's address) via the lookup tool rather than an approximation recalled from memory.

proactiveInitiative.title: 🎯 Proactive Initiative
proactiveInitiative.description: After completing the main request, the assistant evaluates whether results reveal cross-domain connections relevant to the user. Example: weather shows rain Saturday → checks calendar for outdoor activities. In Pipeline mode, a dedicated node runs the LLM evaluation after the answer. In ReAct mode the agent also cross-checks during its own reasoning (the CROSS-CHECK step) and — when enabled — the same dedicated initiative node now runs after the loop, so both modes get the proactive enrichment. The evaluation receives pre-computed connection candidates from the semantic type registry (which data from this turn can feed which adjacent tools — ADR-090), and prepares the final answer's context (memory, RAG, journal, psyche) in parallel to cut latency (ADR-091).

telephony.title: 📞 Agentic Telephony
telephony.description: LIA can place outbound phone calls through a goal-directed ElevenLabs Agent, driven by your own per-user connector (bring-your-own credentials — no LIA-side metering). Data protection is enforced by capability, not by prompt: the call agent exposes a single read-only availability tool that returns free/busy slots only — never event titles, attendees, locations or content. Nothing is recorded and the transcript is never persisted; when the call ends, a signed per-user webhook triggers a tool-less LLM synthesis reinjected asynchronously into the chat as a short, expiring summary with an optional one-tap follow-up. Every call is confirmed by you before dialing (HITL draft) and the whole subsystem is feature-flagged (ADR-127). The agent operates under a strict mandate enforced by its system prompt: no expense or commitment beyond the objective; any out-of-mandate offer is captured in dedicated structured fields (additional cost, pending decision) that the post-call synthesis must surface.

todayBriefing.title: 🌅 Today Briefing
todayBriefing.description: The dashboard home page is a daily briefing: personalized LLM greeting + 2-3 sentence synthesis above a 9-card grid (enriched weather, agenda, unread mails, birthdays, reminders, health, « For you » — open loops + automations digest —, pending/overdue tasks, latest Drive documents). Pure architecture: no LangGraph chain, parallel asyncio.gather, per-section Redis cache with adapted TTL (weather 1 h, agenda 10 min, mails 5 min…). Split endpoints (/briefing/cards fast + /briefing/synthesis LLM-bound) for progressive rendering. Tokens and EUR cost of each LLM call surfaced in the UI next to the timestamp and tracked in user usage statistics via track_proactive_tokens (cached tokens correctly subtracted).

changelog.title: Version History
changelog.description: LIA functional updates version by version

v1_25_18.title: v1.25.18 — 🎯 LIA says only what it checked

items.i1: 🎯 No more approximate details — when an exchange calls no tool, LIA now anchors on the data actually retrieved moments earlier instead of rephrasing from memory. It announced an appointment at “4pm” when the calendar had returned 11:15am: fixed.
items.i2: 🙋 A plain “I don’t know” instead of a guess — if a piece of information was never retrieved, LIA says so plainly rather than filling the gap with a plausible value.
items.i3: 🕐 Weather in your local time — three-hour forecast slots were shown in UTC; they now follow your own timezone.
items.i4: 🌍 Weather in your language — weather summaries were written in French whatever your language. They are now translated across the 6 languages.
items.i5: 📅 Out-of-range forecast: a clear answer — asking for weather too far ahead used to return a silent approximation. LIA now tells you how far the forecast actually reaches.
items.i6: 📍 Two appointments, two forecasts — when several items were enriched on the same day at the same place, one of them silently lost its data. Each now keeps its own.
items.i7: 🗺️ No more weather for a town that does not exist — a parameter left empty became the word “null”, and LIA looked for a place by that name. It now falls back to your own location.
items.i8: ❤️ Your health signals stop vanishing — nearly one proactive notification in two was prepared without your activity data. The read is 50× lighter, and any drop is now traced.

v1_25_17.title: v1.25.17 — 🔐 Your account grows a spine

items.i1: 🔑 Passkeys — sign in with Face ID, your fingerprint or your device code. Phishing-resistant, nothing to remember (Settings > Security).
items.i2: 📱 Authenticator app (TOTP) — add a 6-digit second step to password sign-in, with 10 single-use backup codes shown exactly once.
items.i3: 🛡️ Identity confirmation — sensitive actions (managing passkeys, exporting your data, signing out other devices) ask you to re-confirm who you are. Right after signing in, nothing to confirm for 5 minutes.
items.i4: 💻 My devices — see every session connected to your account (browser, system, approximate IP) and sign out one device or all the others.
items.i5: 🔔 New sign-in alerts — a push notification warns your devices when your account signs in from an unrecognized device. Can be turned off in My devices.
items.i6: 📦 Export my data — request a complete archive of your data (readable Markdown + JSON + your files); a notification tells you when it is ready to download.
items.i7: 📴 Offline mode — LIA now shows a proper offline page and loads faster thanks to smart caching. Your data is never cached on disk.
items.i8: 🎨 Reorganized Security settings — Strong authentication, My devices and Export my data are now three clean collapsible sections.

items.i1: 💬 Smarter input box — your draft survives a refresh or navigation, and ↑/↓ walk through your last 10 sent messages to re-edit them (like a terminal).
items.i2: 📌 Protected reading — while you scroll up to re-read, a streaming answer no longer drags you to the bottom. A floating button with a counter brings you back when YOU decide.
items.i3: 🔁 Follow-up suggestions — up to 3 tappable chips under the latest answer propose your likely next request; tapping fills the input, never sends.
items.i4: ⚡ Slash commands — type « / » in the chat: resume, briefing, agenda, search, plus everyday shortcuts (unread emails, weather, weekend weather, tasks, reminders, news) and your dialogue skills.
items.i5: 🧩 Your dashboard, your rules — hide or reorder the 9 briefing cards in Settings (a hidden card is not even fetched anymore); a starter checklist reveals what your instance can do; open commitments get their own consult/close section.
items.i6: 📲 LIA installs like an app — add it to your home screen (Android, iOS, desktop), share text or links straight into a chat draft, and use the new action row under every answer (copy, feedback, execution details).
items.i7: 🛍️ Skills gallery — browse skills as cards with previews and declared output channels, and install a skill directly from an https URL (server-validated, same strict pipeline as file import). Admins: the Telephony connector now appears in the connectors administration.
items.i8: 🌍 Your language everywhere — the assistant's journal and your compiled portrait are now always written in your configured language.

v1_25_15.title: v1.25.15 — 📱 A showcase that fits your phone

items.i1: 📱 The landing page finally looks right on phones — no more clipped text or buttons, and the layout no longer shifts during the demo animation. An automated test now replays the whole animation cycle on every release so it never comes back.
items.i2: ❓ Public FAQ redesigned — instant search, section navigation, and 51 questions instead of 13 (connectors, phone calls, voice mode, image generation, privacy). The “What can I ask LIA?” answer is reorganized into 12 expandable domains — same content, finally readable.
items.i3: 🎬 The demo animation has its own page — /demo, free of menus and distractions, ready to share on social networks in all 6 languages.
items.i4: ♿ Accessibility verified — the public pages pass the accessibility audit (contrast included), in light and dark themes.

v1_25_14.title: v1.25.14 — 🧠 Foundations for more natural moods

items.i1: 🧠 The mood engine, measured for real — a deep audit showed why the assistant's soft moods (tender, melancholic, content…) almost never appeared: its resting point was structurally locked on the assertive side. Two new settings prepare the fix (recentering + removing an artificial « joy » boost) — nothing changes by default: your admin activates them only after measuring.
items.i2: 📏 A measurement instrument for admins — a new read-only script replays the mood-quality battery against real usage (moods visited, variety, dominant emotions): activation decisions now rest on numbers, comparable before/after.
items.i3: 🛡️ Anti-regression guards — the desired mood properties are now enforced by automated tests (frozen resting points, a reachability oracle): a future change can no longer silently re-lock the palette.

v1_25_13.title: v1.25.13 — 🔗 LIA connects its domains: commitments, automations, your documents

items.i1: 🔁 Open loops — your commitments, tracked — say « I must call the plumber back » and LIA quietly keeps it as an open loop: a timely reminder at the right moment (never nagging — each loop has a cooldown), and it closes itself the day you say « done ». Also visible on the dashboard. Off by default — your admin enables it.
items.i2: ⏰ Create automations from the chat — « give me an AI press review every morning » now works as a sentence: LIA shows a confirmation card (days, time, instruction), and only creates the recurring automation once you confirm. List, pause or resume them in natural language too. And when you keep asking the same thing at the same hour, LIA can offer to automate it for you.
items.i3: 📄 Your documents become active — LIA can now search your uploaded document spaces on its own and combine them with other sources: « compare the PDF quote with Paul's email » is a real request.
items.i4: 👤 Person 360° view — « prepare my call with Marie »: one pass gathers her contact card, your recent emails, shared meetings and what LIA remembers about her — and says honestly which source was unavailable.
items.i5: 🗂️ Three new briefing cards (nine in total) — « For you » (your open loops + what your automations did, with the exact time of the next run), « Tasks » (overdue first, in red — a task due today is never counted late), « Documents » (latest modified Drive files: summarize in one click, or open in Drive).
items.i6: 🚗 Departure alert — « leave by 13:30 — 30 min drive »: for your next located meeting, LIA checks real traffic and tells you when to leave, weather included. Off by default.
items.i7: 🎂 Birthdays & 📞 call follow-up — LIA now warns you the very day (« Want me to draft a message, or call? ») and after a call placed on your behalf, it proposes to add the agreed appointment to your calendar.
items.i8: 🧭 Small touches — the chat search now sits on the left of the header (with the offline pill beside it); interest discoveries can be anchored to your city (« exhibition in Lyon this weekend », off by default).

v1_25_11.title: v1.25.11 — 🗺️ Widgets you can rely on: everywhere, durable, honest when they fail

items.i1: 🗺️ The interactive map now works on iPhone — external widgets (like the map) were blocked by a security header only Chrome-based browsers could bypass. Every browser now displays them; on iOS the hands-free wake word gives way to push-to-talk.
items.i2: 📍 "Show me where I am" uses your real position — the assistant used to improvise (it could answer with a map of France). It now receives your geolocation when you share it, and the permission prompt appears the moment your message needs it.
items.i3: 💾 Widgets survive a reload — maps, games and diagrams reopen with the conversation, on any of your devices, instead of turning into grey "unavailable" boxes.
items.i4: 👻 No more duplicate or ghost widgets — a widget could appear twice, or an old one resurface under a new answer. Widgets are now placed by the application itself, never rewritten by the AI.
items.i5: 🩺 A widget that fails tells you why — instead of an endless blank square: an explanation, a Retry button, a link that opens the content in a new tab, and the technical detail to report.
items.i6: ✏️ Drawing requests go straight to the right tool — asking for a diagram could produce a map or an improvised file. These requests now reach the drawing app (Excalidraw) directly.
items.i7: 🔒 Security wave — 16 code-scanning alerts and 7 dependency advisories fixed at the source, and the dependency audit now blocks the pipeline instead of warning silently.

v1_25_10.title: v1.25.10 — 🔔 Readable notifications, and a conversation that opens in the right place

items.i1: 🔔 Your notifications no longer show code — a scheduled-action result could land on your lock screen as <div class="lia-response"><h2>… The text is now flattened before it is sent, on the push notification as well as the in-app toast.
items.i2: 🔁 The notification says what the conversation says — the text pushed to your phone was built before the final formatting, so it could differ from the message you opened seconds later in the chat. Both now come from the same source.
items.i3: 🗣️ The voice reads exactly what is written — two defects made it drift: it spoke the icon identifiers of data cards ("event", "mail") before the sentence, and it could swallow fragments of text containing comparisons such as "x<a and b>c". Both are fixed.
items.i4: ⬇️ A long conversation opens at your last message — history used to open midway, forcing you to scroll down to reach the end. Positioning is now immediate, however long the conversation.
items.i5: 🌏 Chinese interface: scheduled-action titles are translated — they were displayed in English while the rest of the interface was localised.

v1_25_9.title: v1.25.9 — 🧪 The interface gets tested, and real bugs surface

items.i1: 🖼️ The image viewer becomes usable at the keyboard — opening a picture full screen now moves focus into the viewer, keeps the Tab key inside it, and hands focus back to the thumbnail you came from when you close. Screen readers announce it as a dialog named after the image. Before, a keyboard user was dropped at the top of the page and had to tab all the way back.
items.i2: 🔌 Your connector preferences stop being silently reverted — a preference you had just changed could be overwritten moments later by a background load that had started before your click, and the same setting could be requested twice. Both are fixed: what you choose now wins.
items.i3: 🔗 Connect all no longer skips a connector — when the authorization sequence resumed after a redirect while you had just started another one, the two queues overwrote each other and a connector could quietly drop out of the run. They can no longer overlap.
items.i4: 🧪 For admins — the interface is now genuinely tested — frontend coverage nearly doubled on functions (29 % → 55 %), with 40 new test suites over uploads, chat streaming, notifications, connectors, voice and push notifications. That work is exactly what surfaced the three fixes above: they were found by testing the real code instead of mocks.
items.i5: 📜 Seven versions reappear in this history — v1.15 and v1.20.17 through v1.20.22 had been written and translated, but were never added to the list this page renders: their entries existed and simply never displayed. A test now fails if any version is written without being wired, in either direction.

v1_25_8.title: v1.25.8 — 🎯 Proactive notifications get varied and concrete

items.i1: 🔄 Topics finally rotate — proactive notifications used to circle back to the same interest almost every evening. They now draw from a varied sample (one interest per theme, least recently covered first), and a theme served by either notification flow steps aside for a while. One passion no longer monopolizes your feed.
items.i2: 🔗 Concrete suggestions, with sources — when a notification builds on one of your interests, LIA now looks up real, fresh facts and names them (a film, an announcement, an event) with clickable source links, instead of a vague "have a look at a recent release".
items.i3: 🧠 Anti-repetition that actually reads what was said — LIA re-reads the content of its last 10 notifications (7 days) and never proposes the same topic, activity or product again, even when it comes from a different source (an interest, a memory, a journal entry).
items.i4: ⚙️ For admins — five new .env knobs (sample size, anti-repetition window, enrichment toggle and timeout), a new Prometheus metric tracking enrichment outcomes, Brave-sourced notifications no longer mislabelled as "custom" in the audit trail, and the Telegram shutdown no longer logs a spurious error on every restart.

v1_25_7.title: v1.25.7 — 🎛️ The agentic core becomes visible and controllable

items.i1: 🎛️ One-tap approval — when LIA is about to act for you (send an email, confirm a deletion…), a card appears with Confirm / Cancel buttons — and Modify for drafts. You can still reply by text or voice, exactly as before.
items.i2: 🔎 The backstage of every answer — under each message, a collapsed “⚙ N steps · X s” line shows what LIA actually did (routing, tools, reasoning), expandable in one click. The transparency of costs now extends to the flow of actions.
items.i3: 🔌 Reconnect in one click — if a connected service (Gmail, Calendar…) has expired, LIA tells you plainly in the chat with a Reconnect button that takes you straight to the right setting, instead of a vague apology.
items.i4: 🚀 Onboarding that takes action — the tutorial now lets you connect your services in one click, and each example command prefills the chat so you can try it right away.
items.i5: ✨ Experience fixes — cancelling a clarification no longer loops forever, the approval card disappears once the action is handled, and the tutorial no longer re-opens on every navigation.

items.i1: 🎯 Variety-first notifications — your interests are now grouped into subjects (several AI tools = one subject) and selection rotates them: recently covered subjects rest, rarely served ones get priority. One passion no longer monopolizes your notifications (measured: the dominant theme drops from ~50% to ~33% of notifications).
items.i2: 🔗 Clickable source links — every interest notification now ends with links to the original articles (Perplexity, Brave, Wikipedia), so you can read further with one tap. Push and Telegram get a readable text version.
items.i3: 🧹 Duplicate interests self-heal — case variants and near-identical topics ("Anthropic" vs "anthropic") are now merged automatically every night, keeping your interest list clean and your notification history intact.
items.i4: 🇨🇳 Chinese notification titles fixed — proactive notification titles were silently falling back to English for Chinese users; they now display correctly in 中文.
items.i5: ⚙️ For admins — the whole selection is tunable via .env (mode, subject cooldown, rarity exponents, source-link cap) with an instant uniform-draw fallback, and 4 new Prometheus metrics track selections, re-clustering and merges.

v1_25_5.title: v1.25.5 — 📞 The phone assistant becomes trustworthy

items.i1: 🎙️ Natural calls end to end — the assistant greets the instant the line opens (no more seconds of silence), knows today's date ("tomorrow" resolves to the right weekday, spoken out loud), speaks with a crisp voice over the telephony-native audio format, and hangs up by itself once the goal is met.
items.i2: 🛡️ A strict mandate: never an unplanned expense — if the person offers an extra, an option or any commitment beyond your request (even a 3€ cheese topping), the assistant notes the offer and its price, says it cannot confirm by itself and that someone will call back. You decide — never the assistant.
items.i3: 📋 Complete, reliable call reports — the call summary always states every cost mentioned with its amount, flags anything left open and asks how you want to proceed; dates are always absolute ("Saturday July 18", never a "tomorrow" that goes stale).
items.i4: 📅 Faithful call follow-ups — "create the appointment" after a call now reuses exactly the date, time, place and title agreed on the phone. If an action plan still looks wrong after checks, LIA asks you instead of executing something false — and it will never invent an email address for an invitation.
items.i5: ⚙️ A self-healing connector — configuration fits one screen, settings changes apply automatically on the next call (no more disconnect/reconnect), a call wrongly stuck "in progress" frees itself, and call history survives disconnection.
items.i6: 🔧 For admins: 6 new telephony settings — the voice agent's language model (pinned to a model without "thinking aloud"), TTS model and voice, audio format, country dial code, guard grace window. The "Telephony Agent" LLM type (56th) is tunable from the admin panel.

v1_25_4.title: v1.25.4 — 📊 Complete supervision: 25 dashboards, zero blind spots

items.i1: 📈 Three new Grafana dashboards — journals and the user portrait, telephony (calls, durations, automatic recoveries) and the morning briefing each get a dedicated dashboard. Admins can finally watch these features live — they were running with no visibility at all.
items.i2: 🔭 No more invisible metrics — 100% of the app's 419 metrics are now covered by at least one panel (76 were orphaned). New dedicated sections: step-by-step response latency, the semantic guard, background runs, AI-cache savings, tool-registry health.
items.i3: 👁️ Panels you can finally read — when nothing happened, incident counters now show 0 instead of an ambiguous “No data” (you couldn't tell “all good” from “broken panel” before); every panel now carries an explanatory description, and views stay populated even across 7 days of history.
items.i4: 🔧 A performance measurement repaired — conversation load time was never actually measured (the probe listened on a path the engine never takes). The metric is now wired to the right entry point, with a test locking the fix in place.

v1_25_3.title: v1.25.3 — 🧠 Sharper confirmations, leaner AI costs

items.i1: ✅ Confirmations that understand you better — when LIA asks you to confirm an action, your reply ("yes", "no, cancel", "send it to Marie instead") is now classified with its full set of examples restored — a long-standing silent bug kept them from ever reaching the AI. Edits and cancellations are recognized more reliably.
items.i2: 🎭 Confirmation questions in your assistant's voice — approval questions now follow the personality you chose (gentle, professional, playful…) instead of a fixed sarcastic register.
items.i3: 💰 Cheaper, faster AI calls — the fixed part of every internal instruction is now structured so providers can cache it: fewer billed tokens and lower latency on repeated requests, whatever model each function uses.

v1_25_2.title: v1.25.2 — 🎬 The public landing page, reinvented

items.i1: 🎬 A demo that shows the real product — the home animation becomes a faithful miniature of the app: four real scenes (orchestration with your approval, a weather×calendar initiative carried through, a genuine phone call, a mini-app built in chat), and while LIA "thinks", a glass pane reveals the orchestration backstage with the live cost counter.
items.i2: 📖 A five-chapter story, zero information lost — the page now tells what makes LIA different ("LIA gets it done." · "Nothing leaves without you."…), each chapter opened by one of LIA’s own chat bubbles; every detailed feature card remains available in expandable catalogs, protected by an automatic zero-loss guard.
items.i3: 🔍 Transparency, front and center — a "LIA has nothing to hide" section (cost to the cent, public 8.3/10 audit, open source) and "A day with LIA": four tabbed sample days (freelancer, family, developer, administrator) to picture yourself in.

items.i1: 🔒 Your sensitive links stay private — verification and password-reset links, and the tokens they carry, are never written to the logs anymore. A central filter redacts credentials everywhere and fingerprints sign-in tokens, so activity can still be traced without ever exposing a secret.
items.i2: 🛡️ A trusted way to report a security issue — LIA now publishes a standard security.txt file and an updated security policy that routes vulnerability reports privately through GitHub Security Advisories.
items.i3: 🔐 Stronger transport and secrets — the site now enforces HTTPS strict transport (HSTS), and production secret files are locked down to owner-only access during deployment.

v1_25_0.title: v1.25.0 — 🛡️ Audit V11: revised framework, cleaner than ever

items.i1: 🛡️ The technical audit was fully revised — 24 normalized areas aligned with industry referentials (ISO/IEC 25010), every score backed by executed evidence: 8.3/10 with zero major and zero minor findings. The full report — method, scope and open worksites included — is public on GitHub.
items.i2: ♿ Accessibility proven on the real product — the automated accessibility journeys (dark mode, keyboard, 320 px mobile, 200% zoom) now run against a production build and pass 17/17. A reported dark-mode contrast defect turned out to be a test-harness artifact — the palette is clean.
items.i3: 🧪 A test campaign with zero blind spots — every previously skipped backend test was reactivated or realigned to current contracts: the integration suite now passes 579/579 with zero skipped tests, on Windows and Linux alike. More proof, fewer surprises.

v1_24_0.title: v1.24.0 — 📞 LIA calls on your behalf

items.i1: 📞 LIA can place a call for you — ask LIA to phone a contact ("call Marie and ask if she's free Tuesday"). It holds the conversation on your behalf, then reports back in the chat with a summary and, when it makes sense, a one-click follow-up.
items.i2: ✅ You stay in control — LIA always shows you who it will call and why, and waits for your confirmation before dialing. The summary comes back on its own, without blocking your conversation.
items.i3: 🔒 Private by design — during the call LIA can only share your free/busy availability, never your meeting titles, guests or locations. Calls are never recorded and the full conversation is never kept — only a short summary that expires.
items.i4: 🔌 Bring your own line — telephony is a per-user connector in Preferences → My Connectors: connect your own ElevenLabs number and key. Calls are billed on your own accounts.

items.i1: 🧸 A companion that follows you — a LIA mini-avatar now floats on the dashboard pages (except chat, where the full avatar already lives). It shows the current mood, starts "thinking" when LIA works in the background, and carries a badge when notifications are waiting. A click opens chat; you can minimize it to a small dot.
items.i2: 🌅 A greeting that follows the hour — on an empty conversation, LIA welcomes you with ☕ in the morning, 👋 during the day, 🌛 in the evening, and 😴 at night (while it tidies its memories).
items.i3: 🔔 Notifications you can feel — when a proactive notification arrives, LIA's avatar gives a little attention wobble at the very moment it appears.
items.i4: ✨ Visible freshness on the dashboard — after refreshing a card, a discreet "updated ✨" confirms the data was just refreshed.

v1_23_12.title: v1.23.12 — ✨ Wow effects: the psyche takes shape

items.i1: ✨ Rare emotion particles — when a strong emotion takes hold of LIA (joy, tenderness, wonder, gratitude…), a few particles escape her avatar, once. It is rare — by design.
items.i2: 🎬 Gentle answer start — the working steps now fade into the first words of the reply instead of being abruptly replaced; and the dashboard weather card animates with the real sky (rain drops, snowflakes, sun halo).
items.i3: 🖼️ Product-level landing demo — the animated conversation on the presentation page now shows the real living steps and the writing caret, just like the app.

items.i1: 🧱 Internal architecture overhaul — the authentication domain now focuses purely on identity and sessions, while your profile and account lifecycle live together in one place. Nothing changes in how LIA looks or behaves: same features, same data, stronger foundations for what comes next.

🎭 Living mood avatar — on the current reply, LIA's mood emoji is a real animated face; older messages keep their mood snapshot, which wakes up on hover. The colored ring pulses when LIA's mood shifts, and relationship milestones (Exploratory, Affective, Stable) are celebrated with a one-time notification.
items.i2: 🎪 Animated personalities — the active personality's emoji lives in the header, and each personality animates on hover in the selection menu.
items.i3: ⚙️ Living progress — while LIA works, past steps dim and the current one breathes; a caret blinks while the answer is being written; the waiting animation changes shape with every reply; the send button takes off; an animated 👋 welcomes you on an empty conversation.
items.i4: 🗂️ Living tab — if you switch to another tab while LIA works, the tab title alternates with “✦ LIA is writing…” until the reply is done.
items.i5: ♿ Your preferences respected — all these animations turn off with your system's “reduce motion” setting (animated files are then not even downloaded) and follow the psyche display setting.

items.i1: 🌍 Confirmation previews fixed in all 6 languages — three display defects in the confirmation cards are fixed: deleting a subject-less email showed the French '(sans objet)' whatever your language (now localized in each of the 6 languages); forwarding an email without an added message displayed the literal text 'None'; deleting an empty reminder showed a blank card (now a '?' consistent with the other deletions).
items.i2: 🛡️ Card rendering consolidated (admin) — the internal machinery building these previews was reorganized into a dedicated component, locked by a test net that pins the display character-for-character (61 cases, 16 draft types, 6 languages), and the application now refuses to start if a draft type has no registered renderer. No action required: no new environment variable, no migration.

items.i1: ✅ Clearer error for inconsistent proactive-notification settings — setting a daily minimum higher than the daily maximum in the heartbeat settings used to fail with a generic 'internal error'. It now returns a clear validation message, displayed in your language.
items.i2: 🛡️ Sturdier, fully supervised API errors (admin) — every backend error now goes through LIA's central error mechanism: uniform responses, automatic structured logs and Prometheus metrics on each error path, with the API contract proven unchanged by a dedicated test net. A CI guard prevents regressions. No action required: no new environment variable, no migration.

items.i1: 🚀 Startup sequence reorganized — the internal machinery that initializes LIA at boot (caches, agents, integrations, scheduled jobs, graceful shutdown) has been reorganized into dedicated modules, with the — critical — boot order now documented in black and white. Nothing changes in daily use: the boot was verified strictly identical, event by event, before/after. Future startup evolutions are much safer.
items.i2: 🛠️ No action required (admin) — no new environment variable, no migration; the technical guides (background jobs, MCP, caches) now point to the new locations of the initialization code.

items.i1: 🎙️ Voice engine consolidated — the internal machinery that speaks LIA's answers (progressive speech, voice-over after actions, cost attribution) has been reorganized into a dedicated, independently tested component. Nothing changes in what you see or hear — but every chat and voice event sequence is now locked by an automated safety net, making future voice evolutions much safer.
items.i2: 🛡️ Quality guards & self-hosting (admin) — the codebase now refuses oversized source files (they can only shrink) and blocks private infrastructure values before they are ever committed; the daily log-digest e-mail (Logwatch) is now configured through environment variables instead of a hand-edited config file.

items.i1: 🔒 Safer maintenance operations (admin) — the production reindexing script no longer asks the administrator to copy a session cookie into a terminal command; the operation now runs entirely inside the server. Your admin credentials no longer end up in the command history.

v1_23_4.title: v1.23.4 — 🛡️ Cost guardrails for image generation

items.i1: 🖼️ Image generation protected — a technical rate limit (default: 10 images per 5 minutes per user) now blocks runaway loops before any cost is incurred. Normal use is unaffected; if the limit is reached, LIA tells you how long to wait.
items.i2: 🖥️ Remote server assistant capped (admin) — the DevOps tool is now limited to 5 tasks per 10 minutes per administrator: each task is a paid Claude run plus real actions on a server.
items.i3: 📊 Full monitoring (admin) — image generation now reports in the standard tool dashboards (usage, duration, blocked calls), and all four thresholds are tunable via environment variables without rebuilding.

v1_23_3.title: v1.23.3 — ⚡ Faster, and your data finally connects

items.i1: ⚡ Faster responses — LIA starts answering about 1 second earlier on every request: its internal preparation steps now run in parallel.
items.i2: 🗺️ "How do I get to my brother's?" is now reliable — LIA now systematically fetches the address from your contacts before computing the route. No more routes to a random location because a person's name was mistaken for an address.
items.i3: 🛡️ A guardrail before every action — if a plan tries to use a person's name where an address or an email is expected (route, invitation, sending mail), LIA catches it before acting and fetches the real information from your contacts first.
items.i4: 🔗 New natural chains — "email the attendees of this meeting", "reply to the sender", "what's the weather at my destination?", "add this restaurant's address to this contact": data from your tools (calendar, email, places, routes) now connects across domains.
items.i5: 🔌 Sturdier background generation — if the server restarts mid-response, the conversation now shows a clear message within a minute instead of waiting forever, and internal stream cleanup is guaranteed even after a hard crash.

v1_23_2.title: v1.23.2 — 🚨 LIA now watches over itself

items.i1: In case of an incident (application down, database or Redis unavailable, disk almost full, failed backup, public access cut off…), the administrator now receives an immediate email alert — no more waiting for the daily log digest to find out.
items.i2: 13 vital health checks run continuously, including an end-to-end probe of the public URL and a daily-backup watchdog: if last night's database backup failed, you know within minutes.
items.i3: Every alert email links to its step-by-step resolution guide (runbook), and a follow-up email confirms when the incident is resolved.

items.i1: The technical audit score moves to 8.4/10 across 24 areas — and the full report is now published on GitHub: scorecard, method, remediation loop and open worksites included, with the commands to reproduce the measurements yourself.
items.i2: The "360° technical audit" tile on the landing page now opens the full report directly.
items.i3: Every audit figure displayed in the app (landing page, FAQ, Story page) has been refreshed, in all 6 languages.

items.i1: 🧩 Created skills are installed instantly — Ask LIA to create a skill and it now lands directly in My Skills, active and ready to use: no more copying code blocks, rebuilding folders or uploading a zip. LIA announces the skill by its name once it's available.
items.i2: 💬 Guided creation remembers your answers — The Skill Generator's step-by-step dialogue (need analysis, archetype choice, generation) now keeps its context across turns: it no longer re-asks questions you already answered.
items.i3: 🔁 Iterate on your skills safely — Ask for a change and the skill is updated in place (even at your skill quota). A failed import can never corrupt the existing version: the previous skill is restored automatically.
items.i4: 🛡️ Clear name conflicts — Built-in skill names and names used by other users are reserved: an import reusing one is cleanly refused, and when generating, LIA simply picks a close variant.
items.i5: 🔒 Hardened skill imports for everyone — Manual uploads benefit too: strict name validation (a malicious file can no longer write outside its own skill folder), zip size and file-count guards, and one validated pipeline for every import path.

v1_22_0.title: v1.22.0 — 🔄 Answers that keep going without you

items.i1: 🔄 Your answers keep generating in the background — Leaving the page, switching apps or losing the connection no longer kills an in-progress answer: LIA finishes it server-side and it's waiting in your history when you come back — with its full cost accounting.
items.i2: 📡 Live resume when you return — Come back while LIA is still writing and the in-progress bubble rebuilds itself and continues streaming live, automatically. Works across tabs too — and only one answer runs at a time per conversation.
items.i3: ⏹️ A stop button, finally — Stop an in-progress answer with one click. The partial text is kept and marked "interrupted"; actions already performed (a sent email…) are not undone, and what was consumed is billed honestly.
items.i4: 🔊 Voice only when someone is listening — When an answer finishes in the background with nobody connected, LIA no longer synthesizes its audio: lower costs, same experience when you're there.

v1_21_26.title: v1.21.26 — 🛡️ A sturdier chat & voice core

items.i1: 🎙️ Voice mode recovers from network drops — If the connection was lost while LIA transcribed your speech, the interface could stay stuck on "processing" forever. It now shows the error and goes right back to listening — and a rare background error that appeared after each wake-word recording is gone too.
items.i2: 🌍 Chat error messages in your language — Connection problems, expired sessions or usage limits used to appear with a fixed French prefix around an English message, whatever your language. These messages are now properly translated in all 6 languages.
items.i3: 🛡️ The chat engine is now regression-proof — The heart of LIA (message streaming, action approvals, voice mode) is covered by 434 automated tests with locked coverage thresholds: any regression in these critical areas is now blocked before it can reach you.

v1_21_25.title: v1.21.25 — 🩺 Health checks that tell the truth

items.i1: 🩺 A real availability signal — LIA now exposes two health probes instead of one ambiguous endpoint: /health reports that the app is running, while the new /ready confirms that everything needed to serve you — database and cache — is actually up. Monitoring and deployments can finally tell a brief hiccup from a real outage.
items.i2: 🚦 Honest diagnostics for self-hosters — The one-command health check reports correct statuses again for every service (it had been failing silently since the development stack moved to HTTPS), and the documented startup behaviour now matches what really happens at boot.
items.i3: 🧱 Fresh foundations — The Redis client, the frontend test engine and about forty interface libraries were brought up to date, with the full test suite green.

items.i1: 📅 Your next appointments, without detours — Asking for your next appointments no longer triggers the full daily briefing: LIA now clearly distinguishes a specific question from a whole-day overview, and always reads your real calendar before answering.
items.i2: 🔒 Security updates across the board — Five third-party libraries were updated to their patched versions (including the SSH client and the Claude connector library), and our automated security scanning was repaired so every change is now checked continuously.
items.i3: ⚙️ Sounder foundations — Nearly 200 silent error-handling spots in the backend were made explicit, with a permanent CI guard preventing new ones, and the web platform moved to Node.js 24 LTS — issues get diagnosed faster and fixed sooner.

items.i1: 🔁 Microsoft: clearer reconnection guidance — When your Outlook, Calendar or To Do access expires, the message now clearly tells you to reactivate the connector in Settings — exactly like Google.
items.i2: 🔒 More privacy in technical logs — GPS coordinates no longer appear in server logs during address lookups, and error responses from external services are trimmed so they never carry unnecessary content.
items.i3: 📊 Better connector monitoring — Every Google/Microsoft error (authentication, quota, outage) is now precisely classified and measured in our dashboards, so external-service incidents are detected faster — with zero change to how you use LIA.

v1_21_22.title: v1.21.22 — 🛡️ Clear error messages and hardened reliability

items.i1: 🛠️ Forms explain again what's wrong — When an input is invalid (for example a too-short password at sign-up), LIA once again shows the precise message explaining the rule to follow, instead of a generic technical error. The defect affected every form with advanced validation rules.
items.i2: ✅ 450+ integration tests now watch over every update — The whole critical chain (accounts, connectors, conversations, pricing) is now automatically re-validated against a real database on every code change, and the test-coverage requirement was raised. In practice: less regression risk with each new version.

v1_21_21.title: v1.21.21 — 🕐 The right time, in your timezone

items.i1: 🕐 Voice mode announces the correct local time — When a voice comment mentions the current time, LIA now always resolves it in your preferred timezone. Previously, in rare cases, the spoken time could be the server's clock (UTC) instead of yours.
items.i2: 🌍 Date & time correctness, guaranteed for good — Every date LIA handles (displayed dates, birthday reminders, technical timestamps) is now guaranteed timezone-aware: an automated check permanently blocks the entire "server time vs your time" bug family from ever coming back.
