items.i3: 📘 Installation guide fully rewritten (for self-hosters) — The Getting Started guide was rebuilt from scratch: production-proven default values throughout, step-by-step setup of the external platforms (Google, Microsoft, Apple…), a feature configuration reference and a final deployment checklist.

items.i1: 🔒 17 vulnerable components updated — The automated security audit now inspects every building block LIA ships with (~240, including the indirect ones that were invisible to it before). It flagged 17 components with known vulnerabilities (25+ CVEs); all were updated, and the audit now reports zero known vulnerabilities.
items.i2: 📦 Every installation ships exactly what was tested — LIA's builds are now reproducible: each version locks the exact list of its components, verified by cryptographic fingerprint at installation. Two installations of the same version are guaranteed identical — no more invisible drift between them.
items.i3: 🛡️ For self-hosters — The software inventory (SBOM) published with each release now lists the exact versions actually shipped, transitive dependencies included. Updating a dependency is one command (task deps:lock), and the CI refuses any change that skips the lockfile.

items.i1: 🧹 A leaner, safer engine — Around 13,600 lines of inactive code (old mechanisms that were never used) were removed after exhaustive verification, and the admin dashboards were cleared of their empty panels. LIA becomes simpler to maintain and evolve, with no visible change.
items.i2: 🌐 More robust web search and weather — The connections to Brave, weather and Perplexity now share a hardened common foundation: smart retries on transient errors, a circuit breaker that stops insisting when an external service is down, fairer request pacing, and a fix for a connection leak that could build up over time.

items.i1: 🛠️ More reliable under the hood, with no visible change — The core that writes LIA's answers has been fully reorganized internally, with nothing changing in what you see, so it is more reliable and easier to evolve. The reorganization is locked in by around a hundred new automated tests that guarantee strictly identical behavior.

🔒 Stronger privacy in the logs — LIA's internal application logs no longer contain any of your personal content — names of files you upload, message text, calendar or task titles, reminders. At the standard level only anonymous counters and identifiers remain, in line with data-minimization best practice.
items.i2: ⚡ A smoother app during image generation and uploads — Generating an image or importing a document into a knowledge space no longer briefly slows other actions down: these heavier operations now run in the background, so the app stays responsive for everyone.

items.i1: 🔢 Readable math & science formulas — When LIA writes a mathematical or scientific formula, it now appears as a properly typeset equation — like in a textbook — instead of raw symbols and code. This works both for formulas inside a sentence and for standalone equations.
items.i2: 💶 Cleaner currency amounts — Prices such as “9$” inside a rich answer no longer show an unwanted backslash before the amount.

v1_21_12.title: v1.21.12 — ✅ Clearer, more reliable action confirmations

items.i1: 📧 Clearer batch confirmations — When LIA prepares several actions at once (for example an email to two people), the confirmation now shows the correct action and, for emails, who each one goes to — so you can check the recipients before confirming. A batch of sends no longer shows a misleading “confirm this deletion?” prompt.
items.i2: 🛡️ Reliable confirmations in autonomous mode — Asking LIA (in autonomous mode) to delete an email or event, or to run a connected-tool action, could freeze with no confirmation appearing. LIA now always shows a proper confirmation before any such action, exactly as in the standard mode.
items.i3: ✅ A consistent confirmation experience — Confirmations now behave identically across both execution modes (standard and autonomous), and nothing is ever carried out without your explicit approval.

items.i1: 🧠 More reliable capture of your memories, journals and interests — Parsing of the assistant's internal outputs (from which it notes what it remembers about you) has been hardened: it now tolerates small formatting imperfections and silently fails far less often. As a result, what LIA should remember about you is captured more faithfully.
items.i2: ⚡ Leaner analysis of your requests — When your message carries no personal reference to resolve (such as “my wife” or “my brother”), a redundant AI analysis step is now skipped — slightly faster, leaner processing, with no change for you.
items.i3: 🛡️ Admin · bounded psyche history — LIA's emotional-evolution history (one snapshot per message) is now purged beyond a configurable retention window (90 days by default), keeping server storage growth bounded. Adjustable via configuration.

v1_21_10.title: v1.21.10 — 🎭 LIA's personality finally comes through

items.i1: 🎭 LIA's personality and mood finally show — Its tone, rhythm and word choice genuinely shift with its inner state, in every reply. LIA doesn't announce its mood — it lets you hear it. Ask it directly how it's doing and it can still tell you.
items.i2: 🌈 A richer, more changeable inner life — LIA's mood genuinely varies and evolves from one exchange to the next instead of staying stuck in a single register, and between conversations it gently drifts back toward neutral — the way a real mood settles.
items.i3: 💬 The same living LIA in its proactive messages — Reminders, voice comments and proactive nudges now carry the same evolving personality, so LIA speaks in one recognisable voice whether it answers you or reaches out first.

v1_21_9.title: v1.21.9 — 🌍 The assistant speaks your language in approval flows

items.i1: 🌍 Confirmations, edits and refusals now in your language — When LIA asks you to confirm, modify or cancel an action, its messages — and its understanding of your reply (“yes”, “no”, “rather send it to Marie”) — are now fully in your language, across all six languages. Non-French users no longer see any French in these exchanges.
items.i2: ⚡ Faster, more reliable follow-ups — References like “the restaurant of this meeting”, “directions to that address” or “show me the 2nd one” resolve directly again, without a needless extra planning step, and follow-ups on a file (“open the first one”) work reliably.
items.i3: 🛡️ Admin · cross-domain shortcut toggle — A new setting lets you enable or disable the LLM-free shortcut for cross-domain references (“the restaurant of this meeting”) in production without a redeploy.

items.i1: 🗓️ Searching your appointments by topic works reliably — Asking for “my medical appointments”, or for an event by a fuzzy or accented name (“hôtel particulier”), could return nothing. The assistant now lists your events over the period and filters the topic when answering, instead of relying on an unreliable calendar text search. Searching by person (attendee) stays direct.
items.i2: 🗓️ “My next appointments” no longer misses events — For an open request with no explicit date (“my next medical appointments”, “my next 3 appointments”), the assistant could wrongly narrow the search to too short a window. It now uses the right period, while still honouring your explicit dates (“on August 15”, “next week”).
items.i3: 🛡️ Admin · result volumetry enforced everywhere — The global ceiling on the number of items returned by external APIs (calendar, mail, contacts…) is now applied uniformly by every connector (Google, Apple, Microsoft), closing a bypass. Configurable.

v1_21_7.title: v1.21.7 — 🎨 Regression fixes: voice, interactive widgets & diagrams

items.i1: 🎤 Voice input (push-to-talk) works again — A security tightening in v1.21.5 accidentally blocked voice capture, so holding the send button showed 'an error occurred during voice input'. Push-to-talk is fully restored.
items.i2: 🗺️ Interactive maps & 🎨 diagram widgets display again — The same tightening had stopped the interactive-map skill and third-party widgets (such as Excalidraw diagrams) from rendering. They work again, now running inside a dedicated secure sandbox that keeps the rest of the app strictly protected.
items.i3: 🎨 Complex diagrams no longer time out — Asking LIA to draw a detailed diagram could be cut off after two minutes, right before it finished. Diagram generation is now given the time it needs.
items.i4: 🤖 No more off-topic answers when something fails — When a requested action failed, LIA could reply with an unrelated result (for example a map for a diagram request). It now tells you honestly that the action did not succeed instead of masking it.
items.i5: ✅ The assistant checks its plan again — An internal safeguard that verifies the assistant's plan really matches your request had silently stopped working. It is fixed and made more robust across the whole assistant.

v1_21_6.title: v1.21.6 — 🔒 Privacy, reliability & sandbox hardening (audit wave 4)

items.i1: 🔒 Complete erasure when you delete your account — Deleting your account now also permanently erases your health data (heart rate, steps) and your last known location, and any device that was sending health data to LIA can no longer do so afterward. Full alignment with your right to erasure (GDPR).
items.i2: 🤖 More reliable assistant agents — Fixed a problem that could make the specialized agents (calendar, email, contacts…) fail repeatedly on a request. They also always use the correct current date and time, even after the app has been running for a long time.
items.i3: 🔔 More complete proactive suggestions — Under heavy load, proactive notifications could silently miss part of your context (agenda, weather, tasks, interests…). Every source is now gathered reliably, so proactive messages reason on the full picture.
items.i4: 🛡️ Stronger isolation between simultaneous users — Closed a rare timing situation where, with many people using LIA at once, one person's private context (such as a personal journal excerpt) could momentarily influence another person's request. Your data stays strictly your own.
items.i5: 🧩 Admin · hardened skill sandbox — Scripts bundled with skills now run with reduced privileges and strict resource limits (CPU, memory, processes, file size), and can no longer reach the server's Docker socket. A runaway or malicious script is contained; the admin DevOps assistant is unaffected.

items.i1: ⚡ A smoother, more responsive app — Heavy background operations (push notifications, image generation) no longer briefly freeze the interface, and email search returns results faster. Under the hood, blocking work was moved off the main thread and several sequential lookups now run in parallel.
items.i2: 🗓️ Correct date formats in every language — A regional-format bug caused dates to use an invalid locale for some languages (notably English and Chinese). Dates now display in the proper format for your language.
items.i3: 🛡️ Reinforced security — The personalized greeting on your dashboard can no longer run injected content coming from external data (for example a booby-trapped event title), and a strict browser security policy (Content-Security-Policy) was added as an extra layer against script injection.
items.i4: 🔒 Admin · internal services isolated from the network — In production, internal services (database, monitoring dashboards, metrics) are no longer reachable from the local network: only the web application is exposed, behind the secure tunnel. The firewall's interaction with Docker is now documented.
items.i5: 🌍 Admin · instant broadcasts & configurable translator — Translated broadcast announcements are now stored, so re-reading one costs nothing (previously re-translated on every view). The personality translator also appears in the admin LLM Configuration and honors your model overrides.

v1_21_4.title: v1.21.4 — 🛡️ Reliability & privacy: systemic hardening (audit wave 2)

items.i1: 📊 Accurate usage statistics at the cycle rollover — At each new billing cycle, some of your dashboard counters (voice, images, requests) could keep part of the previous cycle's values depending on which event crossed the boundary (a message, a voice dictation, or simply opening the dashboard). All counters are now reset together: the usage and cost figures shown are reliable from the first day of the cycle.
items.i2: 🔒 Stronger privacy — no personal data in technical logs — Operational logs could contain personal information (home address and GPS coordinates, contact names and emails, email recipients and subjects, memory excerpts). This content is now removed (only technical counters and identifiers remain), with a safety net that automatically masks it even if a future oversight occurs. Compliant with data minimization (GDPR).
items.i3: 🇨🇳 Chinese labels for Chinese-speaking users — Two areas of the app (contact field types, data summaries) showed French instead of Chinese for accounts set to Simplified Chinese. They now display correctly in Chinese.
items.i4: 🌍 Fallback message in your language — When the assistant exceptionally cannot produce a reply, the short fallback message shown was always in French (without accents). It now appears in your language (6 languages).
items.i5: 🛡️ Admin · tool and connector robustness — A failing tool module can no longer vanish silently from the catalogue: the anomaly is now detected (a visible failure in continuous integration, a dedicated counter in production) rather than swallowed. In addition, the API-key "last used" timestamp and the error diagnostics of OAuth connectors are now correctly persisted to the database.

v1_21_3.title: v1.21.3 — 🛠️ Reliability: audit fixes (calendars, tasks, labels, security)

items.i1: 🗓️ Connected services made reliable — Several fixes to your connected services: events created or edited in Apple Calendar now honor the requested timezone (a "10:00 in Paris" event is no longer saved at 10:00 UTC); Microsoft Calendar event search works with an apostrophe ("l'anniversaire" no longer breaks the query); and the Google Tasks "list my task lists" command, which failed on every call, works again.
items.i2: 🗺️ Correct route maps — An encoding bug distorted the geometry of multi-segment routes: route maps now render correctly.
items.i3: 🏷️ Ambiguous Gmail labels: it asks you — When a label you wanted to delete or apply matched several candidates, the assistant showed a generic error instead of asking which one. It now asks the disambiguation question.
items.i4: ⏹️ Stop really stops — Closing the conversation during an in-progress autonomous exploration (ReAct mode) now actually interrupts the work — previously the stop was swallowed and the loop kept going.
items.i5: 🌍 Connector messages in your language — "Service not activated" / "no service configured" connector messages now appear in your language (6 languages) instead of always in French.
items.i6: 🛡️ Admin · security and settings — Searching users by email is now restricted to administrators (it was reachable by any signed-in account — an account-enumeration risk); the planner budget and step count set in configuration are finally honored (one code path always served fixed values); and two internal settings (metrics sync interval, iterative MCP step timeout) become configurable.

v1_21_2.title: v1.21.2 — 🔒 Hardened security: sanitized rendering and real IP addresses

items.i1: 🔒 Protection against malicious content (XSS) — The assistant's answers can relay content from elsewhere (an email body, a fetched web page, a tool result). That content is now sanitized before display: no embedded code can execute in your session anymore. All legitimate rendering (cards, action buttons, tables, interactive mini-apps) stays identical.
items.i2: 🧮 Math formulas finally reliable — Formulas now display correctly however the assistant writes them (inline, block, LaTeX code block…), dollar amounts (9$, 1.50$) are never swallowed by math rendering anymore, and a bug that froze the whole conversation after a formula or an interactive app (endless "Generating response…") is fixed.
items.i3: 🛡️ Admin · Real IP addresses and locked-down access — The production API is no longer reachable directly from the local network: Cloudflare is the single entry point. Per-IP rate limits now really apply per visitor (previously all clients shared the same internal IP — one aggressive client could block everyone), and both the logs and the Grafana geo map finally show real public IP addresses.
items.i4: ⚡ Leaner request processing — The internal layers every request passes through were rewritten in a lighter form: less work per request and per streamed response chunk, benefiting smoothness, especially on modest hardware.
items.i5: 🧰 Old conversations upgraded automatically — Conversations created with older versions are now silently migrated to the latest internal format when loaded. Nothing to do on your side; resuming old threads after updates becomes more reliable.

v1_21_1.title: v1.21.1 — ✅ Trustworthy draft editing: what you approve is exactly what goes out

items.i1: ✅ What you approve is exactly what gets sent — When reviewing a draft (email, event…) before sending, your successive edits could be silently re-generated at confirmation time: the content actually sent could differ from the last version displayed. The mechanism has been rebuilt: each edit is applied exactly once, and the confirmed content is guaranteed identical to the last content you saw. The same guarantee applies to bulk operations: the list of items you confirm is exactly the list that gets processed, and refining it with a filter ("keep only this week's") no longer reloads your data at every step.
items.i2: 💬 Each draft version in its own bubble — When you requested a change, the new version overwrote the previous bubble in the conversation, making it look like the assistant wasn't responding. Every re-presented version now appears in a new bubble, and the reloaded history matches what you saw live.
items.i3: ✍️ "Sign with my name" actually works — The assistant didn't know your first name when writing emails: it left a placeholder ("[Your name]") or invented one. It now uses the first name from your profile, both at initial drafting and during edits. Nothing else changes: no signature is added unless you ask for one.
items.i4: ❓ Clarification questions are finally displayed — When your modification instruction was ambiguous, the assistant generated a clarification question… that was never shown. It now appears alongside the re-presented draft, so you know what to specify.
items.i5: 🕐 Times and dates in your timezone — The "today" opening hours on place cards, the age shown for contact birthdays and the default period of email searches are now computed in your timezone rather than the server's — including right after midnight.
items.i6: 🛡️ Reliability & monitoring (admin) — Closing the conversation during a bulk operation now actually cancels the in-flight work; the "stop on first error" mode really stops the batch; Grafana's HTTP metrics use bounded labels (route templates instead of raw identifiers — adjust your queries if they filtered on exact paths); and production startup no longer logs harmless errors (Telegram webhook, system embeddings).

v1_21_0.title: v1.21.0 — ⚡ Faster answers and sharper proactive suggestions

items.i1: ⚡ Noticeably faster answers — Major latency campaign: rich (HTML-mode) answers start 3–4 seconds earlier, the answer's context (memory, documents, journal) is now prepared in parallel with the proactive suggestions instead of waiting its turn, long answers render more smoothly, and connections to the AI models are reused between calls. Nothing to configure: it is all automatic.
items.i2: 💡 Sharper proactive suggestions — LIA now knows explicitly which data from your request can feed which tools (a contact's address can feed a route, a places search or the weather). Its follow-up initiatives after an answer become more precise and better targeted, whatever AI model is configured.
items.i3: 🛠️ No more data from the previous turn reappearing — In autonomous (ReAct) mode, asking for example for directions right after your upcoming events could re-display those events inside the new answer. Every conversation turn now starts from a clean slate.
items.i4: 🎯 Routes to your contacts' exact address — In autonomous mode, LIA now looks up the contact's precise address in your address book before computing a route, instead of settling for an approximation (such as the city) recalled from memory.
items.i5: 🏷️ Skill badge visible for everyone — The badge showing which skill generated an answer is now displayed for all users; it was previously limited to administrator accounts with the debug panel.

v1_20_22.title: v1.20.22 — 🛡️ Scheduled actions no longer add to your memory or interests

items.i1: 🛡️ Scheduled actions no longer add unwanted memories or interests — When LIA runs one of your scheduled actions (for example a daily briefing), the instruction it runs is now treated as an automated task, not as something you typed. As a result it no longer feeds LIA's long-term memory or your interest profile (nor the assistant's private journal or its mood) — only the messages you actually send do. Your memory and interests therefore stay faithful to what you really told LIA. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_21.title: v1.20.21 — 🔒 Security hardening and accurate multi-worker metrics

items.i1: 🔒 Security hardening — dependencies updated — 43 known vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies (frontend and backend, including the framework and AI-library stack) were resolved by updating them to patched versions. There is no user-visible change and nothing to do on your side; it keeps the platform's security posture fully up to date.
items.i2: 📊 Admin · Accurate metrics across all workers — In production LIA runs on several worker processes, but the monitoring (Prometheus / Grafana) only saw one of them, so the real-time rate and latency dashboards under-counted by roughly 4× and a few harmless warnings appeared on each deployment. Metrics are now correctly aggregated across all workers, so the admin Grafana dashboards are accurate. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_20.title: v1.20.20 — 🔌 Your custom MCP servers now work in the autonomous (ReAct) mode too

items.i1: 🔌 Your custom MCP servers now work in the autonomous (⚡ ReAct) mode — Until now, the MCP servers you connect (GitHub, HuggingFace, your own services…) were only used by LIA in the standard mode; in the autonomous (⚡ ReAct) mode they were ignored and LIA fell back to a generic web search. They now work in both modes: LIA picks the most relevant tool from your MCP servers on its own, by description, without you having to ask for a specific one. For a server set to “Iterative mode”, the autonomous mode now uses its individual tools directly (it already reasons step by step), while servers with interactive widgets (e.g. Excalidraw) keep their dedicated agent. Admin: a new REACT_MCP_EXPAND_ITERATIVE_ENABLED setting (on by default) lets you revert to the previous behaviour instantly. Nothing to change on your side.
items.i2: 🔧 Fix — MCP tools with optional settings no longer fail on strict servers — Some MCP tools (e.g. GitHub repository search, which has optional “sort”/“order” settings) could fail when LIA left those settings empty, because certain servers reject an empty value with a type error. LIA now omits unset optional settings entirely, as the protocol expects, so these tools work reliably. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_19.title: v1.20.19 — 📓 A sharper, more careful personal journal for the assistant

items.i1: 📓 The assistant's personal journal is now far more careful — LIA keeps a private journal of behavioural notes about how best to help you. It was sometimes writing useless or even counter-productive notes from a single message — for instance deciding to always answer you briefly just because one of your messages happened to be short, or recording that it lacks access to your data and then refusing to even try. It now writes far more sparingly, only when a note is clearly grounded in something you actually said or did, and it never records false limitations about its own abilities. The result is steadier, better-judged behaviour over time. Nothing to change on your side.
items.i2: 🤖 Journal directives now also guide the autonomous mode — The behavioural directives LIA distills in its journal now steer its autonomous (ReAct) reasoning mode too, not only the standard mode — so it stays consistent however it tackles your request. Admin: a new JOURNAL_REACT_CONTEXT_MAX_ENTRIES setting controls how many directives are injected into that mode (default 3).

v1_20_18.title: v1.20.18 — 🎨 Rich display stays consistent for the whole conversation, plus exact usage counting

items.i1: 🎨 Rich (HTML) display stays consistent for the whole conversation — In the rich (HTML) display mode, the first replies displayed correctly, but as the conversation grew some drifted back to plain formatting without you changing any setting. This is fixed: every reply now keeps the rich HTML formatting throughout the conversation, in both execution modes. Nothing to change on your side.
items.i2: 📊 Exact token & cost counting for proactive messages (Admin · Debug Panel) — A proactive (“initiative”) message could appear twice in the Debug Panel — once correctly labelled and once as “unknown” — with the same tokens counted twice, which also inflated the per-message total, the usage logs and user statistics. Counting is now exact: each model call is recorded once. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_17.title: v1.20.17 — 💭 Watch the assistant think, and richer reasoning settings for Claude models

items.i1: 💭 See the assistant reason in real time — When a model with “reasoning” enabled is configured for an agent, its train of thought now streams live in the progress area while it works, then disappears as soon as the final answer arrives. It fills the wait with useful context and shows how the assistant approaches your request. It only appears when reasoning is actually active — nothing is shown for agents that don't reason.
items.i2: 🧠 Per-model thinking settings for Claude (Admin · Configuration LLM) — Each Claude model now exposes exactly the reasoning controls its API really supports: Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 use adaptive thinking with an effort level (off · low · medium · high · max); Opus 4.5 / Haiku 4.5 use a manual thinking budget (on/off + tokens). When thinking is on, temperature is locked automatically (the provider requires it), so you can no longer save an inconsistent configuration. Opus 4.5 also gains a separate global “effort” control.
items.i3: 🔧 Fix — Claude no longer fails when thinking is enabled — With extended thinking turned on for a Claude model, certain internal steps (such as request analysis) could fail and degrade the whole turn. This is fixed: those steps now use the only mode the provider allows with thinking, so turns complete normally. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_16.title: v1.20.16 — 🔊 Voice mode no longer reads formatting aloud during conversation

items.i1: 🔊 The voice no longer speaks formatting markup during conversation — When voice mode is on and you simply chat (without triggering a tool) with the rich (HTML) display mode, the voice sometimes read formatting elements aloud instead of the answer itself. Rich formatting is now reserved for replies that present data from tools; your conversational exchanges stay plain text, read naturally — and look identical on screen in every display mode. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_15.title: v1.20.15 — 📊 Monitoring reliability: Grafana dashboards repaired and sub-agent metrics activated

items.i1: 📊 Grafana dashboards now read correctly — Many monitoring panels that stayed stuck on No data (because of outdated metric names, labels or queries) have been repaired, and the sub-agents monitoring dashboard now fills in: the execution metrics of sub-agents (how many run, their duration, their token usage and their errors) are finally emitted. This only concerns the self-hosting / admin monitoring stack — nothing changes in the assistant you talk to.
items.i2: 🧹 Metrics cleanup — 9 obsolete or never-emitted metrics were removed (lowering cardinality and dropping a label that contained a user identifier), and a small counter leak (the number of active sub-agents) was fixed.

v1_20_14.title: v1.20.14 — 🔊 Voice mode reads a short commentary again (not the on-screen text), and 📜 the full history of long conversations becomes reachable

items.i1: 🔊 Voice mode no longer reads the displayed text out loud when tools are used — When voice mode is on and your request needs a tool (checking emails, calendar, contacts, the weather, etc.), the voice is supposed to deliver a short spoken commentary, distinct from the on-screen reply (which can be long, structured, with cards or widgets). Recently the voice was reading the displayed text verbatim instead, which was both noisier and less natural. This came from a stale signal inherited from the previous turn of the conversation, which prematurely triggered the chat-mode direct read-aloud. Fixed — the spoken commentary is back on turns that use tools.
items.i2: 📜 Long conversations: scroll back to the beginning of the discussion — In a conversation that has grown to thousands of messages, the start was unreachable from the chat — only the latest ~50 messages were loaded with no way to scroll further back (the messages were always preserved in the database, just not displayed). You can now scroll up in the chat: older messages load progressively in batches, deduplicated, and your reading position is preserved (no visible jump). A small "Loading older messages…" indicator appears at the top during each fetch. Works in any conversation; the in-chat search still filters what's currently loaded.

v1_20_13.title: v1.20.13 — 🔧 Responses no longer fail with the latest Gemini models (Gemini 3 series)

items.i1: 🔧 Fix — the latest Gemini 3.x models no longer trigger a generation error — With the most recent Gemini AI models (the Gemini 3 series, e.g. Gemini 3.5 Flash), some responses could fail with the message “A problem occurred while generating the response”, or degrade silently (occasionally unintelligible voice output, incomplete formatting). These models return their text in a different format that LIA didn't interpret everywhere. This is now fixed end to end, in both the default mode and ⚡ ReAct mode — including when you mix several AI models. Nothing to change on your side.

v1_20_12.title: v1.20.12 — 🌙 Dormant interests stay visible and manageable, and your long-term memory warns you before forgetting

items.i1: 🌙 Your dormant interests are no longer lost — When you stop mentioning a topic for a while, LIA puts the matching interest to sleep ("dormant") rather than acting on it. Until now, dormant interests simply vanished from your Settings even though they were still stored — you couldn't review, edit or remove them, and they were deleted automatically after 90 days. They now appear in a dedicated "Dormant" section, clearly marked, where you can reactivate, edit or delete them at any time. A reactivated interest starts fresh, as if newly detected. The counter now also shows the breakdown: active · dormant · blocked.
items.i2: ⚠️ Your memory now warns you before forgetting — LIA automatically forgets long-term memories that have become unimportant and unused (unless you've pinned them). Until now, nothing told you a memory was about to be forgotten. Memories close to automatic removal are now flagged in your Settings list with a "may be forgotten" warning, so you can pin the ones that matter before they disappear.

v1_20_11.title: v1.20.11 — ⚡ ReAct mode becomes proactive, a home greeting that matches your real day, and several display and accuracy fixes

items.i1: ⚡ ReAct mode is now proactive, like the default mode — In ReAct mode (the autonomous, step-by-step reasoning mode), after answering your request LIA can now run a few extra read-only checks in related areas and weave the result into its reply — for example the weather and the travel time for your next appointment, or the contact behind an email. This proactive "Initiative" already existed in the default (Pipeline) mode; both modes now offer it. It only triggers when genuinely useful, and only ever reads — it never creates or changes anything on its own.
items.i2: A home greeting that matches your real day — The one-line greeting at the top of your dashboard now reads your agenda correctly: it tells today from tomorrow, names the next appointment, and reacts to the shape of your day (a free day, a busy one, or a single thing coming up) — instead of vaguely (and sometimes wrongly) implying something was happening "today".
items.i3: Money amounts now display correctly — Amounts written with a dollar sign (e.g. "1.50$" … "9$") in the chat or in proactive notifications were sometimes mangled into a mathematical formula, with spaces removed and characters stacked. They now display as plain text everywhere.
items.i4: Admin — configurable home dashboard limits and accurate cost conversion — How much content each Today Briefing card shows (calendar, emails, birthdays, reminders, etc.) is now configurable via environment variables — the agenda now shows up to 10 upcoming events instead of 3 by default. Separately, the exchange-rate source used to convert LLM costs into euros was fixed (it had been falling back to a stored rate), so cost reporting is accurate again.

v1_20_10.title: v1.20.10 — In ReAct mode, the reply no longer exposes the assistant's internal reasoning and no longer appears twice

items.i1: Cleaner replies in ⚡ ReAct mode — In ReAct mode (the autonomous, step-by-step reasoning mode), two glitches could spoil the final reply. (1) The assistant sometimes let its internal thinking steps show through — labels like "PLAN", "OBSERVATION", "CROSS-CHECK" followed by the "final answer" — instead of showing only the answer itself. (2) The reply text briefly appeared duplicated before collapsing to a single copy. Both are fixed: LIA now delivers only the final, clean, single reply, in ReAct mode just like in the default mode. Nothing changes on your side.

v1_20_9.title: v1.20.9 — In ReAct mode, creating, modifying or deleting now asks for your confirmation before acting — no more false "Done!" with nothing actually happening

items.i1: ReAct mode now asks for confirmation before sensitive actions, just like the default mode — When you use the ⚡ ReAct mode (the autonomous, step-by-step reasoning mode) and asked LIA to create an appointment, send or reply to an email, add a contact, create a task or delete something, it would sometimes answer "Done! I've created the appointment…" while in reality nothing had been created. The action was only prepared internally and then silently dropped — the confirmation step that already exists in the default (Pipeline) mode was missing in ReAct mode. From this release both modes behave identically: a sensitive action (create / modify / reply / forward / delete an event, email, contact, task, file or label) now shows you the same confirmation card with the details, and the action is only really carried out after you confirm — you can also edit or cancel it. Reminders, which are designed to be created instantly, keep working without a confirmation step in both modes.

v1_20_8.title: v1.20.8 — Conversations no longer freeze on long history, context-usage indicator in the chat, visible recovery notice when the summary fails

items.i1: Conversations no longer get stuck when the history grows long — When your conversation accumulates many messages, LIA runs a background compaction step that summarises the older turns to free up context room. On May 16, 2026 a production user could no longer send any message: every turn re-triggered the summary, the language model answered once and then went silent for ~93 s until the connection was finally dropped at 125 s with "Erreur de connexion: network error". Root cause: no maximum delay on the LLM call, no retry on transient errors, no signal sent to the frontend during the wait. This release rebuilds end-to-end resilience: per-chunk timeout (35 s), global timeout (2 min), three attempts with progressive backoff, and — if all of that still fails — an explicit fallback that cleanly truncates the older history rather than leaving you with a silent useless summary. You'll literally see the note "The older conversation was truncated because the summary could not be generated" when that fallback fires, rather than a mute loss of information.
items.i2: Visible indicator in the chat while compaction runs — Before this release, when LIA was summarising your history you had no visual feedback: the send button froze for ~30 s without explanation. Now, the moment compaction starts, a notification (toast) appears at the top of the screen reading "Summarizing the conversation to free up context…" with a spinner; the message input is locked while the summary runs; when it's done the toast morphs into a confirmation "Conversation summarized — N tokens freed" (or a warning if the truncation fallback fired). The toast stays visible no matter where you've scrolled in the conversation.
items.i3: Context-usage pill in the chat header — A new discreet pill next to the search box continuously shows tokens used / compaction threshold as a coloured ring and a percentage. Green below 50 %, amber from 50 to 75 %, orange from 75 to 90 %, rose above 90 %. The displayed percentage is capped at 100 % to stay legible; in case of overshoot (typical right after a long answer), the hover tooltip explains "compaction will run on your next message". The pill persists across page refreshes — no need to send a message just to see it.
items.i4: Admin: new operator settings, Grafana dashboard, transactional recovery script — Five new .env settings drive compaction without a rebuild: COMPACTION_PER_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 35), COMPACTION_GLOBAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 120), COMPACTION_MAX_RETRIES (default 3), COMPACTION_RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS (default 1), COMPACTION_INCLUDE_PREVIOUS_SUMMARIES (default true, consolidates prior summaries instead of stacking them turn after turn). New Grafana dashboard 14-compaction.json with 7 panels (strategy mix, latencies p50/p95/p99, per-chunk timeouts, global timeouts, errors by type, skip reasons, tokens saved). Five new Prometheus metrics including compaction_writer_unavailable_total which makes any silent SSE-signal degradation visible. A transactional SQL script scripts/admin/reset_user_checkpoints.sql resets a single user's checkpoints for stuck-conversation recovery, without touching messages or the application. Full operator documentation in docs/technical/COMPACTION_v2.md.

v1_20_7.title: v1.20.7 — Bulk reminder deletion: the summary is finally readable, with each reminder's name and trigger time

items.i1: The summary after a bulk deletion is finally readable — When you said "delete all my reminders" and confirmed the bulk operation, LIA used to reply with a generic block "✅ 3/3 / ✅ Action completed successfully / ✅ Action completed successfully / ✅ Action completed successfully" — no reminder name, no date, just a counter and three identical lines. Each row now carries the deleted reminder and its trigger time, with a header that agrees grammatically with your language: 🔔 ✅ 3 reminders deleted / ✅ Buy groceries — Friday May 16, 2026 at 2:00 PM / ✅ Call Mom — Saturday May 17, 2026 at 9:00 AM / ✅ Doctor appointment — Sunday May 18, 2026 at 11:00 AM. The same format applies automatically to bulk deletions of emails, events, contacts, tasks, Drive files, and Gmail labels.
items.i2: The confirmation panel before a bulk deletion finally looks the same regardless of the internal path — Before this release, asking for a bulk deletion could present two different looks depending on which code path was taken internally (FOR_EACH on one side, draft-critique batch on the other) — one showed Reminder: Doctor on May 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM, the other showed 🔔 Reminder: Doctor 🔔 Sunday May 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM (doubled emoji, broken formatting). You now see the same unified rendering on both sides: 🔔 Reminder : Doctor - Sunday May 17, 2026 at 7:00 PM — one domain emoji, the category noun (Reminder / Email / Event / Task / Contact / File / Label) before the title, the weekday included in the date, and a dash separator between title and date. The dialog title also moves from "Confirmation required" to "Confirm deletion" for reminders, consistent with other deletion types.

v1_20_6.title: v1.20.6 — More reliable web searches, end-to-end Gemini 3.x LLM support, 28 timeouts now tunable without rebuild

items.i1: Web-search response enrichment (Brave) is more reliable — When LIA triggered a web search to enrich a response (fact-check, recent context, etc.), a misconfigured internal timeout (3 s) cut the request before the search engine had time to reply (5 s). Result: searches that looked like they ran but returned nothing, and answers thin on context. The wrapper timeout is now 8 s and stays consistent with the underlying HTTP call (internal rule: enclosing timeout ≥ HTTP × 1.5). No setting to change — it's fixed in the background.
items.i2: Gemini 3.x LLM: full pipeline (planner, memory, voice, HITL) now compatible — If you (or your administrator) had switched any LLM type to Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (or any future Gemini 3.x) under LLM Configuration, several flows silently fell back to fallback behaviors or even displayed corrupted output. The cause: Gemini 3.x returns its content in a structured form (blocks) where every other provider uses a plain string. 33 places in the code read that string without protection. All of them have been migrated to the official BaseMessage.text API (LangChain Core 1.2+) which handles both shapes. Concretely: the planner, memory reference resolution, HITL question generation (tool approval + plan approval), voice comments, broadcast notifications, and even the LLM cache keys now behave identically with Gemini 3.x or any other provider.
items.i3: Admin: 28 timeouts previously hardcoded are now tunable via .env — The full timeout plumbing (outbound HTTP to Brave / Perplexity / Wikipedia / OpenWeatherMap / Ollama, short/long connector operations, SSE polling, OAuth locks, scheduled-actions executor, WebSocket idle windows, image generation, browser agent, sub-agents, devops Claude…) is now exposed as operator-tunable settings — no more Docker rebuild to adjust a single timeout. A central reference docs/technical/TIMEOUT_REGISTRY.md documents every parameter (role, default, range, consumer file, cascades) with three annexes: Annex A (LLM-call timeouts out-of-scope, managed via LLM Configuration), Annex B (mirror of frontend timing.ts), Annex C (known gaps deferred to a future wave). All defaults match the historical values — no behavior change by default. Three cleanups along the way: 2 dead constants removed, 1 duplicate (currency API) resolved, 1 orphan field (task_orchestrator_execution_timeout_seconds) actually wired as a soft cap on the total duration of multi-wave plans + new Prometheus counter lia_parallel_execution_global_timeout_total.
items.i4: Preventive defense layer on the planner (in observe mode) — When you asked something like « my next two medical appointments », the planner could try to filter the word « medical » directly inside the search (which doesn't work for Google Calendar, Gmail, etc., which only index by literal text) — result: 0 hits or the wrong ones. A new validation layer (ADR-084) now detects these semantic-qualifier leaks (« urgent », « important », « medical »…) in text-search parameters of literal-search tools and reports them via a dedicated Prometheus counter. Current mode: observation only — no plan is mutated in this release, the time to validate frequency and absence of false positives. Phase 2 (auto-correction activation) is planned after a few weeks of telemetry. Controlled by PLANNER_SEMANTIC_LEAK_MODE=observe|autocorrect|off.

v1_20_5.title: v1.20.5 — Sub-agents: expert analyses finally substantive, expert voice preserved, 3 new admin settings

items.i1: Analyses delegated to a sub-agent are finally substantive — When you asked "answer me like a senior analyst, use a specialised sub-agent", the sub-agent used to go off exploring in every direction (up to 30+ successive searches), exhausted its budget before any synthesis, and returned either a truncated answer or a hollow blurb that the main assistant then drowned in its own conversational tone — the delegation added no real value. The sub-agent now follows a clear contract ("if an assistant could write the same thing without you, it's a failure"), calibrates the shape of its output to the signals in the request (deep analysis → sourced multi-section report; summary → faithful condensed version; comparison → parallel dimension-by-dimension structure), cites a URL for every figure, distinguishes facts from inferences, flags missing data instead of inventing it — and the main assistant relays its analysis verbatim (sections, sources, structure intact) without compressing or rewriting it in a sarcastic voice. Bonus: no more forced markdown tables in these answers — comparisons now use parallel lists or sections, which read better.
items.i2: Admin: 3 new settings to pilot the sub-agents — SUBAGENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 180 s, range 30-600) and SUBAGENT_TOOL_MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 300 s, range 60-900) decouple the delegation time budget from the generic MAX_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS ceiling (120 s, unchanged for other tools) — ReAct loops running on a slow reasoning model (deepseek high, gpt-5.2 high) can now legitimately last 90-150 s without being killed mid-synthesis. SUBAGENT_RESEARCH_TOOLS_WHITELIST (default brave_search_tool,fetch_web_page_tool) refocuses the sub-agent on factual verification instead of exploring a catalogue of ~80 tools (which used to burn its entire budget on sterile exploration). Validation at load time: a misspelled name in .env (dashes instead of underscores, semicolons instead of commas) raises a clear error instead of a silently empty whitelist.
items.i3: Admin: sub-agent iteration budget raised to 10 by default — SUBAGENT_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS moves from 5 to 10 (range widened to 1-30, up from 1-15). LangGraph counts every node visit as a superstep, so 5 barely supported 2 tool rounds + synthesis — at 10, the sub-agent has the headroom for 3-4 tool rounds and a complete synthesis without hitting GraphRecursionError. Tune SUBAGENT_DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS in .env if you want to push further (up to 30 for very deep analyses, or drop to 5-6 to save tokens on simple tasks).

v1_20_4.title: v1.20.4 — Reliable web browsing agent, Anthropic Claude 4.x fix, robust LLM config on model change

items.i1: The web browsing agent now completes multi-step tasks reliably — Asking LIA to "go to a website and do X" used to work for a quick lookup but fall apart on anything longer: the browsing loop was cut off after ~30 seconds, saw only a truncated view of the page, sometimes invented URLs with guessed parameters, and rarely reached the right form. Now the loop gets a real time budget (up to several minutes), sees far more of the page (accessibility-tree budget raised from 5 000 to 15 000 tokens), navigates through the site's own controls instead of fabricating URLs, handles autocomplete fields (it clicks the matching suggestion), re-checks the page after each action, detects when it's stuck and changes strategy, and — on transactional flows — advances up to (but not past) the login / payment / final-validation step, then stops and reports what it found and what you still need to do. A new admin setting BROWSER_REACT_MAX_ITERATIONS (default 15) caps how many reason↔act iterations a single browsing task may run.
items.i2: Admin: the Anthropic Claude 4.x models in the LLM Configuration dropdown now work — "Claude Opus 4.6 / 4.5", "Claude Sonnet 4.6" and "Claude Haiku 4.5" were registered in the model catalogue with a dotted id (claude-opus-4.6) that the Anthropic API rejects with 404 not_found_error — picking one of them for any LLM type made that feature fail immediately. The catalogue, the mcp_app_react_agent default and the affected database rows are corrected to the dashed form the API expects (claude-opus-4-6, …); a one-shot migration rewrites existing configuration rows.
items.i3: Admin: changing the model or provider of an LLM type can no longer break that type — In Configuration LLM, switching an LLM type from one model to another could leave behind a "reasoning effort" value whose shape no longer fit the newly selected model (for example a DeepSeek-style "off" left on a config now pointing at a Qwen model) — the feature then crashed on its next call. The reasoning-effort value is now automatically re-normalized to the new model when you change it (kept if compatible, otherwise cleared), the save endpoint rejects an incompatible combination with a clear error, and — as a final safety net — the runtime silently falls back to the model's default if a stale incompatible value ever slips through (logged for the admin).

v1_20_3.title: v1.20.3 — Itinerary tool resilience: directions still work for events that have already started

items.i1: Directions to an in-progress meeting now work as expected — Asking LIA for the route to your next appointment when that appointment had already started (an all-day reservation, a meeting reviewed 30 minutes after kick-off, etc.) used to silently produce a chatty fallback with no map card and no ETA. The Google Routes API rejected the call because LIA passed the event's original start time as the target arrival time, which by then was in the past. Past arrival/departure times are now silently clamped to now + 60 seconds before reaching the API, while genuinely future timestamps remain untouched so traffic prediction stays accurate. Result: the HTML route card and ETA appear reliably, even when you ask after the meeting began.

v1_20_2.title: v1.20.2 — Voice STT/TTS catalogue, per-message cost attribution, sentence streaming

items.i1: New remote Speech-to-Text option (ElevenLabs Scribe) — Voice mode gains a per-user toggle in Settings → Voice mode: keep the free local Sherpa-onnx Whisper (default, audio never leaves the LIA server) or opt into ElevenLabs Scribe ($0.22/h, billed per audio duration) for higher accuracy on conversational speech. A discreet 🎤 badge on each user bubble shows the duration and EUR cost of the transcription. Cost flows into your usual Cost dashboard tile and usage limits — no separate quota.
items.i2: TTS becomes catalogue-driven: 3 providers, single admin form — Voice synthesis is now configured through Configuration LLM → Voice TTS with three providers seeded from day one: Edge (free, default, Microsoft neural voices), OpenAI (tts-1, tts-1-hd) and ElevenLabs (eleven_multilingual_v2, eleven_turbo_v2_5, eleven_flash_v2_5). Per-provider tuning surfaces (Edge SSML rate/pitch/volume, OpenAI speed + format, ElevenLabs stability/similarity_boost/style/use_speaker_boost) and a live voice picker for ElevenLabs (custom + library voices from your account).
items.i3: Per-message TTS cost on assistant bubbles — Paid TTS providers now surface a 🔊 badge on the assistant message showing the character count and the EUR cost of the synthesis (Edge free → no badge). Hover the badge for the provider, model and exact rate. Aggregated into the Cost dashboard tile and exportable via the new tts-usage CSV (admin + user) and the extended consumption-summary.
items.i4: Voice latency: first audio in ~1 second instead of ~5 seconds — A new sentence-level streamer dispatches TTS synthesis as soon as a complete sentence is produced by the LLM, in parallel. The first sentence starts playing while the assistant is still composing the rest of the answer — instead of waiting for the full text. Persistent HTTP keepalive on ElevenLabs saves another ~100–300 ms per sentence. Works in both chat and agent modes.
items.i5: Admin: STT remote kill switch + duration cap (cost-spike defence) — Two safety levers on the remote STT pipeline. The ELEVENLABS_STT_ENABLED environment flag now actually disables remote STT at runtime (instant fallback to local Sherpa for incident response or emergency quota). The ELEVENLABS_STT_MAX_AUDIO_DURATION_SECONDS cap (default 5 min) is now enforced before each call — oversized clips are rejected with a clear error, no provider charge incurred.
items.i6: Voice errors now show a precise reason — Failures across the three TTS providers (Edge / OpenAI / ElevenLabs) are now surfaced with a stable error code: provider timeout, rate limit reached (with retry-after delay when available), authentication issue, network error, empty audio response, generic HTTP error. The frontend can show a precise toast for each — instead of a generic "voice failed" message.
items.i7: New CSV exports for STT and TTS usage — stt-usage and tts-usage are added under Settings → Consumption Export (per-user) and the admin export tab (per-user filter). They list every paid voice call with date, conversation, message ID, provider, duration / characters and EUR cost. consumption-summary also gets new STT and TTS columns so totals stay in one place.

v1_20_1.title: v1.20.1 — Admin LLM: per-model sampling matrix and reusable reasoning shape templates

items.i1: Configuration LLM: sampling sliders only show what the API accepts — In the per-type LLM Configuration dialog, the four sampling inputs (temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty) now appear or hide per individual parameter based on what each model's API actually accepts. Anthropic 4.5+ surfaces only temperature; DeepSeek V4 surfaces all four; GPT-5 series surfaces none. The reasoning widget itself (enum select, integer budget, or toggle+budget) is also driven directly by the model's declared shape — the dialog never lets you pick a value the API would reject.
items.i2: Pricing LLM: "Copy reasoning shape from…" template selector — When you add a new reasoning model in the Tarification LLM Texte admin form, you no longer have to type the reasoning widget / enum values / budget range by hand. A new dropdown lets you pick a representative model whose reasoning behavior is identical (e.g. "like gpt-5" for OpenAI o-series / GPT-5 reasoning, "like claude-opus-4-5" for Anthropic 4.5+, "like deepseek-v4-flash" for DeepSeek V4) and the four reasoning shape fields are snapshot-copied at creation time. The list deduplicates the catalogue automatically (~15 unique reasoning shapes today) and self-enriches: any model created in Custom (advanced) mode with a novel shape becomes available as a template afterwards.
items.i3: Toggle "Is reasoning model" gates the reasoning controls — The Pricing form now hides the template selector and the Custom block whenever the new model is non-reasoning. Switching the toggle off resets the widget to none and clears any pending template choice. kind (chat / image / audio / …), the four sampling toggles and the optional tooltip i18n key remain visible regardless and are saved per model — independent of the reasoning shape choice.
items.i4: Audit log: reasoning template + kind + widget captured on every create / update — The admin audit trail (visible in the security log) now records, for every LLM model creation or edit, which template the admin picked (or null in Custom mode), the model kind and the resolved reasoning widget. Instant forensic visibility on which API contract a given row inherited from.

v1_20_0.title: v1.20.0 — Stratified journal: levels, epistemic status, ambient user-model portrait

items.i1: Personal journals get four abstraction levels (L0/L1/L2/L3) — Every entry now carries a level: L0 raw observation (weak signal worth tracking), L1 operational directive (the WHEN→DO BECAUSE format), L2 transversal pattern (synthesis of several convergent L1s), L3 portrait facet. L2 and L3 are produced exclusively at consolidation, by topic clustering. The Settings panel now shows a level badge on each entry and a Group-by toggle (Theme / Level).
items.i2: Epistemic status on every entry — Each journal entry exposes a confidence dot (low / medium / high) plus evidence and contradiction counters. LIA can now distinguish hypotheses still being tested from observations confirmed across many turns — and quietly demote entries the user keeps contradicting. Confidence and level are editable in the create/edit dialog.
items.i3: Deferred self-evaluation (T → T+1) — At each turn, LIA looks at the directives it injected on the previous turn and reads your reaction in the current message. If you confirmed, the evidence counter ticks up; if you pushed back, contradiction ticks up. The journal therefore measures its own usefulness — at zero added LLM cost (same extractor call, just enriched prompt).
items.i4: New "How LIA sees you" section in the journal Settings — A compiled user-model portrait surfaces above the entries accordion, with two read-only tabs (Full / Brief), a compilation timestamp and a freshness badge. The full version (≈ 200 tokens) feeds the conversation and the planner; the brief version (≈ 60 tokens) is diffused everywhere else LIA speaks: ReAct, voice, reminders, heartbeat notifications, proactive interest pings, fallback responses. Same nuanced model of you, carried across every channel.
items.i5: Three corrective levers on the portrait — The portrait itself is a synthesis and is never directly editable. Three levers are exposed instead: (1) edit/delete the L3 source entries (standard CRUD), (2) 🚩 Signal a problem opens a free-text dialog and triggers a synchronous re-consolidation (~5–10 s) with the user signal pinned at the top of the prompt, (3) 🔄 Consolidate now runs the full consolidation cycle on demand, bypassing the cooldown.
items.i6: Smart filter "show only entries never used" — A new toggle at the top of the entries list surfaces entries with uses=0 and no last-injection date. These are the candidates for reformulation or deletion at the next consolidation pass — instant visibility on which directives never proved useful.
items.i7: Better consolidation discipline — The consolidation prompt now performs an explicit pairwise dedup scan as STEP 1, audits theme misclassifications, actively clusters convergent L1s into L2 patterns, and compiles the user-model portrait — all in the same LLM call (no extra cost). Result: noisy duplicates collapse periodically, distinct entries actually emerge across themes and levels.
items.i8: GDPR: portrait scrubbed on account deletion — When an account is deleted, the three portrait columns (full, brief, compiled timestamp) are blanked out alongside the rest of the user data. The export endpoint also includes the compiled portrait under a portrait key for completeness.

v1_18_1.title: v1.18.1 — Today Briefing polish, fresh screenshots, enriched statistics

items.i1: LIA greeting now overlays the welcome image — The personalized AI-generated greeting now sits directly on top of the LIA avatar, replacing the random marketing taglines. More personal, with the tokens + EUR cost of the call still discreetly shown underneath.
items.i2: Refresh button always visible on mobile — On smartphones, the small sync icon on each dashboard card is now always shown (no need to hover — which doesn't exist on touch screens). On desktop, behavior is unchanged: visible on card hover with the +12° rotation affordance.
items.i3: Usage statistics: start date for the lifetime totals — Under each total counter (messages, tokens, Google API requests, cost), a small 'since DD/MM/YYYY' label shows your account creation date — the reference start of the lifetime totals is now explicit.
items.i4: Illustrative icons on dashboard sections — 'Mon dashboard' now sports a sunrise icon 🌅 (consistent with the daily-ritual nature of the briefing); 'Statistiques d'utilisation' gets a bar chart icon 📊. Both titles also share the exact same typography so the two main sections look like siblings.
items.i5: 12 fresh dashboard screenshots on the landing page — The landing carousel and README images are refreshed with the v1.18.x captures, and 4 new ones are added: chat debug panel, interactive skills, long-term memory, Psyche Engine. Cache is invalidated automatically so no browser stays on the old images.
items.i6: 'Skills' and 'Health data' descriptions trimmed on the home page — Both descriptions were 4× longer than the rest; rewritten to the same length as their neighbors in 6 languages, no information lost (the long-form details live in the FAQ and the docs).

v1_18_0.title: v1.18.0 — Today Briefing: the home becomes a daily ritual

items.i1: New 'Today' home page — The dashboard replaces static stats with a daily briefing: a personalized AI-generated greeting, a 2-3 sentence synthesis as a teleprompter, then a grid of 6 operational cards: enriched weather (with 5-day forecast, wind, rain probability), today's agenda, unread mails, upcoming birthdays, active reminders, health metrics.
items.i2: Non-blocking progressive rendering — The 6 cards appear as soon as the sources respond (≈ 1 s) without waiting for the AI. The synthesis arrives once the LLM has finished (≈ 1-3 s) with a discreet 'updated ✨' badge for 1.5 s. If a card temporarily fails (expired Google token, etc.), only that card shows its CTA — the others stay visible.
items.i3: Per-section cache with on-demand refresh — Each card has its own TTL adapted to its change rate (weather 1 h, agenda 10 min, mails 5 min, birthdays 24 h, reminders live, health 15 min). Per-card 'refresh' button visible on hover, 'refresh all' button at the top of the grid to re-fetch every source and regenerate the synthesis.
items.i4: Tokens and cost visible at a glance — Greeting and synthesis LLM calls display their actual consumption (token count + EUR cost) next to the timestamp, with a tooltip detailing the model used and the IN / OUT / CACHE breakdown. This consumption is also aggregated into your usual usage statistics, with no double-counting of cached tokens.
items.i5: Weather localized in 6 languages — Day abbreviations in the 5-day forecast strip now use the browser's date format (Mon, lun., Mo., lun, lun, 周一) instead of a fixed English label.
items.i6: Health card with aligned columns — The 'today' and '14-day average' values for each metric (step count, heart rate) are now laid out in a fixed grid: the vertical separators between today/average line up horizontally across both metrics, regardless of label length.
items.i7: Compact Quick Access — The previous 3 quick-access cards are replaced by 2 cards (Help + Settings) with refined icons and hover states. The 'Security' card with no actionable purpose was removed.

v1_17_2.title: v1.17.2 — Health data: the assistant dialogues with your measurements, generic ingestion API

items.i1: New 'Assistant' toggle in Settings → Health data — A single opt-in switch (off by default) authorizes the assistant to read your health data for 4 integrations at once: conversation, proactive notifications, memories, internal journals. While off, no health data ever reaches the LLM.
items.i2: The assistant answers your health questions — Ask in chat: 'How many steps today?', 'My heart rate this week?', 'Anything unusual in my health recently?'. LIA answers factually with totals, averages, and baseline comparisons. Never diagnoses — only reports numbers.
items.i3: Reliable answers over natural time ranges — 'This week', 'this month', 'the last 7 days' are interpreted correctly and the assistant surfaces the values directly in its reply (totals, per-day detail) without retreating behind 'no data'.
items.i4: Adaptive baseline (bootstrap → rolling) — LIA honestly qualifies its comparisons: the first 7 days are announced as 'based on N days of data only', then switches to a 28-day rolling median. Factual variation detection (streaks ≥ 3 days above 20% delta) and structural events (inactivity ≥ 3 days on steps).
items.i5: Proactive Heartbeat integration — When the toggle is on, proactive notifications can combine weather + calendar + health ('sunny + 4 days inactive → short walk?'). Injected signals only carry deltas / trends / events — never raw values.
items.i6: Generic ingestion API — The health API accepts measurements from any source (iOS Shortcuts, Android automation, third-party integration, IoT). When several sources cover the same period, the server merges them smartly (MAX for steps, average for heart rate). Landing and FAQ repositioned around this generic messaging.
items.i7: Extensibility for future measurement types — Architecture designed to accommodate new kinds (sleep, SpO2, calories…) without friction: ingestion, aggregation, baseline, Heartbeat, memory, and journal services adapt automatically.

v1_17_1.title: v1.17.1 — Health data: daily batch ingestion, simultaneous Watch+iPhone handling

items.i1: Daily batch ingestion instead of hourly push — For your iPhone Shortcut to fire reliably, the iPhone no longer needs to be unlocked every hour. On unlock or at a fixed time, the Shortcut pushes the whole day's samples. Re-sending the same day is free: the server deduplicates automatically on the measurement interval.
items.i2: Two separate Shortcuts (steps + heart rate) — The v1.17.0 single hourly POST is replaced by two dedicated URLs: /api/v1/ingest/health/steps and /api/v1/ingest/health/heart_rate. Each measurement carries its own time range (ISO 8601 with timezone). Action required: reconfigure your iPhone Shortcut per the updated guide.
items.i3: Smart fusion of simultaneous Watch + iPhone samples — When your Apple Watch and iPhone measure the same time interval, LIA now merges them intelligently: MAX for steps (each device counts a complementary subset of movement), rounded average for heart rate (two sensors aimed at the same signal). Fixes a 500 error that previously blocked longer-range uploads.
items.i4: Deletion by measurement type — Management actions under Settings → Health data → Management are revamped: delete all heart-rate measurements (step data kept), delete all step measurements (HR kept), or wipe everything. Each action truly deletes the affected rows rather than nulling columns.
items.i5: Chart UX improvements — Tooltips are now readable in dark mode (background and text follow the active theme). The Statistics section now displays the actual aggregation window (e.g. "Apr 21 18:00 → Apr 22 18:00") to defuse the "HR stats don't move when I change period" confusion — they're invariant when all measurements already fit inside the smallest window.

v1_17_0.title: v1.17.0 — Health data: iPhone Shortcuts ingestion + charts

items.i1: New "Health data" section in Settings → Features — LIA can now receive heart rate and step counts from an iPhone Shortcut automation. Everything is visualized as a line chart (HR) and a bar chart (steps) with a period selector (hour / day / week / month / year) and dashed lines for the period average.
items.i2: Dedicated, revocable token auth — Generate a token (starts with hm_…) from the app, copy it once (never shown again, only a display prefix remains) and paste it into your Shortcut. The token only authorizes health data ingestion — nothing else of your account. You can issue multiple tokens and revoke any of them independently.
items.i3: Granular deletion — Three actions in the "Data management" sub-section: delete all heart rates (steps preserved), delete all steps (HR preserved), or wipe everything. GDPR-aware: raw HR and step values are never written to server logs.
items.i4: Step-by-step iPhone Shortcut setup guide — End-to-end documentation (steps A-E + hourly schedule) in docs/guides/GUIDE_IPHONE_SHORTCUTS_HEALTH.md with payload example, troubleshooting and security notes. Default physiological bounds: HR ∈ [20, 250] bpm, steps ∈ [0, 15 000] per sample (configurable).

v1_16_10.title: v1.16.10 — Observability overhaul: 20 dashboards, full metric coverage, faster DB

items.i1: Two new Grafana observability dashboards — A dashboard dedicated to sub-agents and skills (activity, token budget, rich outputs) plus another for ReAct mode and the browser (invocations, iterations, tool errors). Admins now have 20 dashboards covering 354+ panels, with no blind spots.
items.i2: 90+ Prometheus metrics revived — An audit surfaced that a significant share of metrics declared in code were never actually emitted in production (router, planner, HITL, OAuth, connectors, voice, drafts, initiative, data-registry, conversations). Instrumentation added everywhere, with defensive guards so metric failures never break the critical path.
items.i3: Faster DAU/WAU and connector activation queries — Three DB indexes added via migration (obs_indexes_001): ix_conversations_updated_at, ix_conversations_created_at, ix_connectors_status. The gauge-updating background task drops from ~500ms (full scan) to <50ms on a populated DB.
items.i4: No more Prometheus cardinality bomb on connectors — The operation label on connector_api_* metrics used to receive raw URL paths (with UUIDs, tokens, numeric IDs), blowing up Prometheus memory over time. A segment-by-segment sanitizer (UUID/id/hex_id/token → placeholders) is now applied upstream.
items.i5: FastAPI validation errors (422) are tracked — Pydantic validation failures on incoming payloads are now counted per field + error_type (capped at 10 per request to bound cardinality), visible on dashboard 16 to surface bad-payload patterns.

v1_16_8.title: v1.16.8 — Rich skills: cards, images, mini-apps right in the chat

items.i1: Your skills can now render cards, images and interactive mini-apps — In addition to a text reply, a skill can now return an interactive HTML frame (Google Maps view, weather dashboard, monthly calendar, unit converter...) and/or an image (QR code, chart). Seven new built-in skills showcase this: interactive-map, weather-dashboard, calendar-month, qr-code, pomodoro-timer, unit-converter, dice-roller.
items.i2: Theme and language stay in sync with your frames — When you toggle dark mode or change the app language, the embedded mini-apps update live without a reload. Ergonomics stay consistent across the whole conversation.
items.i3: Frames now visible regardless of your display mode — Interactive mini-apps (skills, MCP apps, drafts) now show up in Rich HTML, Markdown and Cards display modes — previously they were invisible outside the Cards mode.
items.i4: End-to-end documentation for building rich skills — The Skills Guide now includes a complete "Localization, theming and runtime conventions" section in the Advanced tab, with copy-paste code examples (QR code with segno, coin flip with animation and re-roll). The built-in skill-generator has been updated too, so it produces compliant skills on the first shot.
items.i5: Skills settings: less visual clutter — The "Built-in skills" and "My imported skills" sections are now collapsed by default — when you've accumulated many skills, the Settings page stays readable.

v1_16_7.title: v1.16.7 — Relevant weather alerts, even when you travel

items.i1: No more nonsense temperature alerts at night — LIA no longer sends you "temperature dropping" notifications that just describe the natural day/night cycle. The detector now compares today's average temperature with tomorrow's — and alerts you in both directions (colder OR warmer) so you actually know how to dress for the day ahead.
items.i2: Weather alerts follow you when you're away (opt-in) — If you enable it, LIA can use your current browser position for proactive weather notifications when you're travelling more than 50 km from home. Your location is encrypted, never historized (each update overwrites the previous one), and wiped immediately if you turn the option off or remove your home address. The notification always tells you the city it's talking about, so you know where the forecast refers to.
items.i3: Full transparency on what's stored — A new "Currently stored" block under Proactive notifications shows the exact coordinates LIA has kept, when they were last updated, and a "Clear now" button to wipe them on demand. This is how privacy should be.

items.i1: Your factual corrections finally stick — When you say "actually, I changed jobs, I'm at Meta now" or "my daughter's name is Elsa, not Emma", LIA now updates the existing memory instead of creating a contradictory duplicate. Your history stays coherent.
items.i2: Pinned memories strictly protected — LIA never tries to modify or delete memories you've locked. You keep full control over what stays frozen.
items.i3: Less redundancy in what LIA remembers — A new daily cleanup automatically merges near-identical memories that accumulate over conversations. Your psychological profile stays crisp.
items.i4: Memories age more gracefully — LIA now better distinguishes what deserves to be remembered (durable facts useful for personalization) from what is transient (thanks, passing moods). Medium-importance preferences stop cluttering memory after a few weeks, while important information (family, identity, milestones) is preserved long-term.

items.i1: "This meeting", "the first one", "delete it" — LIA finally keeps up — The assistant now remembers the last item you actually manipulated, searched for, or even just referenced. No more confusion between a meeting you just created and the one you're talking about now: when you say "delete this meeting" after asking "what was the first meeting returned?", LIA deletes the right one.
items.i2: Clearer HITL preview for updates — When LIA asks you to confirm a modification (meeting, contact, task), the preview is now structured as two clean blocks: "Changes" (only what actually changes, with old → new) and "Full details after update" (the complete post-update snapshot). No more contradictory "Other details unchanged" labels followed by values that just got updated.
items.i3: Consistency after create / update / delete — After an action is confirmed (e.g., a meeting created via HITL), the previously displayed list stays in sync automatically: updates propagate to search results, deletions remove the deleted item, and the conversational focus always tracks the latest handled item.

items.i1: Skills trigger more reliably on natural phrasing — LIA now understands your intent by reading each skill's description rather than relying on technical hints (detected domains). Variations like "I want my daily briefing", "Do my briefing", or "Summarize my day" now always activate the right skill, without misfiring.
items.i2: Custom skill authoring simplified — The max_missing_domains configuration field has been removed from the skill-editing guide. Skills trigger automatically when their description matches your request — no more fiddling with technical parameters for LIA to recognize them.

v1_16_3.title: v1.16.3 — Enriched briefing, email fix & random phrases

items.i1: Daily briefing: emails and reminders now included — The daily briefing skill now consistently retrieves your recent emails and pending reminders, alongside calendar events, tasks, and weather. The issue where emails never appeared in the briefing is fixed.
items.i2: Skills compatible with all user profiles — If you haven't connected a service (e.g., Gmail), the corresponding steps are automatically skipped without blocking the rest of the briefing. You always get the maximum available information.
items.i3: Fun analyzing phrases are back — The witty waiting messages ("🔮 Consulting the crystal ball...", "🚀 Liftoff imminent...") are back during the initial analysis of your request, adding a touch of personality.

items.i1: Real-time execution steps — You can now see each processing step as it happens: analysis, planning, validation, orchestration, and each tool call (emails, calendar, weather, contacts...). Steps accumulate visually and disappear when the response arrives.
items.i2: Tool names in ReAct mode — ReAct mode now shows which specific tool is being used (e.g., "Retrieving events...", "Searching contacts...") instead of a generic "Executing tool..." message. A reasoning snippet is also displayed.
items.i3: Pipeline steps now visible — Previously, only a random analyzing phrase was shown during Pipeline execution. You now see the actual progression: routing → planning → validation → task orchestration → tool execution → response.
items.i4: Improved tone consistency — LIA's personality and emotional state are now more reliably integrated into all responses, including proactive notifications, reminders, and voice comments. A safety guardrail ensures LIA never projects its own mood onto you.
items.i5: Reliable temporal memory — When you mention relative dates ("tomorrow", "next Saturday", "next week"), LIA now systematically converts them to absolute dates before storing them. Your memories stay reliable and relevant even weeks later.

items.i1: Admin LLM overrides now fully enforced — Configuration changes made in the Administration panel (provider, model, temperature, reasoning mode, etc.) are now guaranteed to apply everywhere, including interest notifications and proactive content. Previously, some background tasks could ignore admin settings.
items.i2: Interest notification truncation fixed — Proactive interest notifications that ended with "..." mid-sentence are now complete. The issue was caused by an incorrect reasoning mode consuming output tokens.

items.i1: ReAct mode — New execution mode where the assistant reasons step by step: it calls a tool, analyzes the result, then decides autonomously what to do next. More autonomous but consumes 4 to 8× more tokens than Pipeline mode — best reserved for complex research or exploratory questions where the added value justifies the cost. Activate it via the 🔀/⚡ toggle in the chat header (🔀 = Pipeline, ⚡ = ReAct).
items.i2: Cross-domain initiative — In ReAct mode, the assistant proactively checks related information. Example: asking about Sunday's weather may also surface your calendar events for that day.
items.i3: Skills in ReAct — Your active skills are now available in ReAct mode. The assistant can autonomously activate and use them during its reasoning.
items.i4: Improved cost tracking — Token consumption and costs are now accurately tracked for all LLM providers, including in multi-step ReAct conversations.
items.i5: Execution steps in debug panel — ReAct reasoning steps (setup, reasoning, tool execution, finalization) now appear in the debug panel for transparency.

v1_15_3.title: v1.15.3 — Memory precision, interest deduplication, improved RAG search

items.i1: More precise memory retrieval — Irrelevant memories appear less often in conversation context, thanks to recalibrated similarity thresholds.
items.i2: Better targeted journal behavioral directives — Directives from your journals are now more relevant and less generic.
items.i3: Improved interest deduplication — Similar but distinct interests (e.g., Italian cuisine vs Japanese cuisine) are no longer incorrectly merged.
items.i4: Less repetitive content notifications — Proactive notifications now avoid sending you similar content repeatedly.
items.i5: More relevant RAG document search — Search results across your documents are more precise and better targeted.
items.i6: Optimized LLM models for extraction — Data extraction tasks now use more capable models for better results.
