items.i1: Psyche v2 — Expanded emotion palette to 22 emotions, graduated directives, serenity floor, narrative transitions, multi-emotion self-report, emotional resonance, proactive emotions, and enriched avatar tooltip.

v1_15_1.title: v1.15.1 — MCP App Fix & ReAct Timeout

items.i1: MCP iterative timeout fix — Excalidraw diagrams and other iterative MCP tools were failing because the timeout was too short (60s) for the multi-step ReAct agent. The timeout is now automatically extended to at least 120s for all iterative MCP tools.
items.i2: MCP App widget display fix — Interactive widgets (like Excalidraw diagrams) could disappear from the response when the intelligent filtering did not recognize them as relevant results. MCP App widgets are now always preserved in the response.

v1_15.title: v1.15 — Smart Memory Resolution, Optimization & Security

items.i1: Iterative Mode for Your MCP Servers — Your personal MCP servers can now use iterative mode (ReAct agent). Enable it in settings so LIA reads the server documentation first, then executes tools step by step — ideal for complex APIs like Excalidraw
items.i2: 3-Phase Memory Resolution — When you say 'call my brother' or 'send an email to my wife', LIA now identifies personal references more accurately with targeted per-reference memory search. Fewer errors, less noise, more relevance
items.i3: Improved Error Messages — When issues occur (AI provider overload, content filter, timeout), error messages are now clear and translated in your language instead of showing technical codes
items.i4: Refined Proactive Initiative — Proactive suggestions after an action (weather before an appointment, contact related to an email) now focus only on different domains than what was already handled. Result: more relevant suggestions, less noise
items.i5: Safe Reminder Cancellation — Cancelling a reminder now requires confirmation before execution, preventing accidental deletions
items.i6: Localized Weather Dates — Weather forecasts now display dates in your language ('Monday, April 8' instead of raw ISO dates)
items.i7: Faster Responses — Internal prompts compressed by 30–70%, reducing response time and cost per query
items.i8: 'These emails / these appointments' Fix — Plural references like 'delete these emails' or 'modify these appointments' are now correctly detected to act on the right items
items.i9: Improved Contact Search — When the planner provides a name instead of a technical ID, LIA automatically searches for the contact by name instead of failing silently
items.i10: Iterative Mode Toggle Fix — Enabling/disabling iterative mode on personal MCP servers is now correctly saved and displayed
items.i11: Dedicated AI for MCP Apps — MCP servers with interactive widgets (like Excalidraw) now automatically use a more powerful AI model, configurable by administrators in the LLM Config panel under 'MCP App (ReAct)'

v1_14.title: v1.14 — LIA's Psyche: Dynamic Emotional Intelligence

items.i1: Response Display Mode — Choose between 3 display modes: HTML Cards (structured visual cards — default), Rich HTML (beautifully formatted responses) or Markdown (plain text). Configurable in Settings > Personalization
items.i2: LIA's Psyche — Your assistant develops a dynamic psychological state: mood (14 states), emotions (22 types), a deepening relationship, drives, and self-efficacy. Mood and emotions subtly influence the tone and style of every response
items.i3: Emotional Avatar — A mood emoji replaces the classic LIA logo on messages. The avatar reflects the emotional state in real time with a colored ring and detailed tooltip
items.i4: Emotional Dashboard — Visualize the evolution of mood (PAD), emotions, relationship, and drives across 4 interactive charts with time range selector (24h to 90d)
items.i5: Comprehensive Education Guide — 'Understanding the Psyche' section with 7 illustrated subsections: overview, personality traits, mood, emotions, relationship, drives, settings
items.i6: Customizable Expressiveness — Expressiveness (stoic → highly expressive) and stability (volatile → very stable) sliders to adjust emotional temperament. Mood refresh and full reset options
items.i7: Evolution Awareness — The assistant knows how its mood and emotions have shifted since the last message, providing narrative continuity to conversations
items.i8: Prompt Directives Overhaul — All context blocks injected into prompts now carry precise operational directives (how to use the data), improving response relevance
items.i9: Smart Skill Activation — Skills without a plan template are now automatically detected and activated. Skills with Python scripts run via a dedicated ReAct agent in an isolated loop; others inject passively with no extra LLM call
items.i10: Script Execution Fix — Skill script execution now works in all environments (Docker, Linux, Windows) with process isolation and robust error handling
items.i11: Faster Startup — Tool selection embeddings are now cached on disk. Server restart is faster and no longer consumes unnecessary API calls
items.i12: Proactive Suggestions Preserved — Suggestions generated by proactive initiative (weather, reminders, etc.) are no longer lost during intelligent response filtering
items.i13: Streamlined confirmations — Delete and modify operations now require only one confirmation instead of two or three. Confirmation titles are now explicit ("Confirm deletion", "Confirm sending", etc.)
items.i14: Anti-hallucination defense — The system automatically detects and strips parameters invented by the AI during planning, preventing silent failures on deletions and other operations

v1_13.title: v1.13 — Design System v4, Skills, Administration & Account Lifecycle

items.i1: Account Lifecycle — Administrators can deactivate, delete (data purge with billing history preservation) and permanently erase (GDPR) user accounts in 3 secure steps
items.i2: Background Task Protection — Proactive notifications, reminders, scheduled actions and journal consolidation no longer consume AI tokens for deactivated or deleted accounts
items.i3: Visual Account Status — Admin panel visually distinguishes Active (green), Deactivated (red) and Deleted (gray strikethrough) accounts with state-appropriate action buttons
items.i4: Design System v4 — Complete visual redesign of all 14 HTML cards with reusable components, colored vignettes, chips, avatars and collapsible sections
items.i5: Skills Guide Redesigned — New comprehensive 3-tab guide (Fundamentals, Create, Advanced) with full agent, tool and parameter catalogue
items.i6: Enhanced Administration — 5 new counters in user management (Skills, MCP, Scheduled Actions, RAG Spaces, Blocked) and sortable Email/Blocked columns in limits
items.i7: Multi-provider — Calendar, Email, Contacts, Drive and Tasks tools now presented as compatible with Google, Microsoft and Apple
items.i8: DevOps Claude CLI — Administrators can diagnose servers via Claude Code in natural language directly from LIA
items.i9: Calendar DST Fix — Events created during daylight saving transitions now have the correct time
items.i10: Cross-domain context fix — "Show me the last email" after viewing calendar events now works correctly
items.i11: Route-to-calendar timezone fix — Travel time calculations to calendar events now use the correct local time (a 2-hour offset could cause arriving 2 hours too early)

items.i1: AI Image Generation — Create images from text descriptions, with quality, size and format options
items.i2: Image Editing — Modify existing images using natural language instructions
items.i3: Image Preferences — Quality (low/medium/high), size (square/portrait/landscape) and format (PNG/WebP) configurable per user
items.i4: Live Screenshots — During web browsing, screenshots are displayed in real-time in the conversation
items.i5: Journal Deduplication — Similar entries are automatically merged to avoid duplicates
items.i6: Image Pricing — Admin panel to manage image generation pricing by model, quality and size
items.i7: Image Download — Download generated images and screenshots directly from the chat via a button or long-press on mobile
items.i8: Precise Hue Light Control — LIA now distinguishes a specific light (e.g., 'living room ceiling') from the entire room, thanks to automatic device discovery before each command

items.i1: Proactive Initiative — After responding, LIA detects complementary signals and enriches its response (e.g., rainy forecast → checks for outdoor events)
items.i2: MCP Iterative Mode — Better Excalidraw diagram generation with a dedicated ReAct agent
items.i3: GPT-5.4 Support — New GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4-mini models available
items.i4: Route Time Fix — Arrival and departure times now respect the user's timezone
items.i5: CC/BCC Modification — CC and BCC recipients can now be modified during draft review
items.i6: Enhanced Security — SSRF prevention, OAuth validation, parameter injection protection

items.i1: Mobile Push-to-Talk — Improved touch handling on smartphones (swipe cancellation, no context menu interference)
items.i2: Reduced Voice Latency — Parallelized and pre-warmed connections, faster end-of-speech detection
items.i3: Ready Chime — A short sound confirms LIA is ready to listen after the wake word
items.i4: Speech Language — Voice recognition uses the user's preferred language
items.i5: Safari iOS — Voice mode now works on Safari (iPhone/iPad)
items.i6: Rich HITL Review — Detailed draft display with emojis, before/after comparison and clickable links

items.i1: Usage Limits — Per-user quotas (tokens, messages, cost) with monthly cycle and global limits
items.i2: Limits Dashboard — Admin interface to manage quotas and block/unblock users
items.i3: Smart Blocking — Chat is disabled with a clear message when quota is exceeded
items.i4: Consumption Export — Each user can export their usage (LLM tokens, Google API, summary) as CSV
items.i5: Journal Semantic Search — Migration to high-quality embeddings with search keywords
items.i6: Emotional Safety — Adaptive behavioral directives for sensitive topics detected in memory
items.i7: Email Fixes — Reply, forward, CC/BCC and recipients fixed across all providers (Google, Apple, Microsoft)

items.i1: Philips Hue Connector — Control your lights by voice: "turn off the living room", "set the office to blue"
items.i2: Hue Pairing — Bridge discovery and pairing wizard (local and cloud)
items.i3: 6 Smart Home Tools — List/control lights, rooms and scenes with fuzzy name matching
items.i4: Min/Max Temperature — Weather cards now show the day's temperature range

items.i1: Personal Journals — LIA maintains thematic journals (reflections, observations, analyses, learnings)
items.i2: Auto Consolidation — Periodic reorganization of notes with intelligent merging and synthesis
items.i3: Context Injection — Journals enrich both responses and planner reasoning
items.i4: Technical Blog — 20 detailed articles on architecture, integrations and features (6 languages)
items.i5: Self-Knowledge — LIA answers questions about itself through a built-in FAQ knowledge base

items.i1: Web Browsing — LIA can navigate websites, fill forms and extract information
items.i2: Qwen Provider — Alibaba Cloud model support (qwen3-max, qwen3.5-plus, qwen3.5-flash)
items.i3: Ollama Models — Automatic discovery of models installed on your Ollama server
items.i4: 15 RAG Formats — PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, EPUB, CSV, HTML, RTF and more

items.i4: External Content Protection — Web content is wrapped to prevent prompt injection
items.i5: Email Notifications — Proactive notifications now include your urgent unread emails
items.i6: /resume Command — Force history synthesis to free up context

items.i1: FastAPI Update — Migration to FastAPI 0.135 for better streaming disconnection handling
items.i2: SSE Stability — Client disconnections during streaming are handled gracefully

items.i1: LAN Access — Configure access from other devices on your local network (mobile, tablet)

v1_16_9.title: v1.16.9 — LaTeX, code highlighting, history search and UX polish

items.i1: One-click copy on messages and code — A copy button now appears on hover of every LIA reply, and on every code block. No more manual selection to grab an address, a sentence or a snippet.
items.i2: Math formulas rendered beautifully — When you ask LIA for an equation or a scientific calculation, formulas are now displayed with their mathematical notation (LaTeX). Examples: $E = mc^2$ inline, $$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$ for centered blocks.
items.i3: Colored code with automatic language detection — Python, TypeScript, JSON, Bash, SQL... code blocks now render with syntax highlighting (25 languages supported). Light or dark theme based on your preferences.
items.i4: Search in your conversation history — A search bar has been added to the chat header. Type a word and LIA instantly filters matching messages among those loaded.
items.i5: Readable dates in the chat — Just the time for today's messages, "Yesterday 14:30" for yesterday's, the weekday for the current week, and the full date beyond. No more "Saturday, March 29, 2026" repeated under every recent message.
items.i6: Proactive feedback that sticks — When you click 👍 / 👎 / 🚫 on an interest suggestion, your choice is now persisted server-side and survives a reload or a device switch.
items.i7: Error messages in your language — Weather and Philips Hue smart-light responses are now translated to your preferred language instead of defaulting to French.
items.i8: Smarter mobile keyboard — On your phone, the chat input now enables auto-capitalization, autocorrect, and shows a dedicated "Send" button on the native keyboard instead of a plain return key.

v1_21_19.title: v1.21.19 — ⚡ Faster under load & self-healing storage

items.i1: ⚡ Smoother when several conversations run at once — LIA saves the state of your conversation at every step so it can always pick up where it left off. Until now those saves went through a single database lane per worker and queued up behind each other; they now run in parallel, so response times stay steady even when several conversations are active at the same time.
items.i2: 🔄 Storage that heals itself — If the database restarts or a connection drops, LIA now detects and replaces it automatically. Before, this could silently freeze conversation saving until the application was restarted.
items.i3: 🛠️ For self-hosters — Pool sizes are tunable in .env (LANGGRAPH_CHECKPOINT_POOL_MIN/MAX_SIZE, LANGGRAPH_STORE_POOL_MIN/MAX_SIZE), with the full connection budget documented. Setting the max to 1 reproduces the previous behavior — a rollback that needs no redeploy.

items.i1: 💾 Your data is now backed up automatically — Everything LIA keeps for you (conversations, memory, journals, settings) is saved every night, with 7 days, 4 weeks and 6 months of history kept. And the restore procedure is not theoretical: it is tested for real — an incident can no longer cost more than the last day.
items.i2: 🛠️ For self-hosters — A ready-to-use backup sidecar ships with the stack: schedule and retention configurable in .env, one command to back up (task backup:now), one to prove the restore works (task backup:verify), and a complete restore runbook.

items.i1: 📖 New “Story” page — Discover how LIA is built: nearly 100% of the code is written by an AI under human direction — written engineering rules, blocking automated checks, systematic review, adversarial audits. Accessible from the site menu (Story) and summarized on the home page with its key numbers.
items.i2: ✨ A showcase that shows the real product — The welcome page now opens on a live animated conversation (draft approval, weather card, multi-agent search), a verified-numbers band (agents, tools, tests, versions) and a clearer side-by-side view of the two execution modes. Every figure was re-checked against the code — including 7 AI providers, not 8 — in all six languages.
items.i3: 🔓 Public pages accessible again without an account — Logged-out visitors opening Philosophy, Technical, Blog or FAQ were silently sent back to the login page after a few seconds. Fixed — and a guard test now prevents this bug from ever coming back.

v1_25_12.title: v1.25.12 — ⚡ Six everyday quick wins: search, understand, act

items.i1: 🔍 History search finally complete — accents no longer matter (« reunion » finds « réunion »), matches are highlighted in the bubbles with a result counter, and a « Search entire history » button digs through everything ever said — click a result to jump right to that moment, then « Back to present ». The search is now available on mobile too.
items.i2: ⚙ The backstage survives a reload — the « N steps · X s » line under each response (what LIA actually did) used to vanish when the page closed. It is now saved with the message: you will find it after a reload and on your other devices.
items.i3: 🔌 « Reconnect » shows up whenever needed — when a connected service breaks, the repair banner appeared only at the exact moment of failure; later attempts just said « no connector ». The banner now returns every time the broken service is the missing one.
items.i4: 👍👎 Rate any response — two discreet thumbs next to Copy. Your verdict is remembered across devices and feeds LIA's understanding of you; a 👎 opens an optional « what went wrong? » line. LIA never regenerates an answer without you asking.
items.i5: 🗂️ The briefing becomes a cockpit — the dashboard cards are now clickable: a mail opens the chat prefilled with « Summarize this email and draft a reply », a meeting with « Prepare me for… », a birthday with a message suggestion. Nothing is sent until you press Enter.
items.i6: 🪞 « What LIA understands about you » surfaced — the compiled portrait gets a shortcut at the top of Identity & Memory in Settings, and a discreet dashboard line when it was freshly refined.
items.i7: 🤫 A quieter chat header — the permanently pulsing « Online » badge is gone (only « offline » and « processing » remain), and the token totals moved into the context gauge's tooltip, freeing a full line.

getting_started.title: Getting Started
getting_started.description: How to get started with LIA

q1.question: What is LIA?
q1.answer:
LIA (Learning Intelligent Assistant) is your personal intelligent assistant powered by artificial intelligence. LIA helps you daily with:

• Managing your emails: search, read, send, reply and forward
• Organizing your calendar: create, modify and view your events
• Managing your contacts: search, create and update
• Managing your tasks: create, track and complete your to-dos
• Exploring your files: search and read your Drive documents
• Getting information: weather, Wikipedia, web search, places

LIA understands natural language: talk to it like you would a human assistant!

q2.question: How do I start a conversation with LIA?
q2.answer:
It's simple in 3 steps:

1. Click on Chat in the left menu
2. Type your message in the input box at the bottom of the screen
3. Press Enter to send

💡 Tip: Be natural! LIA understands phrases like "Show me my emails from this week" or "What do I have scheduled tomorrow?"

q3.question: Does LIA support multiple languages?
q3.answer:
Yes! LIA supports 6 languages:

🇫🇷 French (Français)
🇬🇧 English
🇪🇸 Spanish (Español)
🇩🇪 German (Deutsch)
🇮🇹 Italian (Italiano)
🇨🇳 Simplified Chinese (简体中文)

To change language:
• Click the globe icon 🌐 in the title bar
• Or go to Settings > Appearance > Language

LIA will respond in the interface language.

q5.question: How does the approval system work?
q5.answer:
To protect your data, LIA uses an intelligent approval system (Human-in-the-Loop). Before any action that modifies your data, LIA asks for confirmation:

🔒 Actions requiring approval:
• Send, reply to or forward an email
• Create, modify or delete an event
• Create, modify or delete a contact
• Create or complete a task

📋 How it works:
1. LIA prepares a draft of the action
2. You see a detailed preview of what will be done
3. You can:
• ✅ Approve: the action is executed
• ✏️ Edit: correct before validation
• ❌ Cancel: nothing is done

💡 Tip: Take time to review the preview, especially for emails!

q6.question: Can LIA make mistakes?
q6.answer:
Like any AI assistant, LIA may sometimes misinterpret a request. Here's how to get the best results:

✅ Best practices:
• Be specific: "Send an email to john.smith@email.com" rather than "Send an email to John"
• Give context: "Find my emails from this week about the Alpha project"
• Review previews before approving actions

⚠️ If there's an error:
• Rephrase your request with more details
• Use specific dates ("January 15") rather than relative ones ("last week")
• For important emails, always review the preview

🛡️ Built-in security:
Thanks to the approval system, no critical action is executed without your explicit validation.

q7.question: How was LIA built?
q7.answer:
Nearly 100% of LIA's code is written by an AI, under human direction: written engineering rules, blocking automated checks, a review cycle where the human decides, and recurring adversarial audits (latest assessment: 8.3/10 across 24 areas — full report).

The full story — method, trade-offs, operations and what remains to be done — is on the Story page, and the source code is open on GitHub.

q8.question: Can I install LIA like an app on my phone or computer? (v1.25.16)
q8.answer: Yes. LIA is a PWA: on Android/desktop Chrome, use « Install » (LIA suggests it discreetly after a few visits); on iOS Safari, « Share → Add to Home Screen ». You get a home-screen icon, shortcuts (chat, briefing) and — once installed — the system share menu can send text or links straight into a LIA chat draft. Everything is localized in the 6 languages. Since the unified service worker landed, LIA also shows a proper branded page when you are offline and loads faster thanks to smart asset caching — your personal data is never cached on disk.

q1.question: Can I have multiple conversations at the same time?
q1.answer:
LIA works with one active conversation. This design choice allows:

• A coherent context: LIA remembers the entire conversation
• Natural references: "the first email", "the previous contact"
• A smooth experience: no need to juggle between windows

To start fresh:
Click the New conversation button (🗑️ icon). Warning: this deletes the current history.

q2.question: How do I reset a conversation?
q2.answer:
To clear history and start over:

1. In the chat, find the button with the 🗑️ icon in the header
2. Click it
3. Confirm deletion

⚠️ Warning: This action is irreversible. All conversation history will be permanently deleted.

💡 When to reset?
• When you completely change topics
• If LIA seems confused by previous context
• For privacy reasons

q3.question: Are conversations saved?

Yes, your conversations are automatically saved:

• Real-time sync: each message is recorded instantly
• Multi-device: access your conversation from any device
• Persistence: find your conversation even after logging out

📱 Multi-device tip:
You can start a conversation on your computer and continue on mobile (and vice-versa).

q4.question: How do I use line breaks in my messages?

Two keyboard shortcuts to know:

• Enter = Send the message
• Shift + Enter = New line (line break)

💡 Practical example:
To send a structured email, type:

Send an email to John:
Subject: Project meeting
Body:
Hello John,

I confirm our meeting tomorrow.

Best regards

Use Shift+Enter between each line, then Enter to send.

q5.question: Does LIA remember the conversation context?
q5.answer:
Yes! LIA maintains an intelligent context throughout the conversation:

🔗 Contextual references:
• "Show my emails from John" → finds 3 emails
• "Reply to the second one" → LIA knows you're talking about the 2nd email
• "Add Sophie in CC" → LIA remembers the draft in progress

📋 What LIA remembers:
• Previous search results
• Contacts, emails, events mentioned
• Drafts awaiting approval
• The conversation thread

💡 Tip: Use natural references like "the first one", "Mary's one", "tomorrow's appointment".

q6.question: Why does LIA sometimes take time to respond?
q6.answer:
Response time varies based on your request's complexity:

⚡ Fast responses (1-3 seconds):
• Simple conversation questions
• Weather information
• Wikipedia searches

⏱️ Medium responses (3-10 seconds):
• Searching your emails
• Calendar consultation
• Contact search

🔄 Longer responses (10-30 seconds):
• Creating complex emails
• Combined multiple searches
• Actions requiring multiple steps

💡 Visual indicators:
During processing, you'll see messages like "🔍 Analyzing your request..." or "📋 Preparing action plan..."

The display itself is alive: past steps dim while the current one gently pulses, the block fades into the first words of the reply, a caret blinks while the answer streams, and the waiting animation changes shape with every reply. If you switch tabs while LIA works, the tab title alternates with “✦ LIA is writing…”. Everything respects your system's reduce-motion preference.

q7.question: How do I get better results with LIA?
q7.answer:
Here are the best practices for communicating with LIA:

✅ Be specific:
❌ "Find an email"
✅ "Find emails from Peter about the budget"

✅ Give context:
❌ "Send an email"
✅ "Send an email to mary@example.com to confirm the meeting tomorrow at 2pm"

✅ Use specific dates:
❌ "The meeting the other day"
✅ "The meeting on January 15"

✅ Proceed step by step:
For complex tasks, break down into multiple requests.

✅ Check previews:
Before approving an email or modification, carefully review the preview.

q8.question: How do I attach photos or documents to my messages?
q8.answer:
Two ways to attach files:

📎 Paperclip button:
Click the 📎 button to the left of the input area to browse your files.

🖱️ Drag and drop:
Drag files directly from your file explorer into the input area. A visual outline appears to confirm the drop zone.

📁 Accepted formats:
• Photos (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, HEIC) — automatically compressed
• PDF documents — text is automatically extracted

Thumbnails are displayed in the conversation. Click a thumbnail to enlarge it. LIA can analyze the visual content of images and the text of PDFs to answer your questions.

💡 Limits: maximum 5 attachments per message, 10 MB per image, 20 MB per document.

q9.question: What is the /resume command?
q9.answer:
The /resume command triggers intelligent context compaction:

What it does:
• Summarizes old conversation history using AI
• Preserves critical identifiers (names, emails, IDs)
• Frees up context window space for longer conversations

When to use it:
• When your conversation has been going on for a long time
• When LIA seems to lose track of earlier context
• When you want to "reset" the context without losing important information

How it works:
1. Type /resume in the chat
2. LIA summarizes old messages into a concise recap
3. Recent messages are preserved intact
4. LIA confirms the compaction with a brief summary

💡 While compaction runs:
• A toast appears at the top of the screen reading "Summarizing the conversation…"
• The input area is locked automatically while the summary completes
• When done, the toast morphs into a confirmation "Conversation summarized — N tokens freed"
• If the summary cannot complete (LLM outage, timeout), an explicit fallback cleanly truncates the older history with a visible notice rather than a silent loss

📊 Persistent indicator: A discreet pill in the chat header (next to the search box) continuously shows your tokens/threshold usage as a coloured ring — you can see at any moment when the next compaction will fire.

💡 Note: Compaction also triggers automatically when the conversation becomes very long. The /resume command lets you force it at any time.

q10.question: What is the difference between Pipeline (🔀) and ReAct (⚡) mode?
q10.answer:
LIA offers two execution modes, switchable via the 🔀/⚡ toggle in the chat header:

🔀 Pipeline mode (default)
LIA plans all steps upfront, validates them, then executes tools in parallel. This is the fastest and most economical mode: it consumes 4 to 8 times fewer tokens than ReAct mode.

⚡ ReAct mode
LIA reasons step by step: it calls a tool, analyzes the result, then autonomously decides what to do next. More adaptable and autonomous, but consumes significantly more tokens.

💡 When to use which mode?
• Pipeline (🔀): for most requests — emails, calendar, weather, contacts, tasks...
• ReAct (⚡): for exploratory research, complex multi-step questions, or when you need LIA to adapt in real time to results.

⚠️ Cost warning: ReAct mode consumes 4 to 8× more tokens. Reserve it for requests where the added value justifies the extra cost.

q11.question: How do I copy a message, code, and are math formulas rendered correctly?
q11.answer:
Since v1.16.9, the chat has several useful finishing touches:

📋 Copy button on messages and code
• Hover over a LIA reply or a code block → a "Copy" button appears
• Text is copied as-is to your clipboard, with visual confirmation

🎨 Syntax highlighting on code
• Code blocks ```python, ```typescript, ```json, ```bash, ```sql... are auto-colored (25 languages)
• Light or dark theme based on your display preferences

🧮 Math formulas (LaTeX)
• Formulas are rendered with proper mathematical notation
• Inline: $E = mc^2$
• Centered block: $$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$

📅 Relative dates
• Today's messages: time only (14:30)
• Yesterday's: "Yesterday 14:30"
• This week: weekday + time (Monday 14:30)
• Beyond: full date

q12.question: Can I search through my conversation history?
q12.answer:
Yes, since v1.16.9:

🔍 Search bar in the chat
• A search input now appears in the chat header (🔍 icon)
• Type a word or phrase → matching messages are filtered instantly
• Search is case-insensitive ("pizza" also finds "Pizza")

💡 Current limitations
• Searches through messages that are currently loaded in the chat — by default the last 50, but you can load more by scrolling up (see the next question)
• Accent-sensitive ("reunion" won't find "réunion")
• Click ✕ to clear the search and see all messages again

🎯 When to use it?
Find an address, a name, a decision or a detail mentioned earlier in the conversation without scrolling.

q13.question: How do I access older messages in a very long conversation?
q13.answer:
Since v1.20.14, you can scroll up in the chat to reach the beginning of any conversation, even one that has grown to thousands of messages:

📜 How it works
• When you open a conversation, the 50 newest messages are loaded instantly
• Scroll up in the chat — as soon as you reach the top, the previous 50 messages load automatically
• A small "Loading older messages…" indicator appears briefly at the top during each fetch
• Repeat as needed — you can scroll all the way back to the very first message

✨ What stays smooth
• Your reading position is preserved — the viewport stays exactly where you were, the new content slides in above without jumping
• Duplicates are filtered out, so no message ever appears twice

📌 Good to know
• Messages are always preserved in the database — nothing is ever lost, even after compaction (which only summarises older messages for the AI's working memory, not the displayed history)
• The in-chat search continues to filter on what's currently loaded, so loading more messages also expands the searchable scope
• Returning to the conversation later, switching tabs, or running a scheduled action all reload the newest page from scratch — so you start fresh at the bottom

q14.question: What happens if I leave the page while LIA is answering?
q14.answer:
Nothing is lost. Generation continues in the background on the server: your message and the full answer are saved even if you close the tab, switch apps or lose the connection.

When you come back to the chat while the answer is still being written, it resumes live automatically — the in-progress bubble rebuilds itself and keeps streaming (this also works with several tabs open).

You can also stop an in-progress answer: while LIA is writing, the send button becomes a Stop button. The partial text is kept and marked "interrupted" ⏸ — but note that actions already performed (a sent email, a created event…) are not undone.

Only one answer runs at a time per conversation: if you try to send another message during a generation, LIA reattaches you to the answer in progress.

q15.question: How do I approve or cancel an action LIA proposes?
q15.answer:
When LIA is about to do something sensitive (send an email, delete an event, validate a draft…), an approval card appears above the input with Confirm and Cancel buttons — and Modify for drafts, which lets you describe the change to make.

It's a single click, but you can also reply by text or voice as before (“yes, send it” / “no, cancel”): both work in parallel. Once the action is handled, the card disappears and LIA's reply confirms what was done.

q16.question: Can I see what LIA did to produce an answer?
q16.answer:
Yes. Under each answer, a small “⚙ N steps · X s” line summarizes the backstage; one click expands it to show what LIA actually did — the routing, the tools it called, and its reasoning — grouped by category.

It's the same transparency as the cost shown on every message, extended to the flow of actions. The display stays discreet and collapsed by default, so it never clutters the conversation.

Since v1.25.12 this trace is stored with the message: you will find it after a reload and on your other devices (the live reasoning stream itself stays ephemeral).

q17.question: How do I search my entire conversation history?
q17.answer:
Type in the search field of the chat header (or tap the 🔍 icon on mobile). The loaded messages filter instantly — accent-insensitive — with the matches highlighted in the bubbles and a result counter.

If older history exists, a « Search entire history » button queries the server across everything ever said and lists dated results; clicking one jumps to that moment of the conversation, and a banner offers « Back to present » at any time. Sending a new message automatically returns you to the present first.

q18.question: What are the 👍/👎 under the responses for?
q18.answer:
Two discreet thumbs appear next to the Copy button on ordinary responses. Your verdict is saved with the message (you will find it on your other devices) and feeds LIA's understanding: it strengthens or weakens the personal observations that shaped that answer. A 👎 unfolds an optional one-line « what went wrong? » field, recorded as a correction.

You can change your mind — the latest verdict wins. And LIA never regenerates an answer on its own: you stay in charge.

q19.question: Can LIA prepare me before talking to someone? (v1.25.13)
q19.answer:
Yes — ask « prepare my call with Marie » and one pass gathers a 360° view: her contact card, your recent email exchanges, your upcoming shared meetings, and what LIA remembers about her. If a source is unavailable (no calendar connector, for instance), the overview says so honestly instead of guessing.

It also powers the meeting-prep nudge: when a substantial meeting is close, a proactive notification may end with « want me to prepare this meeting for you? ».

q20.question: What are the « / » slash commands? (v1.25.16)
q20.answer: Type / at the start of an empty message to open the command menu: /resume (compact the conversation), /briefing (open the dashboard), /agenda, /search, plus everyday shortcuts — unread emails, weather, weekend weather, tasks, reminders, news — and your dialogue-enabled skills. Filtering understands your language (typing « mété » finds the weather). A command only pre-fills the input: nothing is ever sent without you pressing Enter.

q21.question: Does my typed message survive a refresh? Can I recall what I sent? (v1.25.16)
q21.answer: Yes. Your draft is saved per account as you type and restored after a refresh or navigation (it is cleared when you send, and purged at logout). In an empty input, ↑ walks back through your last 10 sent messages and ↓ walks forward to an empty field — like a terminal. Under every answer, an action row offers copy, feedback (👍/👎) and the execution details (« N steps · X s »).

q22.question: The thread no longer jumps while I re-read — how does it work? (v1.25.16)
q22.answer: When you scroll up to re-read, a streaming answer never drags you back to the bottom. A floating button appears with a counter of the responses that arrived off-screen; one tap brings you back. Sending a message still jumps to it, as expected. Under the latest answer, up to 3 follow-up suggestions may appear as chips: tapping one fills the input (never sends).

q9.question: How does long-term memory work?
q9.answer:
LIA learns about you through its intelligent memory:

🧠 What LIA remembers:

• Personal information: "His birthday is March 15"
• Relationships: "Mary is his sister", "John is his colleague"
• Significant events: "He changed jobs recently"
• Habits: "She exercises on Tuesday evenings"
• Sensitive areas: topics to approach with care

🔄 Automatic extraction:
LIA analyzes your conversations and automatically extracts relevant information in the background.

🔍 Hybrid search:
LIA uses hybrid search combining keywords (BM25) and meaning (semantic) to retrieve your relevant memories with optimal accuracy.

📊 Usage:
These memories personalize LIA's responses. For example, LIA will say "Hello Mary" to your sister without you specifying.

🛡️ Full control:
View, edit, pin or delete your memories in Settings > Memory.

q10.question: How do I manage my stored memories?
q10.answer:
You have full control over what LIA remembers:

📋 View your memories:
Go to Settings > Long-term Memory to see everything LIA has remembered.

✏️ Edit a memory:
• Click the edit button
• Correct the content or category
• Adjust usage nuances

📌 Pin a memory:
Pinned memories are protected from automatic cleanup. Useful for important information.

🗑️ Delete:
• Delete individually or in bulk
• Option to keep pinned memories

📤 Export:
Export all your memories for backup (GDPR compliance).

🔄 Automatic cleanup:
Unpinned memories are automatically purged based on a retention score (importance, recency and actual usage) to keep the system relevant.

⚠️ Forgetting risk:
Memories close to being automatically forgotten are flagged in the list, so you can pin the ones that matter in time.

q11.question: How do I configure my geolocation and home address?

Your address is stored securely and only used for your proximity queries.

q12.question: How does LIA resolve relational references?

✏️ Customize relationships:

💡 Tip:
Mention your relationships naturally in conversations: "My colleague Sophie sent me a file".

• Track your usage in real-time

📱 Note:

q14.question: Which languages are supported for voice transcription?

q15.question: Voice mode isn't working, what should I do?
q15.answer:
Here are solutions to common voice mode issues:

🎤 Microphone problem:
1. Check that your browser has permission to use the microphone
2. Click the 🔒 icon to the left of the URL to see permissions
3. Allow the microphone if blocked

🌐 Unsupported browser:
Voice mode requires a modern browser:
• ✅ Chrome 92+
• ✅ Firefox 79+
• ✅ Safari 15.2+
• ✅ Edge 92+
• ❌ Internet Explorer (not supported)

🔒 Security headers:
Voice mode uses advanced features (SharedArrayBuffer) that require security headers. If you see a "crossOriginIsolated" error, contact the administrator.

🔇 Wake word not detected:
• Say "OK Guy" or "OK Guys" clearly
• Avoid noisy environments
• Get closer to the microphone
• Use Push-to-Talk (click the overlay) as an alternative

⏱️ Slow transcription:
The first transcription may take 2-3 seconds (model loading). Subsequent ones are faster (~500ms).

q16.question: How do I export my consumption data?
q16.answer:
You can export your personal LLM and Google API consumption as CSV files:

📥 To export:
1. Go to Settings > Features
2. Open the My Consumption Export section
3. Choose a date range (current month, last month, last 30 days, or all time)
4. Click Download CSV on the export you want

📊 Three export types:
• LLM Token Usage — Detailed per-call breakdown (model, tokens, cost)
• Google API Usage — Detailed per-call breakdown (API, endpoint, cost)
• My Summary — Aggregated totals (tokens, calls, costs)

🔒 Security:
You can only export your own data. It is not possible to access other users' consumption data.

q17.question: Can I customize the dashboard cards? (v1.25.16)

q18.question: What is the « Open loops » section? (v1.25.16)

Settings → « Open loops » lists them by direction (you owe / you are waiting), with three one-tap actions: Done, Relaunch in chat (pre-fills a follow-up message) or No longer relevant. Nothing is created manually — the ledger's value is being automatic.

q1.question: What is a connector?
q1.answer:
A connector is a secure gateway between LIA and your external services:

🔌 Types of connectors:

Google Services (OAuth):
• 📧 Gmail: read, send, reply to emails
• 📅 Calendar: manage your events
• 👥 Contacts: search and create contacts
• 📁 Drive: explore your files
• ✅ Tasks: manage your tasks
• 📍 Places: search for locations
• 🗺️ Routes: directions and routes

Apple iCloud services (app-specific password):
• 📮 Apple Mail: read, send, reply to emails (IMAP/SMTP)
• 🗓️ Apple Calendar: manage your iCloud events (CalDAV)
• 📇 Apple Contacts: search and create iCloud contacts (CardDAV)

Microsoft 365 services (OAuth):
• 📧 Outlook: read, send, reply to emails
• 📅 Microsoft Calendar: manage your events
• 👥 Microsoft Contacts: search and manage contacts
• ✅ Microsoft To Do: manage tasks and lists

External services (API key):
• 🌤️ OpenWeatherMap: weather and forecasts
• 📚 Wikipedia: encyclopedic search
• 🔍 Perplexity: AI web search
• 🦁 Brave Search: web and news enrichment

Smart Home (hybrid auth):
• 💡 Philips Hue: control lights, rooms, and scenes

Telephony (bring-your-own):
• 📞 ElevenLabs Telephony: LIA places outbound phone calls on your behalf — see the dedicated Phone Calls section

🔒 Security:
Each connector has limited permissions. LIA only accesses necessary data.

⚡ Mutual exclusivity:
For email, calendar, and contacts, only one provider can be active at a time (Google OR Apple OR Microsoft, not both simultaneously). Tasks are available via Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do (one at a time).

q2.question: How do I connect Google services?
q2.answer:
Google services use OAuth 2.0 (secure connection):

Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. Find the desired service (Gmail, Calendar, etc.)
3. Click Connect
4. A Google window opens
5. Select your Google account
6. Accept the requested permissions
7. You're redirected to LIA - the connector is active!

🔐 Permissions:
LIA only requests necessary permissions. For example, for Gmail: reading and sending emails, but not permanent deletion.

💡 Tip:
You can revoke access at any time from LIA settings or from your Google account.

q3.question: How do I connect external services (API key)?
q3.answer:
Some services require a personal API key:

🌤️ OpenWeatherMap (free):
1. Create an account at openweathermap.org
2. Get your free API key
3. In LIA: Settings > Connectors > OpenWeatherMap
4. Paste your key and click Activate

🔍 Perplexity (paid):
1. Create an account at perplexity.ai
2. Subscribe to an API plan
3. Get your API key
4. Activate in LIA as above

📚 Wikipedia:
No key required! Wikipedia is free and directly accessible.

🔒 Key security:
Your API keys are stored securely and encrypted.

q4.question: How do I disconnect a service?
q4.answer:
To revoke LIA's access to a service:

Disconnection from LIA:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. Find the service to disconnect
3. Click Disconnect
4. Confirm disconnection

⚠️ Consequences:
• LIA will no longer be able to access this service
• Your data remains intact with the provider (Google, etc.)
• You can reconnect at any time

🔐 Double security (Google):
For Google services, you can also revoke access from:
• myaccount.google.com/permissions
• This disconnects LIA immediately

q5.question: Why is a connector showing an error?
q5.answer:
Several reasons can explain a connector error:

🔄 Expired token:
Solution: Click Reconnect to refresh the authorization.

🚫 Permissions revoked:
If you revoked access from Google, reconnect.

🔑 Invalid API key:
For API key services, verify your key is correct and active.

⏱️ Quota exceeded:
Some services have usage limits. Wait or upgrade to a higher plan.

🌐 Network issue:
Check your internet connection and try again.

💡 General solution:
Disconnect then reconnect the service. This solves most problems.

q6.question: Can I configure preferences per connector?
q6.answer:
Yes! Some connectors have customizable preferences:

📅 Google Calendar:
• Default calendar: where to create new events
• Example: "Work", "Personal", "Family"
• LIA will use this calendar unless specified otherwise

✅ Google Tasks:
• Default task list: where to create new tasks
• Example: "My main list", "Projects", "Shopping"

📍 Google Places:
• Home address: your default address for "near me" searches
• Automatic geolocation: send your position for accurate results
• Configure both in Settings > Connectors > Google Places

🌐 Browser Geolocation:
• In Google Places settings, enable the geolocation toggle
• Your browser will ask for permission the first time
• Position used for local weather and "near me" searches

To configure:
1. Go to Settings (⚙️ icon in the menu)
2. Open the Connectors section
3. Find the relevant connector (Calendar, Tasks, or Places)
4. Configure the specific preferences for that connector

💡 Tip:
These preferences save you time by not having to specify the calendar, list, or city each time.

q8.question: Are connectors secure?
q8.answer:
Security is our top priority:

🔐 Google services — OAuth 2.0:
• LIA never sees your Google passwords
• You connect directly with Google
• Tokens revocable at any time

🍎 Apple services — App-specific password:
• Uses an application-specific password (not your Apple password)
• Encrypted before database storage
• Revocable from appleid.apple.com
• Apple two-factor authentication is required

🪟 Microsoft 365 — OAuth 2.0:
• LIA never sees your Microsoft passwords
• You connect directly with Microsoft
• Tokens revocable at any time from your Microsoft account
• Limited permissions (Microsoft Graph API)

🔒 Minimal permissions:
• Each connector only requests necessary permissions
• No excessive access to your data

🗄️ Secure storage:
• OAuth tokens and app-specific passwords encrypted in database
• API keys stored securely
• No plaintext storage

🔄 Automatic refresh:
• Google and Microsoft tokens expire regularly and are renewed automatically
• Apple app-specific passwords don't expire (unless Apple ID password changes)

📋 Audit and logs:
• All actions are tracked
• Usage history available

q9.question: How do I connect Apple iCloud services?
q9.answer:
Apple iCloud services use an app-specific password:

Prerequisites:
• An Apple account with two-factor authentication enabled
• Generate an app-specific password from appleid.apple.com

Steps:
1. Go to Settings > Connectors
2. In the Apple iCloud section, click Connect
3. Enter your Apple ID (email)
4. Enter the app-specific password (format xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx)
5. Select the services to activate (Email, Calendar, Contacts)
6. Click Test connection to verify
7. Click Activate

⚠️ Mutual exclusivity:
Activating an Apple service automatically deactivates its Google equivalent (and vice versa). For example, activating Apple Mail will deactivate Gmail.

🔐 Security:
Your app-specific password is encrypted and never exposed. You can revoke it at any time from your Apple account.

q10.question: What Apple iCloud services can I connect?

💡 Same experience:

q11.question: What is connector mutual exclusivity?
q11.answer:
For email, calendar, contacts, and tasks services, LIA applies a mutual exclusivity rule:

⚡ Principle:
Only one provider can be active per category:
• Email: Gmail OR Apple Mail OR Outlook (not multiple)
• Calendar: Google Calendar OR Apple Calendar OR Microsoft Calendar (not multiple)
• Contacts: Google Contacts OR Apple Contacts OR Microsoft Contacts (not multiple)
• Tasks: Google Tasks OR Microsoft To Do (not both)

🔄 Switching providers:
If you activate a new provider while another is active for the same category:
1. The previous service becomes inactive (not deleted)
2. The new service becomes active
3. Your data remains intact with each provider
4. You can switch back at any time

✅ Unaffected services:
Google Drive, Places, Routes, and Philips Hue have no equivalent in other providers and remain always available.

💡 Tip:
You don't need to choose the same provider for everything. For example, you can use Outlook for emails, Google Calendar for your calendar, and Microsoft To Do for tasks.

q12.question: How do I connect Microsoft 365 services?
q12.answer:
Microsoft 365 services use OAuth 2.0 (secure connection via Microsoft Identity Platform):

Steps:

2. In the Microsoft 365 section, click Connect All or select an individual service
3. A Microsoft login window opens
4. Sign in with your Microsoft account
5. Accept the requested permissions
6. You're redirected back to LIA — the connector is active!

🔐 Permissions:
LIA only requests necessary permissions via the Microsoft Graph API. For example, for Outlook: reading and sending emails, but not permanent deletion.

⚠️ Mutual exclusivity:
Activating a Microsoft service automatically deactivates its Google or Apple equivalent for the same category (and vice versa).

💡 Tip:
You can revoke access at any time from LIA settings or from account.microsoft.com.

q13.question: What Microsoft 365 services can I connect?

LIA integrates with 4 Microsoft 365 services:

q14.question: How do I connect Philips Hue?
q14.answer:
Philips Hue uses hybrid authentication (local press-link or remote OAuth2):

telephony.title: Phone Calls
telephony.description: LIA can place real phone calls on your behalf. Complete setup guide (Twilio + ElevenLabs) and everyday use.

q1.question: What can LIA do on the phone?
q1.answer:
LIA can place a real outbound phone call for you, pursue the goal you set, and report back in the chat.

Examples:
• "Call the bakery and ask if they have a cake for Saturday"
• "Call the garage to check if the car is ready"
• "Call Marie and ask if she's free Tuesday evening"

During the call, LIA introduces itself as an assistant calling on your behalf, holds a natural conversation toward your objective, then hangs up and writes you a summary — with a one-tap follow-up action when relevant (for example, creating the event that was just agreed).

💡 Good to know: LIA only places outgoing calls — it never answers your incoming calls.

q2.question: How does a call work, step by step?
q2.answer:
1. You ask in the chat
"Call Dr. Martin's office and ask for an appointment this week"

2. LIA asks for your confirmation
Before dialing anything, LIA shows you a confirmation card: who it will call, which number, and why. Nothing happens without your explicit approval.

3. The call takes place
LIA's voice agent makes the call from your number and works toward the objective. You can keep chatting with LIA — or close the app — in the meantime.

4. The summary arrives in the chat
A written summary is delivered asynchronously, with a suggested follow-up action when there is something to do next. Every call also appears in your call history (Settings > Connectors > Telephony).

q3.question: What do I need before starting?
q3.answer:
Phone calls use your own accounts with two external services — LIA adds no charge of its own:

1. 📞 A Twilio account — provides the phone number LIA calls from (number rental + per-minute pricing).

2. 🎙️ An ElevenLabs account — provides the voice agent that speaks during the call (requires access to the Agents platform; call minutes consume your plan's credits).

3. ✅ The feature enabled by your administrator — if you don't see a Telephony block in Settings > Connectors, ask your administrator to enable it.

The full setup takes about 15 minutes (plus possible validation delays for a French number) and follows 4 steps, each detailed in the next questions:
1. Get a phone number (Twilio)
2. Prepare ElevenLabs (API key + number import)
3. Configure the return webhook
4. Activate the connector in LIA

q4.question: Step 1 — Get a phone number (Twilio)
q4.answer:
Twilio is the operator that provides the number LIA calls from.

1. Create the account
Sign up at twilio.com and upgrade to a paid account (the free trial only calls verified numbers).

2. 🇫🇷 For a French number: submit a Regulatory Bundle
French regulation requires an identity document and a proof of address: Phone Numbers > Regulatory Compliance > Bundles. Human validation takes up to ~3 business days.
• Easiest: a local number (01–05) or national number (09)
• Avoid mobile numbers (06/07): extra requirements and 1–2 weeks of provisioning

3. Buy the number
Phone Numbers > Buy a Number — make sure the Voice capability is checked.

4. Note your credentials
On the Twilio Console dashboard, copy the Account SID and the Auth Token — you will need them in the next step.

💡 Just testing? A US number can be bought instantly, with no regulatory bundle.

q5.question: Step 2 — Prepare ElevenLabs (API key + number)
q5.answer:
ElevenLabs provides the voice agent that speaks during the call.

1. Check your plan
You need a plan with access to the Agents platform. Call minutes consume your ElevenLabs credits (on top of Twilio's per-minute cost).

2. Create an API key
Profile (bottom left) > API Keys > create a key. If you restrict its permissions, it needs at least read/write access to the Agents platform (LIA creates its agent, lists your numbers, and triggers outbound calls). A full-access key works fine to start — you can restrict it after your first successful call.

3. Import your Twilio number
Agents Platform > Phone Numbers > Import from Twilio: enter the number in international format (e.g. +33612345678), the Account SID, the Auth Token, and a label.

⚠️ Two important points:
• Use the native Twilio import, not a SIP trunk — LIA triggers calls through ElevenLabs' Twilio integration.
• Do not create an agent yourself: LIA automatically provisions its own secured agent when you activate the connector (it will appear in your workspace as "LIA telephony — your name").

q6.question: Step 3 — Configure the return webhook
q6.answer:
The webhook is the channel through which the call report comes back into your chat. Without it, calls go out but no summary ever returns.

1. Open the webhooks settings
In the ElevenLabs Agents workspace settings, open the Webhooks section (only a workspace admin can do this).

2. Create a post-call webhook
• Event type: post_call_transcription (transcription only)
• URL: the address LIA shows you at step 3 of its wizard, with a copy button — it looks like https://your-lia-domain/api/v1/telephony/webhook
• Authentication: HMAC

3. Copy the signing secret
ElevenLabs generates a signing secret when the webhook is created — copy it immediately, you will paste it into LIA in the next step.

🔒 Leave "Send audio data" disabled: LIA never receives nor stores any audio — that is a design guarantee.

q7.question: Step 4 — Activate the connector in LIA
q7.answer:
Everything now comes together in LIA, in a 3-step wizard.

Go to Settings > Connectors > Telephony and click Connect. A notice reminds you that calls are billed on your own ElevenLabs/Twilio accounts.

Step 1 — API key
Paste your ElevenLabs API key and click Validate. LIA checks the key and lists the phone numbers of your workspace. ("No numbers" means the Twilio import from Step 2 is missing.)

Step 2 — Number
Pick the number LIA will call from.

Step 3 — Webhook
Copy the displayed webhook URL (if you haven't configured it in ElevenLabs yet, do it now — see the previous question), paste the signing secret, and click Activate.

LIA then creates its secured agent in your ElevenLabs workspace and the connector goes active. You're ready to call! 🎉

q8.question: How do I place my first call?
q8.answer:
💡 Recommended first test: have LIA call your own mobile — you'll experience a call from the other side.

1. In the chat: "Call +336XXXXXXXX and ask whether the package has arrived"

2. LIA shows the confirmation card (callee, number, objective) — confirm.

3. Your phone rings: the agent introduces itself as an assistant calling on your behalf, asks its question, and hangs up.

4. The summary appears in the chat a few moments later — asynchronously, so you can chat in the meantime.

You can also target a contact by name ("call Marie…"): LIA looks up the number in your contacts and asks you to disambiguate if several match. The call history lives in Settings > Connectors > Telephony.

q9.question: Is it private? Can LIA reveal my calendar or record the call?
q9.answer:
Privacy is enforced by design, not by instructions:

• 🔒 Read-only, free/busy only — during a call LIA can check whether you're free or busy at a given time, but never reveals your event titles, participants, locations or any content. The call agent simply has no access to that data.
• 🚫 No recording — the call is not recorded.
• 🗑️ No stored transcript — the full conversation is never saved; only a short summary is kept, and it expires automatically (30 days by default).
• 📢 Transparent disclosure — the agent always introduces itself as an assistant calling on your behalf; it never pretends to be you.
• ✅ You stay in control — every call is confirmed by you before it is placed.

q10.question: Can the assistant accept an extra or commit to an expense for me?
q10.answer: No, never. The assistant operates under a strict mandate: it can only act within the exact scope of your request. If the person offers an extra, an option, a price change or any unplanned commitment (even a small one, like a 3€ cheese topping on a pizza), it neither accepts nor declines on your behalf: it notes the exact offer and its price, explains that it cannot confirm by itself, and announces a call-back to confirm. You then find everything in the call summary — every cost with its amount, every open point — and LIA asks you how to proceed. If you wish, just request a new call with your instructions ("call back and accept the cheese topping").

q11.question: How much does it cost?
q11.answer:
LIA adds no charge of its own — costs go to your two external accounts:

📞 Twilio
• Number rental: ~1–15 €/month depending on the type
• Outbound minutes: per-minute rate based on the destination

🎙️ ElevenLabs
• Agent call minutes, taken from your plan's credits

🤖 LIA
• No surcharge, no markup — only the small LLM synthesis of your summary appears in your LIA usage statistics.

🛡️ Built-in guardrails against surprises:
• One active call at a time
• Hourly call cap per user (10/hour by default)
• Hard cap on call duration (10 minutes by default)

q12.question: It doesn't work — what should I check?
q12.answer:
"Invalid key" at step 1
→ The key is mistyped or lacks permissions (Agents platform access required).

"No numbers" after validating the key
→ Your number isn't imported into the ElevenLabs Agents workspace, or was imported as a SIP trunk instead of the native Twilio integration.

The call goes out but no summary comes back
→ The webhook is the issue: URL not publicly reachable, wrong signing secret, or wrong event type (it must be post_call_transcription).

"A call is already in progress"
→ Only one active call at a time, by design. A stuck call is automatically cleaned up after ~15 minutes.

Calls refused after several in a row
→ You've hit the hourly cap (10 calls/hour by default).

Still stuck? Ask your administrator: the server logs state precisely which webhook events were received and why any were ignored.

q8.question: How do I view my calendar events?

📋 Information displayed:

q9.question: How do I create a calendar event?

q10.question: How do I modify or delete an event?

Google Calendar - Modification and deletion:

q11.question: How do I search my Google Drive files?

q12.question: How do I read a Drive file?

Google Drive - Reading content:

q13.question: How do I manage my tasks?

Google Tasks / Microsoft To Do - Task management:

➕ Create a task:

q14.question: What is the draft and approval system?
q14.answer:
To protect your data, any modification action goes through a draft system:

🔒 How it works:
1. You request an action ("Send an email to John")
2. LIA prepares a draft
3. You see a detailed preview
4. Three options:
• ✅ Approve: the action is executed
• ✏️ Edit: correct the draft
• ❌ Cancel: nothing is done

📋 Actions concerned:
• Sending, replying, forwarding emails
• Creating, modifying, deleting events
• Creating, modifying contacts
• Creating, completing tasks
• Deleting emails

🛡️ Benefits:
• Verification before every important action
• Ability to correct errors
• Full control over your data
• No irreversible action without your agreement

q15.question: How do I use contextual references?

📌 By context:

q16.question: What do the colors on email cards mean?
q16.answer:
Gmail - Email color coding:

Email cards use a colored border on the left side to indicate their status:

📧 Color code:
• No color: Read email (no special marking)
• 🟠 Orange: Read and important email (marked important by Gmail)
• 🟢 Green: Unread email (new message to read)
• 🔴 Red: Unread AND important email (high priority)

💡 Good to know:
• The "important" status is automatically assigned by Gmail based on your habits
• Unread emails also have their subject in bold for better visibility
• The "Unread" badge also appears in the card's metadata

📌 Quick summary:
🟢 Green = To read | 🔴 Red = Urgent | 🟠 Orange = Important already read | Transparent = Already read

tool_examples_external.title: External Services Examples
tool_examples_external.description: How to use Weather, Wikipedia, Perplexity, Web Fetch, Browser Control, Places and Routes

q1.question: How do I get the current weather?
q1.answer:
OpenWeatherMap - Real-time weather:

🌤️ Current weather:
• "What's the weather in Paris?"
• "Current temperature in New York"
• "Is it raining in London?"
• "Weather here" (uses your configured position)

📊 Information provided:

• Conditions (sunny, cloudy, rain...)

• Wind speed and direction
• Visibility
• Sunrise/sunset times

💡 Tip:
Add the OpenWeatherMap connector (free) in Settings > Connectors to enable this feature.

q2.question: How do I get the weather forecast?
q2.answer:
OpenWeatherMap - Detailed forecasts:

📅 Multi-day forecasts:
• "What will the weather be like tomorrow in Lyon?"

• "Will it rain this weekend in Paris?"

⏰ Hourly forecasts:
• "Hourly forecast for today"

📊 What you get:
• Min/max temperature per day
• Precipitation probability
• Expected wind speed
• Condition evolution

💡 Planning:
Useful for planning activities: "What's the best day for a picnic this week?"

q3.question: How do I get Wikipedia information?
q3.answer:
Wikipedia - Get information directly:

✅ GOOD PHRASING (direct information):
• "Who is Elon Musk?"
• "Tell me about the Eiffel Tower"
• "Information about Marie Curie"
• "What is photosynthesis?"

→ LIA gives you directly the article content with a full summary.

⚠️ AVOID (returns a list of articles):
• "Search Wikipedia for..."
• "Find articles about..."

→ These phrasings return a list of links instead of content.

💡 Simple rule:
Ask your question like you would to a friend: "Who is X?", "What is X?", "Tell me about X" rather than "Search for X".

🌍 Multilingual:
LIA automatically chooses the Wikipedia version matching your language.

✅ Free, no configuration required.

q4.question: How do I get the full Wikipedia article?
q4.answer:
Wikipedia - Full article vs summary:

📝 Default: Summary
LIA provides a substantial summary (up to 5000 characters) with essential information.

📖 For the full article:
Ask explicitly:
• "Give me the full article on Napoleon"
• "Detailed Wikipedia article on climate change"
• "I want the entire article on the French Revolution"

🔗 Related topics:
• "What are the articles related to space exploration?"
• "Topics related to the Renaissance"

🔍 When to use search?
Use "search Wikipedia" only if:
• You don't know the exact title
• The topic is ambiguous (multiple homonyms)
• You want to explore different articles

💡 Example:
• "Who is Victor Hugo?" → Direct summary
• "Full article on Victor Hugo" → Detailed article
• "Search Victor Hugo" → List of related articles

q5.question: How do I use Perplexity (Search vs Ask)?
q5.answer:
Perplexity AI - Two modes of use:

🔍 SEARCH MODE (news, web search):
• "Latest news on artificial intelligence"
• "Latest Apple news"
• "Football game results yesterday"
• "Flight prices Paris-Tokyo"

→ Use for: recent news, events, trends, real-time prices.

❓ ASK MODE (complex questions, synthesis):
• "Explain how blockchain works"
• "What are the pros and cons of electric cars?"
• "Compare different machine learning methods"
• "Analyze current real estate market trends"

→ Use for: in-depth analysis, syntheses, comparisons, complex explanations.

💡 How to choose?
• News/Recent facts → "Search...", "News..."
• Complex question → "Explain...", "Analyze...", "Compare..."

📌 Sources and citations:
Perplexity always provides the web sources used for its answers.

⚠️ Configuration required:
Perplexity requires an API key (paid service).

q6.question: When should I use Perplexity vs Wikipedia?
q6.answer:
Choose the right tool based on your needs:

📚 Use WIKIPEDIA for:
• Established historical facts
• Scientific definitions and concepts
• Biographies of notable people
• Geographic information
• Verified encyclopedic content
• ✅ Free, no configuration

🔍 Use PERPLEXITY for:
• Current events and recent news
• Product comparisons and reviews
• Real-time information (prices, schedules)
• Current trends and opinions
• Questions requiring multiple sources
• ⚠️ Requires API key

💡 Concrete example:
• "Who invented the light bulb?" → Wikipedia (historical fact)
• "What's the best LED bulb this year?" → Perplexity (recent comparison)

q7.question: How do I search for places with Google Places?
q7.answer:
Google Places - Location search:

📍 Nearby search:
• "Find restaurants near me"
• "Pharmacies open now"
• "Where is the nearest gas station?"
• "Supermarkets within 1 mile"

📍 Search by area:
• "Italian restaurants in downtown Paris"
• "Hotels near the Eiffel Tower"
• "Museums in central Lyon"

📊 Information displayed:
• Place name and address
• Rating (stars) and number of reviews
• Opening hours
• Phone number
• Distance from your position

💡 Configuration:
For "near me" searches, set your default position in settings or specify the city.

q8.question: How do I get place details?
q8.answer:
Google Places - Detailed information:

📋 Request details:
• "Show me details about the Louvre Museum"
• "Opening hours for Starbucks on Rivoli Street"
• "Phone number for Dr. Martin's office"
• "Reviews for the Marriott Hotel in Lyon"

• Place photo: click to enlarge (2x zoom)

• Phone number
• Official website
• Opening hours (day by day)
• Average rating and number of reviews
• Price range (restaurants)
• Types of services available

📷 Clickable photos:
Place photos are clickable and display larger in a modal window. Click anywhere to close or use the Escape key.

💡 After a search:
Say "more details on the first one" or "Italian restaurant hours" to dig deeper.

q9.question: Can I combine multiple services?
q9.answer:
Yes! LIA can intelligently combine multiple services:

🔗 Combination examples:

Weather + Calendar:
• "What will the weather be for my meeting tomorrow?"
• LIA checks your calendar and the weather

Email + Contacts:
• "Send an email to my contact John Smith"
• LIA finds John's email in your contacts

Places + Calendar:
• "Create an event tomorrow at noon at The Bistro restaurant, 10 Main Street"
• Combining event creation and address

Wikipedia + Questions:
• "How old was Marie Curie when she got her Nobel Prize?"
• LIA searches and calculates

💡 Tip:
Phrase your requests naturally - LIA will automatically choose the right tools.

q10.question: Which services work without configuration?
q10.answer:
Some services are immediately available, others require configuration:

✅ Available without configuration:
• 📚 Wikipedia: Free encyclopedic search
• 🌐 Web Page Reader: Web page reading (URL → content)
• 💬 Conversation: LIA answers your general questions

🔐 Require Google connection:
• 📧 Gmail
• 📅 Google Calendar
• 👥 Google Contacts
• 📁 Google Drive
• ✅ Google Tasks
• 📍 Google Places

🔑 Require an API key:
• 🌤️ OpenWeatherMap: Free, signup at openweathermap.org
• 🔍 Perplexity: Paid, signup at perplexity.ai

💡 Getting started tip:
Start by connecting your Google services (one authorization for all), then add OpenWeatherMap for free weather.

q11.question: How do I get directions?

🗺️ Simple directions:
• "How do I get from Paris to Lyon?"

📍 From my location:

Set your home address in Settings > Connectors > Google Places for "from home" searches.

q12.question: How do I choose the travel mode?
q12.answer:
Google Routes - Travel modes:

🚗 By car (default):
• "Driving directions to Lyon"
• "How long by car to Marseille?"

🚶 On foot:

🏍️ By motorcycle:

q13.question: How do I avoid tolls and highways?

Google Routes - Avoidance options:

💰 Avoid tolls:

🛣️ Avoid highways:

q14.question: How do I plan a trip with multiple stops?

Google Routes - Multi-stop trips:

📍 With waypoints:

🔄 Automatic optimization:

📊 Multi-stop information:

q15.question: How do I use directions with my contacts and events?
q15.answer:
Google Routes - Multi-domain integration:

👥 To a contact:
• "How do I get to my brother's place?"

📅 To an event:

📍 To a recent place:
• "Go back to yesterday's restaurant"

🔗 Advanced combinations:

• "Create an event tomorrow in Lyon with directions"
