The more you enrich your contacts with addresses, the more naturally LIA can guide you.

q16.question: How do I read the content of a web page?
q16.answer:
Web Page Reader - Web page reading:

🌐 Read an article or page:
• "Read this article: https://example.com/article"
• "What does this page say? https://korben.info"
• "Summarize this web page: https://..."
• "What articles are on this page?"

📖 What LIA does:
• Fetches the full page content
• Extracts the main article (smart mode)
• Converts to clean, readable text
• Automatically detects the page language

📊 Information provided:
• Page title
• Clean text content (Markdown)
• Word count
• Detected language

⚠️ Limitations:
• Public pages only (no login-protected content)
• HTML pages only (no PDF, no images)
• No JavaScript rendering (some dynamic sites may be incomplete)
• Max size: 500 KB

✅ Free, no configuration required.

q17.question: When should I use Web Page Reader vs web search?
q17.answer:
Choose the right tool based on your needs:

🌐 Use WEB PAGE READER for:
• Reading the full content of a URL you know
• Summarizing a specific article
• Analyzing the content of a particular page
• Comparing content across multiple pages
• "Read this article: https://..."

🔍 Use WEB SEARCH for:
• Finding information about a topic
• Getting recent news
• Searching without knowing the exact URL
• "What's the latest news about X?"

🔗 Ideal combination:
1. Web search → finds relevant URLs
2. Web Page Reader → reads the full content of a result

💡 Example:
• "Search for articles about Rust" → Web search (Perplexity/Brave)
• "Read this article: https://blog.rust-lang.org/..." → Web Page Reader (full content)

q18.question: What is Browser Control and when should I use it?
q18.answer:
Browser Control lets LIA interact with websites like a real user: navigate, search, click, fill forms, and extract data from JavaScript-rendered pages.

Use for: searching products on e-commerce, filling forms, extracting dynamic content, walking through multi-step flows.
Examples:
- Use the web browser to go to amazon.fr and search for MacBook Pro M4
- Use the web browser to go to nike.com and find white Nike Air for men with prices
- Go to a booking site, find the agency in my city and show me the available cars for next weekend

Good to know: on a transactional flow LIA advances up to the login / payment step, then stops and reports what it found — it never enters credentials or submits a payment.

q19.question: How does the browser agent work?
q19.answer: It uses headless Chromium (Playwright) to: navigate, handle cookies automatically, wait for JS rendering, extract visible content, and interact if needed. The agent decides autonomously which actions to take, re-checks the page after each action to confirm it worked, and detects when it's stuck and changes strategy. A simple lookup takes 15-60 seconds; a multi-step flow (several pages, a form to fill) can take a few minutes.

q20.question: What is the difference between Browser Control and Web Fetch?
q20.answer: Web Fetch: static HTML, read-only, fast (1-3s), cheap. Browser Control: full JS execution, click/fill/search, slower (15-60s), more expensive but handles dynamic pages and interaction.

rappels.title: Reminders & Notifications
rappels.description: Create personal reminders and receive push notifications

q1.question: How do I create a reminder?
q1.answer:
Create reminders using natural language:

🔔 Creation examples:
• "Remind me to call the doctor in 2 hours"
• "Remind me tomorrow at 9am to prepare the meeting"
• "Remind me tonight at 8pm to buy bread"
• "Remind me Friday at 2:30pm to follow up with the client"

📅 Supported date/time formats:
• Relative time: "in 30 minutes", "in 2 hours"
• Absolute time: "at 3pm", "at 9:30am"
• Day: "tomorrow", "next Monday", "January 15"
• Combined: "tomorrow at 10am", "Monday at 2pm"

✅ Confirmation:
LIA confirms creation with the exact date and time in your timezone.

💡 Tip:
Be specific about the reminder content so you easily remember what it's about.

q2.question: How do I see my pending reminders?
q2.answer:
Check your pending reminders easily:

📋 View reminder list:
• "What are my reminders?"
• "Show my pending reminders"
• "List my reminders"
• "Do I have any scheduled reminders?"

📊 Information displayed:
• Content of each reminder
• Scheduled date and time (in your timezone)
• Numbering for easy reference

💡 Example display:
🔔 Your pending reminders:
1. Call the doctor - 12/28 at 2:00 PM
2. Prepare the meeting - 12/29 at 9:00 AM

🔗 Using references:
After listing your reminders, you can reference them by number: "Cancel the first one" or "Cancel reminder number 2".

q3.question: How do I cancel a reminder?
q3.answer:
Several ways to cancel a reminder:

🗑️ By natural reference:
• "Cancel my next reminder"
• "Cancel the last reminder"
• "Cancel the first reminder"

🔢 By number (after listing):
• "Cancel reminder number 2"
• "Delete the 3rd reminder"

📝 By content:
• "Cancel the doctor reminder"
• "Cancel the reminder about the meeting"

✅ Confirmation:
LIA confirms the cancellation by showing the deleted reminder's content.

⚠️ Important:
• Only pending reminders can be cancelled
• Already sent reminders cannot be cancelled
• Cancellation is immediate and permanent

q4.question: How do push notifications work?
q4.answer:
Push notifications alert you even when the app is closed:

🔔 How it works:
• At the scheduled time, you receive a notification on your device
• The notification contains your reminder content
• The message is personalized based on your active LIA personality
• Works even if the app is closed or in the background

📱 Supported devices:
• Web browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)
• Android (browser and PWA)
• iOS (installed PWA only)

⚙️ Technology used:
LIA uses Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to send notifications reliably and instantly.

💡 Tip:
For the best experience, enable notifications in settings and add LIA to your home screen on mobile.

q5.question: How do I enable notifications on my device?
q5.answer:
Enable notifications in a few steps:

⚙️ Activation:
1. Go to Settings
2. Find the Push notifications section
3. Click Enable
4. Your browser asks for permission → Accept

📱 On mobile (iOS):
iOS notifications require installing LIA as a PWA:
1. Open LIA in Safari
2. Tap Share → Add to Home Screen
3. Open the app from your home screen
4. Enable notifications in settings

🔧 If notifications are blocked:
You need to re-enable them in your browser settings:
• Chrome: Settings > Privacy > Site Settings > Notifications
• Firefox: Settings > Privacy > Permissions > Notifications

📋 Device management:
In settings, you can see all your registered devices and remove them individually.

q6.question: What's the difference between reminders and Google Tasks?
q6.answer:
Reminders and tasks have different uses:

🔔 LIA Reminders:
• One-time notification at a specific time
• No persistence after sending
• Ideal for: "Remind me to call John at 3pm"
• Message personalized with your LIA personality
• Push notification on all your devices
• No state tracking (done/not done)

✅ Google Tasks:
• Persistent task list
• Remains visible until completion
• Ideal for: "Add 'Go shopping' to my list"
• Synced with Google Tasks
• State tracking (to do/completed)
• Organization in lists

💡 In summary:
• Reminder = "Notify me at a specific time" (one-shot notification)
• Task = "I need to do this" (list of things to accomplish)

🔗 Possible combination:
You can use both: create a task for tracking, and a reminder so you don't forget to do it.

interests.title: Interests
interests.description: Personalized proactive suggestions on your favorite topics

q1.question: How does LIA learn my interests?
q1.answer:
LIA learns your interests automatically by analyzing your conversations:

🧠 Automatic learning:
• LLM analysis of each conversation
• Detection of topics you're passionate about
• Filtering of practical requests (weather, emails...)

✨ What is detected:
• Expressed enthusiasm or curiosity
• Information requests on a topic
• Repeated mentions of a theme
• Personal opinions shared

📂 10 categories:
Technology, Science, Culture, Sports, Finance, Travel, Nature, Health, Entertainment, Other

🎯 Abstraction level:
LIA extracts categories, not products. Example: "iPhone 18 Pro" → "Apple Smartphones, iOS"

q2.question: How do proactive notifications work?
q2.answer:
LIA sends you relevant content on your favorite topics:

📬 Principle:
• Notifications sent without you asking
• Content adapted to your interests
• Personalized with LIA's active personality

📚 Content sources:
1. Perplexity: recent news and research
2. Brave Search: up-to-date web results
3. Wikipedia: encyclopedic articles
4. AI Reflection: generated content if no source fits

⏰ Triggering:
• Only within your time window (9am-10pm by default)
• Configurable frequency (1 to 5 per day)
• Never when you're actively using chat
• 1-hour global cooldown between notifications

📱 Delivery:
• Push notification (even with app closed)
• Real-time display in chat
• Archived in conversation history
• Clickable source links at the end of the message to read the original articles

q3.question: How do I manage my interests?
q3.answer:
Manage your interests in Settings:

⚙️ Access:
Settings → "Interests" section

🎚️ Global settings:
• Enable/Disable proactive suggestions
• Time window: set notification hours (9am-10pm by default)
• Frequency: min/max notifications per day (1-5)

📋 Interest list:
• View all your interests with their weight
• Block: no more notifications on this topic
• Delete: permanently remove
• Add manually: create an interest

🏷️ Filter by category:
Navigate by type (Technology, Science, Culture...)

q4.question: How does the weight system work?
q4.answer:
Each interest has a weight that evolves:

📊 Weight calculation:
• Bayesian algorithm (Beta distribution)
• Starts with a slightly positive prior
• Increases with positive signals
• Decreases with negative signals

📈 Positive signals (+weight):
• Mentioning the topic in a conversation
• Clicking "I like this topic" 👍

📉 Negative signals (-weight):
• Clicking "Less interested" 👎
• Temporal decay (0.5%/day without mention)

⏳ Temporal decay:
• If you stop talking about a topic, its weight decreases
• Dormant interests after 15 days without mention — but they stay visible and manageable (reactivate, edit or delete) in a dedicated section of Settings
• Automatic deletion after 30 days of dormancy

🎯 Selection for notification (variety-first):
Your interests are grouped into subjects (e.g. several AI tools = one subject). Recently notified subjects rest for a while and rarely served subjects get priority — one passion never monopolizes your notifications. Within a subject, the least recently covered interest is favored

q5.question: How do I give feedback on a notification?
q5.answer:
When you receive a notification, give your opinion:

👍 "I like this topic":
• +2 positive signals
• The topic will be suggested more often
• Use when the message was interesting

👎 "Less interested":
• +2 negative signals
• The topic will be suggested less
• Use if it wasn't relevant this time

🚫 "Never suggest again":
• Permanently blocks this topic
• No more notifications on this theme
• Reversible in settings

💡 Where to find the buttons:
Feedback buttons appear only in the chat message, not in settings (because they only make sense in the context of a received notification).

q6.question: How is duplicate content avoided?
q6.answer:
LIA uses several anti-duplicate mechanisms:

🔄 Duplicate protection:

1. Interest deduplication:
• Semantic similarity via AI-powered embeddings
• 90% threshold: two similar topics → consolidation
• "Python" and "Python Programming" = same interest

2. Content deduplication:
• SHA256 hash of content (exact comparison)
• Semantic similarity (90% threshold)
• Checked against the last 7 days

3. Cooldowns:
• Global: 1h minimum between 2 notifications
• Per topic: 12h before discussing the same interest again
• Per subject: 36h before revisiting the same theme
• Daily quota: max N notifications/day

📊 Result:
You will never receive the same content twice, nor topics too similar in a row.

heartbeat.title: Proactive Notifications
heartbeat.description: LIA takes the initiative to keep you informed

q1.question: What are proactive notifications?
q1.answer:
Proactive notifications allow LIA to take the initiative to contact you with useful information:

🧠 How it works:
• LIA continuously analyzes multiple data sources (calendar, weather, emails, interests, memories, journals)
• An LLM intelligently decides whether there's something useful to tell you
• The message is rewritten with your personality and in your language

📌 Examples:
• "Rain expected in 45 minutes, don't forget your umbrella"
• "You have a meeting at 2pm and rain is forecast — bring an umbrella"
• "A topic you're interested in is trending today"

🎯 Varied and concrete:
• Topics rotate: a subject just covered steps aside, rarely served ones get priority — one passion never monopolizes your notifications
• When a notification is built around one of your interests, LIA looks up real, fresh facts and names them (a film, an event, an announcement) with clickable source links — no vague "have a look at..."

💡 Philosophy:
LIA only sends a notification when it is genuinely useful — quality over quantity.

q2.question: How do I enable proactive notifications?
q2.answer:
Enable the feature in just a few clicks:

⚙️ Access:
Settings → "Proactive Notifications" section → Enable the toggle

📝 Available options:
• Min/max per day: set the minimum (default: 1) and maximum (default: 3) notifications per day (range: 1-8)
• Time window: configure your own start hour (default: 9 AM) and end hour (default: 10 PM) — independent from interest notification hours
• Push notifications: enable/disable push (FCM/Telegram) separately

💡 Silent mode:
If you disable push, LIA's messages are archived silently in conversation + SSE. You'll see them at your next login without being disturbed.

q3.question: What data sources are used?
q3.answer:
LIA aggregates 8 data sources in parallel to decide whether to notify you:

📅 Calendar:
• Upcoming events (next few hours)
• Requires an active calendar connector (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Microsoft)

🌤️ Weather + Changes:
• Current conditions + transition detection: rain starting/stopping, temperature drop OR rise for tomorrow (compared on daily averages — nighttime cooling no longer triggers false "temperature drop" alerts), strong wind
• Requires an OpenWeatherMap connector + configured home location
• Optional travel-aware location (v1.16.7): when you enable "Use my current location for weather alerts", LIA uses your browser position instead of your home address when you're more than 50 km away. See the dedicated question below.

✅ Tasks:
• Pending or overdue tasks
• Requires an active tasks connector (Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do)

📧 Emails:
• Today's unread emails (urgent, actionable)
• Requires an active email connector (Gmail, Apple, Microsoft)

⭐ Interests:
• A varied sample of your active interests — one per theme, least recently covered first (so the same topic never comes back day after day)

🧠 Memories:
• Relevant information extracted from your memories

📓 Journals:
• Relevant entries from the assistant's personal journals (self-reflection, observations, learnings)
• Requires journals to be enabled (Settings > Features > Personal Journals)

📊 Indicators:
The Settings section shows a green badge for each connected source and a gray badge for unavailable sources.

q4.question: How often will I receive notifications?
q4.answer:
Frequency is controlled at multiple levels:

📊 Your controls:
• Min/max per day: you choose (1-8 range, default min 1 / max 3)
• Time window: only during your configured hours (default 9 AM - 10 PM, independent from interest hours)

🛡️ Automatic safeguards:
• Global cooldown: minimum 1h between 2 proactive notifications
• Anti-redundancy: LIA re-reads the content of its last notifications (10 over 7 days) and never proposes the same topic, activity or product again — even when it comes from a different source
• Cross-type dedup: interest notifications count too, in both directions (a theme covered by either flow rests for a while)
• Activity cooldown: if you chatted with LIA in the last 15 minutes, no notification will be sent

💡 In practice:
You'll receive between 0 and 3 notifications per day, only when relevant. Some days, LIA may decide not to send anything.

q5.question: How do I give feedback on a notification?
q5.answer:
Your feedback helps LIA improve:

👍👎 Feedback buttons:
• Each notification displays thumbs up / thumbs down buttons
• Your feedback is recorded to improve future decisions

📜 History:
• View your recent proactive notifications in the dedicated section
• Each entry shows the sources used and priority level

⚙️ Adjustment:
• If you receive too many notifications, reduce the daily maximum
• If notifications aren't relevant, disable unwanted sources (disconnect the corresponding connector)

q6.question: Are proactive notifications affected by usage limits?
q6.answer: Yes. When your usage limits are reached, proactive notifications are automatically paused until your limits are reset or adjusted by your administrator.

q7.question: How do weather alerts work when I'm travelling? (v1.16.7)
q7.answer:
By default, proactive weather notifications use your home address. If you're travelling, you can opt in to let LIA use your current position instead:

⚙️ How to enable:
Settings → Proactive Notifications → scroll to Weather location when traveling → toggle on.

🎯 When it kicks in:
LIA uses your current browser position (instead of your home) only when all these conditions are met:
• The option is enabled
• Your last known position is less than 24 hours old
• You are more than 50 km away from your home address

Below that distance, the home address is kept (avoids switching for intra-city noise). Past 24 h, the position is considered stale and notifications fall back to home automatically.

🏙️ Transparent notifications:
When the position used isn't your home, the notification always mentions the city it's referring to, so you instantly know where the forecast is from.

🔒 Privacy by design:
• Your position is encrypted (same cryptographic scheme as your home address)
• It is not historized — each update overwrites the previous one, there is no trail
• It is wiped immediately if you disable the option or remove your home address
• A Currently stored block shows you exactly what LIA has kept, with a Clear now button to wipe on demand
• The backend rate-limits itself to one update per 30 minutes per user

💡 Requirements:
You also need to enable browser geolocation (in Settings → Location → Geolocation). Without it, no position can be captured — a banner reminds you if needed.

q8.question: What are “open loops”? (v1.25.13)
q8.answer:
An open loop is a commitment LIA heard in conversation and quietly keeps for you — « I must call the plumber back », « Marie owes me the quote ». At the right moment (imminent deadline, or a loop left silent too long), a proactive notification gives you a gentle memory-jog, direction-aware: « You wanted to call the plumber back — is now a good time? » vs « Still no news from Marie about the quote? ».

Never nagging: each loop has its own cooldown — once surfaced, it will not come back for several days. A loop closes itself when you say « done », or via the dashboard « For you » card, and quietly expires after weeks of inactivity.

⚙️ Admin: off by default (OPEN_LOOPS_ENABLED).

q9.question: Can LIA tell me when to leave for a meeting? (v1.25.13)
q9.answer:
Yes. When your next calendar event has a location and starts within a few hours, LIA checks real traffic (Google Routes) from your effective position and can notify you: « Leave by 13:30 — 30 min drive to your 14:00 appointment », combined with weather when it matters (« rain expected at 14:30 »).

One route check at most per cycle, cached per event — and the same notification is never sent twice for one event.

⚙️ Admin: off by default (HEARTBEAT_DEPARTURE_ENABLED); requires a configured home location.

q1.question: What is a scheduled action?
q1.answer:
A scheduled action is a recurring task executed automatically by LIA:

📋 Principle:
• You define a title, an instruction and a schedule
• LIA executes the instruction automatically on chosen days and times
• Results appear in your conversation + push notification

📌 Examples:
• "Search today's weather" — every day at 8am
• "Search the latest 5 AI news" — Mon, Wed, Fri at 7:30pm
• "Show my tasks and appointments for today" — Sat, Sun at 9am

🔁 Recurrence:
Each execution is automatically rescheduled for the next slot.

q2.question: How do I create a scheduled action?
q2.answer:
Create an action in 4 steps:

⚙️ Access:
Settings → "Scheduled Actions" section → Add button

📝 Configuration:
1. Title: descriptive name (e.g., "AI Watch")
2. Instruction: the prompt sent to LIA (e.g., "Search the latest 5 AI news")
3. Days: select days of the week (Mon-Sun buttons)
4. Time: choose the execution time

💡 Tip:
Be specific in the instruction, as if you were talking to LIA directly.

q3.question: How do I test a scheduled action?
q3.answer:
You can test an action immediately without waiting for the scheduled time:

▶️ Test button:
• Click the Test button on the action card
• Execution starts in the background
• Results appear in your conversation + push notification

💡 Usefulness:
• Verify the instruction produces the expected result
• Adjust the prompt if needed before the first scheduled execution

q4.question: What happens in case of error?
q4.answer:
LIA handles errors robustly:

⚠️ On failure:
• The action is rescheduled for the next slot
• The error message is displayed on the card
• The consecutive failure counter increments

🛑 Auto-disable:
• After 5 consecutive failures, the action is automatically paused
• Status changes to "Error"
• You can re-enable it via the switch after fixing the issue

🔄 Re-activation:
• Re-enabling the action resets the counters
• The next trigger time is recalculated

q5.question: How many scheduled actions can I create?
q5.answer:
You can create up to 20 scheduled actions:

📊 Limits:
• Maximum 20 actions per user
• Each action can target one or more days of the week
• Time is configured to the minute

⚙️ Management:
• Enable/Disable: inline switch to pause without deleting
• Edit: change the title, instruction, days or time
• Delete: permanent deletion (past results remain in conversation)

q6.question: Are scheduled actions affected by usage limits?
q6.answer: Yes. When your usage limits are reached, scheduled actions are blocked. The action remains scheduled and will resume automatically on the next cycle or when your administrator adjusts your limits.

q7.question: Can I create automations directly from the chat? (v1.25.13)
q7.answer:
Yes — in one sentence: « give me an AI press review every weekday at 8am ». LIA validates the schedule and shows a confirmation card (title, days, time, instruction); nothing is created until you confirm. You can also list your automations (« what are my automations? ») and pause/resume one in natural language.

💡 Bonus: when you ask the same kind of thing at the same hour on several distinct days, LIA can spontaneously offer: « Want me to turn this into a recurring automation? » (deterministic detection, one suggestion max per month per pattern, off by default — RECURRENCE_SUGGESTION_ENABLED).

Deleting an automation remains a Settings action.

mcp_servers.title: MCP Servers
mcp_servers.description: Connect external tools via the MCP protocol

q1.question: What is an MCP server?
q1.answer:
An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is an external service that exposes tools usable by LIA:

🔌 How it works:
• MCP is an open standard (Anthropic) for connecting tools to an AI assistant
• Each server exposes one or more tools (functions) that LIA can call
• MCP tools integrate seamlessly alongside native tools (Google, weather, etc.)

📌 Example MCP servers:
• HuggingFace Hub: search ML models
• GitHub: manage repositories and issues
• Slack: send messages
• Database: SQL queries

💡 Benefit:
Extend LIA's capabilities without limits by connecting any MCP-compatible service.

q2.question: How do I add an MCP server?
q2.answer:
Add a server in a few steps:

⚙️ Access:
Settings → "MCP Servers" section → Add button

📝 Configuration:
1. Name: descriptive name (e.g., "HuggingFace Hub")
2. URL: HTTP(S) endpoint of the MCP server
3. Description (optional): describe what the server does so LIA knows when to use it
4. Authentication: choose the type (none, API key, bearer token, OAuth 2.1)
5. Timeout: maximum call duration (5-120 seconds)

🔗 After creation:
Click Test Connection to verify the server is reachable and discover available tools.

q3.question: What authentication types are supported?
q3.answer:
Four authentication types are available:

🔓 None:
For public servers or internal network services

🔑 API Key:
• Sent in a customizable HTTP header
• Default header: X-API-Key
• Ideal for simple APIs (HuggingFace, etc.)

🎫 Bearer Token:
• Token sent in the Authorization: Bearer header
• For APIs using static access tokens

🔐 OAuth 2.1:
• Full authorization flow with PKCE
• Optional Client ID and Client Secret (pre-registration)
• Automatic refresh of expired tokens
• For APIs requiring user authorization (GitHub, Slack...)

💡 Security:
All authentication credentials are encrypted server-side.

q4.question: How do I test the connection to an MCP server?
q4.answer:
You can test a server in two ways:

⚡ From the list:
• Hover over the server → click the lightning bolt icon
• Results appear in a popup window

⚡ From the edit form:
• Open the server settings
• Click Test Connection
• Results appear below the button

✅ On success:
• The number of discovered tools is displayed
• A detailed tool list (name + description) appears
• Status changes to "Active"

❌ On failure:
• A detailed error message is shown
• Status changes to "Error"
• Check the URL, authentication, and server availability

q5.question: How do I configure OAuth 2.1 for an MCP server?
q5.answer:
OAuth setup is a two-step process:

📝 Step 1 — Configuration:
1. Select auth type "OAuth 2.1"
2. Enter Client ID and Client Secret if required by the provider (optional)
3. Add the required OAuth Scopes (e.g., repo project read:org for GitHub) — check the provider's documentation
4. Save the server

🔗 Step 2 — Authorization:
1. A "Connect OAuth" button appears on the server card
2. Click it → you're redirected to the provider
3. Grant access → automatic return to LIA
4. Status changes to "Active" ✅

🔄 Token refresh:
• Tokens are refreshed automatically
• If refresh fails, status reverts to "Authentication required"
• Click "Connect OAuth" again to re-authorize

q6.question: How does LIA use MCP tools in a conversation?
q6.answer:
MCP tools are used automatically by LIA when relevant:

🧠 Smart selection:
• LIA analyzes your question and identifies relevant tools
• The server description helps LIA choose the right MCP server
• MCP tools are selected alongside native tools (Google, weather, etc.)

📊 Result display:
• MCP results appear as visual cards in the conversation
• Each card shows the source server and tool name
• Content can be text or formatted JSON

💡 Tips:
• Write a good server description to guide LIA
• Test the connection to ensure tools are properly discovered
• You can enable/disable a server via the toggle without deleting it

q7.question: What are OAuth scopes and why are they important?
q7.answer:
OAuth scopes define the permissions requested during authorization:

🔐 Why scopes matter:
• Without scopes, the OAuth token has minimal permissions
• Tool discovery (list_tools) works without scopes (metadata only)
• But tool calls (call_tool) return 403 Forbidden without the right scopes

📋 Common scopes by provider:
• GitHub: repo project read:org
• Slack: channels:read chat:write
• Check your provider's documentation for required scopes

⚙️ How to configure:
1. Edit your MCP server
2. Fill in the "OAuth Scopes" field (space-separated)
3. Save, then click "Connect OAuth" again to re-authorize with the new scopes

💡 Tip:
If your MCP tools return 403 errors after a successful OAuth connection, it's likely a missing scopes issue.

q8.question: How does automatic description generation work?
q8.answer:
LIA can auto-generate a domain description for your MCP servers:

🤖 Automatic generation:
• During connection testing, if no description is set, an LLM analyzes the discovered tools
• It generates an intelligent description that helps LIA understand when to use this server
• The description is optimized for query routing (selecting the right server based on the question)

✨ Manual regeneration:
• In edit mode, click the Generate description button (sparkle icon) next to the description field
• This overwrites the existing description with a fresh tool analysis
• Requires having tested the connection first (to discover tools)

💡 Tips:
• You can always write a manual description that won't be overwritten by the connection test
• Auto-generation is a good starting point that you can refine afterwards

q9.question: How do I generate Excalidraw diagrams and schemas?
q9.answer:
LIA can create architecture diagrams, workflows, org charts and more using the Excalidraw MCP server:

📝 How to use:
Simply describe what you want in natural language:
• "Create a client-server architecture with a database"
• "Draw a 5-step onboarding workflow"
• "Make an org chart for a marketing team"

⚙️ How it works (3-step process):
1. LIA generates a structured intent describing components and relationships
2. A first dedicated LLM call creates the shapes (boxes, circles, text)
3. A second LLM call adds the arrows (connections between shapes)

💡 Tips for best results:
• Describe the components you want (servers, databases, users...)
• Specify relationships between them (connects to, sends data to...)
• Mention the layout type if desired (flowchart, hierarchy, network...)

⚠️ Prerequisite:
The Excalidraw MCP server must be configured and active in your MCP server settings.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Extend LIA capabilities with expert instructions

q1.question: What is a skill?
q1.answer:
A skill is a SKILL.md file that extends the assistant's capabilities with expert instructions, structured workflows, or planning templates. They follow the open agentskills.io standard, compatible with 30+ products (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot...).

Three skill types:

  • Prompt expert: expert instructions without tools (writing, coaching...)
  • Advisory: methodology + LIA can call its own tools
  • Plan template: deterministic plan with automatic tool calls (briefing, meeting prep...)

q2.question: How do I import a skill?
q2.answer: In Settings > Features > My Skills, click Import skill and select a .md or .zip file. Compatible skills are available on skillsmp.com or GitHub.

q3.question: How do I create my own skill?
q3.answer:
The easiest way: just ask LIA! Say something like "create a skill for [your need]" and the built-in Skill Generator guides you step by step: need analysis, archetype selection (among the 5 archetypes), generation, automatic validation — and direct installation: the finished skill lands in My Skills immediately, active and ready to use, and LIA announces it by name.

You can also manually create a SKILL.md file with a minimal YAML header (name + description) followed by Markdown instructions. See the built-in guide (📖 button in My Skills) for advanced options.

q4.question: What is the difference between admin skills and my skills?
q4.answer:
Admin skills (built-in): shipped with the application, available to all users. You can enable/disable them individually.

My skills (imported): personal skills you import. You can toggle, download, or delete them.

Skill names are unique: an import reusing the name of a built-in skill (or of another user's skill) is cleanly refused — pick a variant name instead.

q5.question: How does LIA decide which skill to use?
q5.answer:
Skill activation is model-driven — the LLM reads the L1 catalogue (names + descriptions) and decides which skill matches your request.

For skills with a deterministic plan_template, an optimization mechanism (SkillBypassStrategy) can trigger the skill directly without consulting the LLM planner.

q6.question: Can I download or share a skill?
q6.answer:
Yes. Hover over any skill in settings and click the download icon (⬇️). You will get a .zip file containing SKILL.md and all associated files (references/, scripts/, assets/).

Share this zip with other users or publish it on agentskills.io-compatible marketplaces.

q7.question: What is the Skill Generator?
q7.answer:
The Skill Generator is a built-in system skill that lets you create your own skills using natural language. Simply describe your need ("I want a detailed 5-day weather forecast") and the assistant guides you through 4 steps:

  1. Need analysis: clarifying questions about the task, tools, and desired format — the dialogue keeps its context across turns
  2. Archetype selection: Prompt Expert, Advisory, Plan Template, Visualizer, or Generator
  3. Generation: creates the SKILL.md (plus scripts and references if needed) compliant with the agentskills.io standard
  4. Validation & installation: automatic format verification, then direct installation — LIA announces the skill by name and it is immediately active in My Skills (toggle, download or delete it there like any imported skill)

q8.question: Can skills render maps, images, or interactive mini-apps? (v1.16.8)
q8.answer:
Yes. Since v1.16.8, a Python skill script can return, in addition to text, an interactive HTML frame (Google Maps view, weather dashboard, monthly calendar, Pomodoro timer, unit converter...) and/or an image (QR code, chart).

Seven new built-in skills showcase this mechanism: interactive-map, weather-dashboard, calendar-month, qr-code, pomodoro-timer, unit-converter, dice-roller.

How it works:

  • Theme and language stay in sync — frames detect and respect your current theme (light/dark) and language automatically. A theme change propagates live without reload.
  • Auto-sizing — the frame resizes automatically to fit its content.
  • Strict security — frames run in a sandboxed iframe (allow-scripts allow-popups, no allow-same-origin), with a Content Security Policy injected for user-imported skills.
  • Visible in all display modes — Rich HTML, Markdown, Cards: frames show up everywhere.

To build your own skill with frames or images, open the Skills Guide (Advanced tab → "Localization, theming and runtime conventions" section), or simply say: "create a skill that shows a QR code".

q9.question: What does the skills gallery show? (v1.25.16)
q9.answer: Settings → Skills now displays your skills as cards. Opening one shows its localized description, a preview image when the skill bundles one, its declared output channels (text, interactive frame, image) and the actions (enable/disable, download, delete). Every skill imported from outside LIA carries a provenance warning: its instructions run with access to your connected data, so only keep skills whose source you trust.

q10.question: Can I install a skill directly from a URL? (v1.25.16)
q10.answer: Yes — « From URL » in Settings → Skills. Paste an https address serving a SKILL.md file or a .zip package. The server validates everything: https only, no private/internal addresses, no redirects, size cap, and the same strict import pipeline as a file upload (name conflicts, quota, content validation). Failed attempts are rate-limited per user.

sub_agents.title: Sub-Agents
sub_agents.description: Specialized assistants for complex delegated tasks

q1.question: What are sub-agents?
q1.answer:
Sub-agents are specialized ephemeral assistants that the principal LIA assistant can delegate tasks to. When your request requires deep research, multi-source analysis, or specialized expertise, the assistant can spawn one or more experts to work in parallel.

Sub-agents are invisible — you interact only with the principal assistant, which synthesizes their findings into a natural response.

q2.question: When does LIA use sub-agents?
q2.answer:
LIA decides to call on experts when:

  • Your request involves parallel research across several areas (e.g., comparing transport options)
  • A topic benefits from deep specialized analysis (e.g., technical audit, market research)
  • Multiple independent expert viewpoints are needed at the same time

Simple questions are always handled directly — experts are only called in when they add real value.

You stay in control: before launching the experts, LIA asks for your confirmation. If you decline, it automatically switches to a standard plan without sub-agents.

Tip: you can also explicitly ask LIA to use experts, for example: "Use specialized experts to handle my request".

q3.question: Can I disable sub-agents?
q3.answer:
Sub-agent activation is managed at the application level by your administrator (via a global configuration flag) — it's no longer a per-user setting in your account.

You stay in control on each delegation: before launching a sub-agent, LIA systematically asks for your confirmation. If you decline, the assistant automatically switches to a standard plan without expert delegation — you can keep declining as often as needed.

If you'd prefer to never see a sub-agent delegation, ask your administrator to disable the feature globally.

q4.question: Do sub-agents cost more tokens?
q4.answer:
Yes — each sub-agent performs its own LLM calls (planning + tool execution + synthesis). A delegation with 3 experts can cost 3-5x more tokens than a single direct search.

Token guard-rails are in place: per-execution budget, daily budget per user, and auto-disable after consecutive failures. All sub-agent costs are tracked and visible in your usage statistics.

rag_spaces.title: Knowledge Spaces (RAG)
rag_spaces.description: Upload and use your own documents to enrich AI responses

q1.question: What are Knowledge Spaces?
q1.answer:
Knowledge Spaces (RAG — Retrieval-Augmented Generation) allow you to upload your own documents to create personal knowledge bases. When you ask a question, LIA automatically searches these documents and enriches its responses with relevant content.

Key features:

  • Upload 15+ formats: PDF, TXT, MD, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, RTF, HTML, ODT, ODS, ODP, EPUB, JSON, XML
  • Automatic chunking and indexing via Gemini embeddings
  • Hybrid search (semantic + BM25 keyword) for optimal relevance
  • Source citations in responses

q2.question: What file formats are supported?
q2.answer:
Knowledge Spaces accept 15+ formats:

  • PDF — text extraction via PyMuPDF
  • TXT — plain text files
  • Markdown (.md) — documentation and notes
  • DOCX — Microsoft Word documents
  • PPTX — PowerPoint presentations
  • XLSX — Excel spreadsheets
  • CSV — tabular data
  • RTF — Rich Text Format
  • HTML — web pages
  • ODT / ODS / ODP — LibreOffice documents
  • EPUB — e-books
  • JSON — structured data
  • XML — structured markup

Limits: maximum 20 MB per file, up to 50 documents per space, and 10 spaces per user.

q3.question: How does document processing work?
q3.answer:
When you upload a document, LIA processes it in the background:

  1. Text extraction — content is extracted based on file type
  2. Chunking — text is split into overlapping segments (1000 characters with 200 overlap)
  3. Embedding — each chunk is converted to a vector using OpenAI's embedding model
  4. Indexing — vectors are stored in PostgreSQL (pgvector) for fast similarity search

The document status changes from processing to ready when complete. If an error occurs, the status shows error with details.

q4.question: How do I activate or deactivate a space?
q4.answer:
Each space has an activation toggle. When a space is active, its documents are included in RAG searches during conversations.

Tips:

  • Only activate spaces relevant to your current work to improve relevance
  • An indicator in the chat header shows how many spaces are active
  • Click the indicator to quickly manage your spaces
  • Deactivating a space does not delete any data — you can reactivate it anytime

q5.question: How does hybrid search work?
q5.answer:
LIA uses a hybrid search combining two complementary techniques:

  • Semantic search — finds content with similar meaning using vector embeddings (cosine similarity)
  • BM25 keyword search — finds content with matching keywords (exact term matching)

Results are merged using a weighted fusion formula. This ensures both conceptually relevant and keyword-accurate results are surfaced.

Quality controls: minimum relevance score threshold, token budget limit (2000 tokens max), and configurable number of chunks per query.

q6.question: How much does RAG cost?
q6.answer:
RAG uses OpenAI embeddings, which have a small cost:

  • Indexing (upload) — one-time cost per document, using gemini-embedding-001
  • Search (each query) — embedding of your question (~few tokens per query)

Costs are fully tracked and visible in the assistant message cost breakdown and your usage dashboard. The RAG embedding cost appears under the gemini-embedding-001 model.

Tip: For a typical 10-page PDF, indexing costs less than $0.001.

q7.question: How does Google Drive sync work?
q7.answer:
You can link Google Drive folders to your knowledge spaces. Click 'Link Folder', browse your Drive, and select a folder. LIA lists the supported files, downloads them, and processes them through the same indexing pipeline.

Use 'Sync Now' to update — LIA detects new, modified, and deleted files automatically.

Key details:

  • Supports Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides via API export
  • Per-file error isolation — one failed file does not block others
  • Feature flag: RAG_SPACES_DRIVE_SYNC_ENABLED

q8.question: Can I ask the assistant about its own features?
q8.answer:
Yes! LIA has a built-in knowledge base that lets it answer questions about itself directly in conversation:

🧠 How it works:
• LIA automatically detects when you ask about the app ("What can you do?", "How do I connect my calendar?")
• It searches its FAQ knowledge base (200+ Q&A across 24 sections) using the same hybrid search as user spaces
• An App Identity Prompt describing all capabilities is injected into the response

⚡ Zero overhead:
This only activates when you ask about the app. Normal queries (emails, calendar, etc.) are not affected at all.

🔧 Admin features:
Administrators can manage system knowledge spaces in Settings > Administration > RAG Spaces:
• View staleness status (content hash comparison)
• Trigger manual reindexation
• System spaces are automatically indexed at app startup

q9.question: Can LIA search my documents on its own? (v1.25.13)
q9.answer:
Yes. Your document spaces are now an active domain: beyond the automatic context injection, the planner can decide to search them — with derived queries, several passes if needed, and combinations with other sources: « compare the PDF quote with what Paul sent by email » chains a document search and an email search.

The « Documents » briefing card also shows your latest modified Drive files — one click to summarize in chat, or open directly in Drive.

journals.title: Personal Journals
journals.description: Assistant's personal logbooks for reflections and learnings

q1.question: What are personal journals?
q1.answer:
Personal journals are thematic notebooks where the AI assistant records its own reflections, observations, analyses, and learnings. Unlike user memories (facts about you), journals contain the assistant's own perspective — written in first person, colored by its active personality.

4 themes: Self-reflection, User observations, Ideas & analyses, Learnings.

4 abstraction levels: L0 raw observation (weak signal worth tracking), L1 operational directive (the default WHEN→DO BECAUSE format), L2 transversal pattern (consolidation only), L3 portrait facet feeding the user model (consolidation only).

q2.question: When does the assistant write in its journals?
q2.answer:
Two mechanisms:

  • Post-conversation: After conversations (4+ messages), the assistant may write a reflection. Most conversations produce nothing — it's selective. The assistant also looks at the directives it injected on the previous turn and your current reaction (deferred self-evaluation T → T+1): if you confirmed, the evidence counter ticks up; if you pushed back, the contradiction counter ticks up. Zero added LLM cost — same extractor call, enriched prompt.
  • Periodic consolidation: Every few hours, the assistant reviews all notes — explicit pairwise dedup, classification audit, active clustering of convergent L1s into L2 patterns, and compilation of the user-model portrait — all in the same LLM call.

q3.question: How do journals influence responses?
q3.answer:
Two complementary mechanisms:

  • Semantic injection of relevant entries in the response prompt and the planner prompt — the assistant decides which notes are relevant from the similarity scores.
  • Ambient diffusion of the compiled user-model portrait across eight flows where LIA speaks: conversation and planner receive the full version (~200 tokens), while ReAct, voice, reminders, heartbeat notifications, proactive interest pings and fallback responses receive the brief version (~60 tokens). The same nuanced model of you is carried across every channel — your assistant doesn't "forget who you are" depending on the surface it speaks through.

q4.question: Can I read and edit the assistant's journals?
q4.answer: Yes! In Settings > Features > Personal Journals you can read entries grouped by theme or by abstraction level (toggle at the top of the accordion), edit title / content / mood / level / confidence, delete or even create your own entries. Your additions are transparent — the assistant can't tell the difference. A new filter "Show only entries never used" surfaces directives that have never been injected (zero uses), so you can clean them up quickly.

q5.question: What settings can I configure?
q5.answer:
Toggles: Enable/disable journals, consolidation, conversation history analysis (with cost warning).

Numeric settings: Max journal size (40,000 chars default), prompt injection budget (1,500 chars), max entry size (2,000 chars), max search results (10).

q6.question: How much does it cost?
q6.answer: Journal operations use background LLM calls. Extraction: one call per qualifying conversation (most return empty). The deferred self-evaluation enriches the same prompt at zero added LLM cost. Consolidation: one call every 4–12 h per user; the same call now also compiles the user-model portrait, so portrait diffusion adds no extra LLM call. Per-turn diffusion adds roughly +200 tokens to the conversation/planner prompts and ~+60 tokens to the secondary flows, plus one extra DB read (~1 ms). Models configurable in Admin > LLM Configuration. Real costs visible in Settings.

q7.question: What about privacy?
q7.answer: Journal data is per-user and isolated. All data can be exported (JSON/CSV) or deleted (GDPR) — the export now includes the compiled portrait. When journals are disabled, data is preserved but not used. When an account is deleted, the compiled portrait is scrubbed alongside the entries.

q8.question: How does the "How LIA sees you" panel work?
q8.answer:
A dedicated section sits at the top of the journals settings. It surfaces a compiled portrait of you, in two read-only tabs:

  • Full (~200 tokens) — a faceted portrait: traits of fond, current phase, contexts, contradictions, blind spots, evolution. Used in conversation and planner prompts.
  • Brief (~60 tokens) — the essence in 2–3 sentences. Diffused across the secondary flows (voice, reminders, heartbeat, ReAct, proactive, fallback).

The portrait is a synthesis voice and is intentionally not directly editable. Three corrective levers are exposed instead:

  1. Edit L3 source entries — standard CRUD on entries flagged level=L3. The portrait recompiles on the next consolidation.
  2. 🚩 Signal a problem — opens a free-text dialog. Submitting it creates a special user_correction entry and triggers a synchronous re-consolidation (~5–10 s, loader visible) that re-weights the L3 entries with your signal pinned at the top of the prompt.
  3. 🔄 Consolidate now — runs the full consolidation cycle on demand, bypassing the cooldown.

The portrait carries a freshness indicator — over 7 days old, it shows as "obsolete" so you can trigger a recompile.

q1.question: Are my conversations private?
q1.answer:
Yes, your conversations are strictly private:

🔐 Confidentiality:
• Your conversations are only accessible by you
• No sharing with third parties
• Administrators cannot read your messages

🗄️ Secure storage:
• Data stored in a secure database
• Complete isolation between users
• Encryption of sensitive data

🧠 AI usage:
• Your conversations are processed to respond to you
• They are NOT used to train models
• No analysis for marketing purposes

q2.question: How is my data protected?
q2.answer:
Multiple security levels protect your data:

🔐 Authentication:
• OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (security standard)
• Secure server-side sessions (Redis) with HTTP-only cookies

🔒 Data protection:
• Encryption in transit (HTTPS/TLS)
• HTTP-only cookies (XSS protection)
• Built-in CSRF protection

🛡️ Personal Information Protection (PII):
• Your sensitive data (emails, contacts) remain confidential
• Never shared with unauthorized third-party services
• Minimal access to external APIs

📋 Best practices:
• Automatic logout after inactivity
• Ability to revoke connector access
• Audit logs of sensitive actions

💾 Durability:
• Automatic daily database backups (7 days / 4 weeks / 6 months of history kept)
• Restore procedure tested for real — an incident cannot cost you more than the last day

🧬 Software supply chain:
• Every release ships a locked, cryptographically verified list of components (reproducible builds)
• All dependencies — including indirect ones — are automatically scanned for known vulnerabilities

q3.question: What data does LIA collect?
q3.answer:
LIA only collects data necessary for its operation:

📋 Data collected:
• Profile: name, email, language, timezone
• Conversations: history of your exchanges with LIA
• Connectors: OAuth tokens (not your passwords)
• Preferences: theme, personality, settings
• Statistics: number of messages, tokens consumed
• Home address: optional, encrypted in database (for 'at home' queries)

❌ Data NOT collected:
• Your Google passwords
• The full content of all your emails
• Your Drive files (only those you request)
• Real-time geolocation data (sent on-the-fly, not stored)

🗑️ Right to erasure:
You can request complete deletion of your account and data.

q4.question: Can I delete my account and data?
q4.answer:
Yes, you have a right to complete erasure:

🗑️ What will be deleted:
• Your user account
• All your conversation history
• All your OAuth connectors
• Your preferences and settings
• Your usage statistics
• Your health data (heart rate, steps) and health-ingestion tokens
• Your last known location

⚠️ Irreversible action:
Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

📧 How to proceed:
Contact your administrator to request account deletion.

💡 Alternatives:
• Reset conversation (deletes history)
• Disconnect connectors (revokes access)
• These actions are reversible unlike account deletion

q5.question: Does LIA have access to all my emails/files?
q5.answer:
No, LIA has limited and controlled access:

📧 Gmail:
• LIA searches ONLY when you ask
• It doesn't automatically scan your mailbox
• Emails are not stored on LIA's side
• Temporary cache for performance (few minutes)

📁 Google Drive:
• Access only to files you request
• No automatic scanning of all your files
• Content is not stored permanently

📅 Calendar:
• Reading events on your request
• No continuous monitoring of your schedule

🔐 Principle of least privilege:
LIA only accesses data strictly necessary to respond to your request, at the moment you make it.

q6.question: Do external services see my data?
q6.answer:
Understand the data flow:

🔄 Google Services:
• Your data stays with Google
• LIA queries Google via their official APIs
• Google sees the requests (like in their app)
• Google's privacy policy applies

🌤️ OpenWeatherMap:
• Only receives the requested city name
• No personal data transmitted

📚 Wikipedia:
• Only receives the search query
• Public service, no tracking

🔍 Perplexity:
• Receives your search question
• Perplexity's privacy policy applies

💡 General principle:
LIA transmits the minimum information necessary to each service. Your personal data is never shared unnecessarily.

q7.question: What are passkeys and how do I enable them?
q7.answer:
A passkey lets you sign in with Face ID, your fingerprint or your device code — no password typed, nothing to remember.

🔑 Why it is safer:
• Phishing-resistant: a passkey only works on the real LIA site
• The secret key never leaves your device
• A leaked password becomes useless to an attacker

⚙️ How to enable:
1. Go to Settings > Security > Strong authentication
2. Click Add a passkey and follow your browser (Windows Hello, Face ID, Android…)
3. Optionally name it ("iPhone", "Work PC") and add one per device

On the login page, your browser will then offer the passkey directly in the email field (or use the "Sign in with a passkey" button).

q8.question: How do I add a second verification step (TOTP)?
q8.answer:
The authenticator app adds a 6-digit code as a second step to password sign-in.

⚙️ Setup:
1. Settings > Security > Authenticator app (TOTP) → Enable
2. Scan the QR code with Google Authenticator, 1Password, Aegis…
3. Enter the 6-digit code shown by the app

🔒 Backup codes: 10 single-use codes are shown exactly once — store them safely; each one replaces the app code if you lose your phone. You can regenerate a fresh set at any time (the old set is invalidated).

Signing in then takes two steps: password, then the current code from your app.

q9.question: Why does LIA sometimes ask me to confirm my identity?
q9.answer:
Sensitive actions are protected by an identity confirmation (a "step-up"):

🛡️ Protected actions:
• Managing passkeys and the authenticator app
• Exporting your data
• Signing out all other devices
• Disabling password sign-in

⏱️ How it behaves:
• Right after signing in, nothing is asked for 5 minutes
• Afterwards, one quick confirmation (password, code, passkey — or a fresh Google sign-in for Google accounts) re-opens the window

The point: even if someone borrows your open session, they cannot quietly lock you out or walk away with your data.

q10.question: How do I see and disconnect the devices connected to my account?
q10.answer:
Settings > Security > My devices lists every live session of your account.

💻 What you see:
• Browser and system families (e.g. "chrome · windows") — never the full technical detail
• A truncated IP (e.g. 192.168.1.x) and coarse last-activity time
• The device name when it is registered for push notifications

🔌 What you can do:
• Sign out one device — it loses access immediately, even mid-conversation
• Sign out all other devices (asks for an identity confirmation)

🔔 New sign-in alerts: your devices receive a push notification when the account signs in from an unrecognized device — the toggle to turn it off is in the same section.

q11.question: How do I export all my data (GDPR)?
q11.answer:
You can download a complete archive of your data at any time (GDPR right to portability).

📦 What the archive contains:
• Your profile and settings
• Conversations, memories, journal — as readable Markdown AND structured JSON
• Your uploaded files (attachments, knowledge-space documents)

🚫 What it never contains: connector credentials, security keys, push tokens — secret material is unexportable by design.

⚙️ How: Settings > Security > Export my data → Request an export → a push notification tells you when the ZIP is ready (downloadable for 24 h).

q1.question: How much does using LIA cost?
q1.answer:
LIA pricing depends on your organization:

💰 Cost model:
Costs are based on AI usage:
• Input tokens: your messages and analyzed data
• Output tokens: LIA's responses
• Cache: optimized data reuse

📊 Influencing factors:
• Length of your messages
• Request complexity
• Volume of data processed (emails, files...)
• Frequency of use

📧 Pricing information:
Contact your administrator for pricing applicable to your organization.

q2.question: How can I view my usage?
q2.answer:
Track your usage from the dashboard:

📊 Available statistics:
• Messages: total count and current month
• Tokens: detailed consumption (input/output/cache)
• Cost: monthly cost estimate

📅 Periods:
• Total cumulative since account creation
• Current month (billing cycle)
• Current period with start/end dates

🔄 Update:
Statistics are updated in real-time after each conversation.

💡 Access:
Statistics are displayed directly on the home page (dashboard).

q3.question: Does LIA work on mobile?
q3.answer:
Yes, LIA is fully responsive:

📱 Compatibility:
• Smartphones (iOS and Android)
• Tablets
• Computers (Windows, Mac, Linux)
• All modern browsers

🔄 Synchronization:
• Your conversation syncs in real-time
• Start on PC, continue on mobile
• Same preferences across all devices

💡 Mobile tip:
Add LIA to your home screen for quick access like a native app.

⚠️ Internet connection:
LIA requires an active internet connection to function.

q4.question: Are there usage limits?
q4.answer:
Some technical limits exist to ensure performance:

📊 Limits per request:
• Emails: 50 results maximum per search
• Contacts: 50 results maximum per search
• Drive files: 50 results maximum
• Events: 50 results maximum

📝 Message size:
• Your messages can be long (multiple paragraphs)
• Very long content (files) is truncated

⏱️ No time limit:
• No limit on messages per day
• No restriction on hours of use

💡 Tip:
For broad searches, refine your criteria rather than asking for "all my emails".

q5.question: How do I report a problem or make a suggestion?
q5.answer:
Several ways to contact us:

🐛 Report a bug:
• Describe the problem encountered
• Specify the steps to reproduce it
• Indicate any error message
• Contact your administrator

💡 Make a suggestion:
• Improvement ideas are welcome
• Describe the need or desired feature
• Submit via your administrator

📧 Administrator support:
Your administrator can:
• Manage your account
• Resolve connector issues
• Forward requests to the technical team

💡 Before reporting:
Check this FAQ - your question may already have an answer!

usage_limits.title: Usage Limits
usage_limits.description: Per-user token, message and cost quotas

q1.question: What are usage limits?
q1.answer:
Usage limits are quotas set by your administrator to control resource consumption:

📊 3 dimensions:
• Tokens (prompt + response + cache) — volume of data processed by AI
• Messages — number of messages sent
• Cost (EUR) — combined LLM + Google API cost

📅 2 modes:
• Per period — monthly rolling cycle from account creation
• Global — cumulative total since registration

Each dimension can be set or unlimited.

q2.question: How is the billing period calculated?
q2.answer:
The period is a monthly rolling cycle aligned with your account creation date:

📅 Example:
If you registered on January 15th, your cycle runs from the 15th of each month to the 15th of the next. This is the same period shown on the dashboard.

q3.question: What happens when I reach a limit?
q3.answer:
When a limit is reached:

🔒 Blocking:
• Message input and voice are disabled
• A red banner explains the situation
• Proactive notifications and scheduled actions are also blocked

🔓 To unblock:
• Wait for the next cycle (period limits)
• Contact your administrator to adjust your quotas

q4.question: Can administrators manually block a user?
q4.answer: Yes. Administrators can block or unblock any user instantly via Settings > Administration > Limits Administration. A reason can be provided and will be shown to the user.

q5.question: What types of limits can be set?
q5.answer:
3 dimensions × 2 modes = 6 possible limits:

• Tokens per period or global
• Messages per period or global
• Cost EUR per period or global

Each dimension can be set to a specific value or left unlimited.

q6.question: Are administrators subject to limits?
q6.answer: Yes, all users including administrators are subject to usage limits. However, administrators can adjust their own limits through the admin interface.

q7.question: What happens if no limits are configured?
q7.answer: If no limit record exists for a user, they have unlimited access. Limits are created either automatically at registration (with default values) or manually by an administrator.

q8.question: Where can I see my current usage?
q8.answer:
Your usage is visible on the dashboard via dedicated tiles:

📊 Tiles:
• Period Limits — current cycle consumption
• Global Limits — total consumption since registration

🎨 Color coding:
• 🟢 Green: < 60%
• 🟡 Yellow: 60-80%
• 🟠 Orange: 80-95%
• 🔴 Red: > 95%

q9.question: How does limit enforcement work?
q9.answer:
LIA uses a 5-layer defense-in-depth architecture:

1. Router — HTTP 429 before streaming
2. Service — SSE error for scheduled actions
3. LLM Guard — Centralized check before each LLM call
4. Proactive Runner — Skip blocked users
5. Direct call migration — Full coverage

⚡ Fail-open: If Redis/DB is down, access is allowed (cost control, not security).

voice_mode.title: Voice Mode
voice_mode.description: Speak to LIA and let it answer out loud. Push-to-talk, wake word, transcription languages, and what leaves your device.

q1.question: How do I activate voice mode?
q1.answer: Go to Settings > Voice Mode and enable it. A voice badge appears in the chat header. Long-press the badge to toggle voice mode on/off. When enabled, you can say "OK Guy" (wake word) or tap the badge to start speaking.

q2.question: How does push-to-talk work?
q2.answer: When voice mode is off and the text field is empty, hold the send button to record your voice. Release to stop — LIA transcribes your speech and places the text in the input field. Works on desktop and mobile.

q3.question: Does voice recognition support my language?
q3.answer: Yes! LIA uses Whisper (99+ languages) and automatically transcribes in your preferred language configured in Settings. The wake word detection uses an English model ("OK Guy"), but the main speech-to-text works in any language.

q4.question: Is my voice data sent to external services?
q4.answer: By default, no. Wake-word detection runs entirely in your browser (Sherpa-onnx WASM, English-only). Speech-to-text uses Sherpa-onnx Whisper running on LIA's own server (your audio never leaves the LIA server). An optional remote STT mode (Settings -> Voice mode -> Distant) transmits the audio to ElevenLabs Scribe for higher accuracy - opt-in only, off by default, with a clear notice in the Settings panel.

q5.question: Can I use a more accurate (remote) speech-to-text?
q5.answer: Yes. In Settings -> Voice mode you can switch from Local (default, free, Sherpa-onnx Whisper running on the LIA server, audio never leaves) to Distant (ElevenLabs Scribe, $0.22/h, billed by audio duration). The remote mode is more accurate on conversational speech, especially in noisy environments. A discreet 🎤 badge on each user message bubble shows the duration and EUR cost of the transcription. The cost flows into your usual Cost dashboard tile and your usage limits - no separate quota. Two safety levers protect against cost spikes: a hard cap of 5 minutes per clip (admin-tunable), and a global kill switch the administrator can flip to force everyone back to local.

q6.question: Which voices does LIA use for speech, and what does TTS cost?
q6.answer: LIA's voice synthesis is configured by the administrator from a single catalogue with three providers: Edge TTS (Microsoft neural voices, free, default), OpenAI TTS (tts-1 / tts-1-hd, premium voices: alloy, echo, nova, ...), and ElevenLabs (eleven_multilingual_v2 / eleven_turbo_v2_5 / eleven_flash_v2_5, including custom and library voices from the configured account). For paid providers, a 🔊 badge on the assistant message shows the character count and the EUR cost; Edge stays free with no badge. Latency-side: a sentence-level streamer starts playing the first sentence in about 1 second, while the assistant is still composing the rest of the answer.

image_generation.title: AI Image Generation
image_generation.description: Generate and edit images using AI

q1.question: How do I generate an image?
q1.answer: Simply ask the assistant to create an image. For example: "Generate an image of an astronaut cat". The image appears as a card below the response.

q2.question: Can I edit a generated image?
q2.answer: Yes! After generating an image, ask the assistant to modify it: "Make it more realistic". The assistant automatically uses the most recent image.

q3.question: How do I configure quality and size?
q3.answer: Go to Settings > Preferences > AI Image Generation. Choose quality (Low/Medium/High), size (Square/Portrait/Landscape), and format (PNG/WebP). Higher quality costs more.

q4.question: How much does image generation cost?
q4.answer: For gpt-image-1: Low $0.011-$0.016, Medium $0.042-$0.063, High $0.167-$0.250 per image. Costs appear in the debug panel.

q5.question: How do I download a generated image?
q5.answer: Three options: (1) Click the download button (arrow icon) that appears when hovering over the image — on mobile, the button is always visible. (2) Click the image to open full-screen, then use the download button in the top-right corner. (3) On mobile, long-press the image to use the native "Save Image" menu.

q6.question: Is there a limit to how many images I can generate?
q6.answer: Two safeguards apply. Your account's usage limits (cost caps per billing cycle, set by the administrator) cover image generation costs like any other cost. On top of that, a technical rate limit protects against runaway loops: by default, 10 image generations (and 10 edits) per 5 minutes per user. Normal use is unaffected — if the limit is reached, the assistant tells you how long to wait before trying again. The administrator can tune the threshold and the window via the IMAGE_GENERATION_RATE_LIMIT_CALLS and IMAGE_GENERATION_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW environment variables.

health_metrics.title: Health data
health_metrics.description: Ingestion API to push heart rate and steps from any source

q1.question: What is the “Health data” section?
q1.answer: A dedicated ingestion API that accepts heart-rate and step measurements from any source: iPhone Shortcuts automation (the documented primary use case), Android scripts, third-party integrations, or compatible IoT devices. Since v1.17.1, ingestion works in batches (up to 1000 samples per request), each measurement carrying its own date_start / date_end interval. Your data is visualized in Settings → Features → Health data as a line chart (HR) and bar chart (steps), with a period selector (hour / day / week / month / year), a dashed line for the period average, and the actual aggregation window displayed in the statistics.

q2.question: How do I set up my iPhone to push data?
q2.answer:
Three steps:

  1. Generate a token from Settings → Features → Health data → Ingestion API. The token starts with hm_ and is shown once only — copy it immediately. The same token authenticates both endpoints (steps + heart rate).
  2. Create two iOS Shortcuts (one per kind) that fetch the day's Apple Health samples and send them as a JSON array (each measurement carries date_start / date_end in ISO 8601 with timezone) to https://your-lia-domain/api/v1/ingest/health/steps and .../heart_rate, with the header Authorization: Bearer hm_….
  3. Schedule an automation — on iPhone unlock or at a fixed time — that runs both Shortcuts. Re-sending the same day is free: the server deduplicates automatically.

👉 Step-by-step guide: docs/guides/GUIDE_IPHONE_SHORTCUTS_HEALTH.md.

q3.question: What data is sent and stored?
q3.answer:
Each request is an array of self-timestamped samples:

  • For steps: {date_start, date_end, steps, o} — the measurement interval and the step count over it.
  • For heart rate: {date_start, date_end, heart_rate, o} — the interval and the bpm value.

The server UTC-normalizes dates and applies per-sample physiological validation: HR outside [20, 250] bpm or steps outside [0, 15,000] are individually rejected with their index and a bounded reason (valid siblings in the same batch persist). When Apple Watch and iPhone measure the same period, LIA merges them intelligently: MAX for steps, rounded average for heart rate. No raw values are ever logged by the server (GDPR compliant).

q4.question: How do I delete my health data?
q4.answer:
In Settings → Features → Health data → Data management three actions are available:

  • Delete heart rates: deletes every heart-rate measurement (steps preserved).
  • Delete steps: deletes every step measurement (HR preserved).
  • Delete everything: erases every measurement permanently (your ingestion tokens remain active).

If you delete your LIA account, all health data is wiped automatically (SQL cascade).

q5.question: Is my token safe if intercepted?
q5.answer:
Yes. The token is treated like a password:

  • SHA-256 hash stored — the raw value is never persisted. Nobody (not even a LIA admin) can recover it after creation.
  • Shown only once: only an 8-char prefix (hm_xxxxxxxx…) remains visible for identification.
  • Revocable individually at any time from the UI. You can issue several (one per device) and manage them independently.
  • Scoped to a single endpoint: a token only authorizes health-data ingestion, never account reads or other actions.
  • Rate limit: 60 requests per hour per token (Redis sliding window, configurable) to block spam while accommodating bursts when the iPhone unlocks. Max batch size: 1000 samples per request (HTTP 413 beyond).

q6.question: How do I ask LIA about my health data?
q6.answer:
Enable the Settings → Health data → Assistant toggle (off by default, opt-in). While off, no health data ever reaches the LLM. Once on, you can:

  • Ask factual questions in chat: “How many steps today?”, “My heart rate this week?”, “Steps day by day over the last 7 days?”, “Am I walking less than usual?”, “Anything unusual in my health lately?”. LIA answers with factual figures (totals, averages, deltas vs baseline) — never medical diagnosis.
  • Receive proactive notifications that combine health + weather + calendar (“Sunny today and 4 days of inactivity → short walk?”).
  • Enrich your memories and internal journals with biometric context at capture time (only deltas and trends — never raw values).

A single switch governs these 4 integrations. The 28-day rolling baseline qualifies comparisons honestly (“based on only N days of data” while history is under 7 days).
