meta.title: LIA — Open Source Personal AI Assistant | Multi-Agent, HITL, 6 Languages
meta.description: LIA orchestrates 19+ specialized AI agents to manage your emails, calendar, contacts, Drive and more. Open source, human validation (HITL), 7 LLM providers, 6 languages. Privacy by design.

hero.subtitle_top:
LIA isn't just another chatbot.
She's an AI that knows you — and has a character of her own.
hero.subtitle_line1: She remembers what matters, notices what changes, tunes in to your mood.
hero.subtitle_line2: Behind the scenes, she orchestrates your emails, your calendar, your home.
hero.subtitle_line3: You keep the power to say yes — or no.
hero.intro_paragraph: LIA is an open-source personal AI assistant that orchestrates 19+ specialized agents to manage your emails, calendar, contacts, files, tasks, reminders, web search, weather, routes, and smart home. Compatible with Google Workspace, Apple iCloud, and Microsoft 365, LIA works in natural language with human validation of every sensitive action. Available in 6 interface languages, with voice mode and 7 LLM providers to choose from.

chat_mockup.aria: Animated demo: four real scenes — LIA orchestrates several agents in parallel and waits for your approval, crosses the weather with your agenda on her own initiative, places a real phone call to book a table, and builds a mini-app right in the chat. The orchestration backstage shows while she works.
chat_mockup.s1_user: I'll be 30 min late tonight — let my wife know and push back my 6:30 pm meeting
chat_mockup.s1_wait: 🐹 Waking up the hamster in the wheel…
chat_mockup.s1_bs_query: “late tonight · tell my wife · move the meeting”
chat_mockup.s1_bs_gate: Your call — nothing leaves without you
chat_mockup.s1_bs_note: 3 tasks in parallel · the flow waits for your approval
chat_mockup.s1_hitl: Found Sophie, and your 6:30 pm “Project sync”. Send the email and move it to 7 pm?
chat_mockup.s1_draft_quote: “Traffic has decided to stress-test our marriage. Verdict at 8 pm…”
chat_mockup.s1_done: Email sent to Sophie · 📅 “Project sync” moved to 7 pm
chat_mockup.s2_user: What's the weather tomorrow morning? I was planning to run before work
chat_mockup.s2_bs_note: Nobody asked — LIA crosses your data on her own and proposes the fix.
chat_mockup.s2_initiative: Showers right on your 7:30 “Morning run 🏃”. Thursday 7 am: full sun, 14°. Want me to move it?
chat_mockup.s3_user: Call Gino's and book a table for 4 on Friday night
chat_mockup.s3_hitl: I'll call Gino's to book 4 seats Friday around 8 pm — may I?
chat_mockup.s3_bs_gate: Approved: call Gino's · goal: book a table
chat_mockup.s3_bs_note: The calling agent only sees your free/busy slots — never your content. No recording, just a written summary.
chat_mockup.s3_done: Booked — they were charming, unlike your calendar.
chat_mockup.s4_user: Build me a little widget to track my hydration
chat_mockup.s4_bs_note: A capability LIA didn't have 5 seconds ago — created by you, in one sentence.
chat_mockup.s4_reply: Installed. Drink, tap, repeat — I'll keep count.

how_it_works.title: How it works
how_it_works.subtitle: From your request to action, in 4 simple steps

step1.title: Ask naturally
step1.description: Talk to LIA like a human assistant. Text, voice, or by attaching photos and documents, in any language you prefer.

step2.title: LIA plans
step2.description: The orchestrator analyzes your request, identifies the right agents, and builds an optimized execution plan.

step3.title: You approve
step3.description: Before any sensitive action, LIA asks for your approval. You stay in control at every step.

step4.title: LIA executes
step4.description: Specialized agents execute the plan in parallel and deliver results in real time.

connected_services.title: Google, Apple iCloud & Microsoft 365
connected_services.description: Emails, calendar and contacts via Google, Apple iCloud or Microsoft 365 — your choice. Plus Google Drive and tasks via Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do. All in natural language, regardless of your provider.

smart_home.title: Smart Home (Philips Hue)
smart_home.description: Control your smart lights by voice: turn on/off, adjust brightness and colors, manage rooms and scenes. Just say "dim the living room" or "activate movie mode". Local or cloud connection.

web_intelligence.title: Search, Weather & Navigation
web_intelligence.description: Multi-source web search (Brave, Perplexity, Wikipedia), real-time weather and 5-day forecasts, nearby places and businesses search, multi-mode route planning (car, walk, bike, transit), automatic geolocation.

voice_mode.title: Voice mode, local recognition
voice_mode.description: Talk to LIA and listen to her responses. Wake word and speech recognition run entirely in your browser — nothing is sent before you speak to LIA. Natural multi-engine speech synthesis. Also works via Telegram audio messages.

natural_language.title: Natural language
natural_language.description: No commands to memorize. Ask what you want like you would a human assistant, LIA understands and acts.

multi_agent.title: 19+ specialized agents
multi_agent.description: Emails, calendar, contacts, files, tasks, weather, web search, Wikipedia, places, routes, reminders and more. A single request automatically activates the right agents.

proactive.title: Proactive intelligence
proactive.description: Push notifications at the right time (weather, meetings, tasks). Themes rotate so the same topic never comes back day after day, and when a notification builds on one of your interests it names real, fresh facts with clickable sources. During conversations, LIA proactively cross-references related information: rain forecast + outdoor event, email with meeting proposal + calendar conflict. Fully configurable.

interests.title: Interest tracking
interests.description: Follow topics you're passionate about (tech, sports, finance, health...). LIA automatically searches relevant content and pushes it as notifications — themes rotate for variety, and every notification links to its sources.

telephony.title: LIA can call for you
telephony.description: Ask LIA to place a real phone call on your behalf — reach a contact, ask a quick question, check a slot. You approve who it calls and why before it dials; LIA holds the conversation, then drops a written summary back into the chat, with a one-tap follow-up when useful. And never a commitment without you: any unplanned expense or option is noted with its price, never accepted — you make the call.

reminders_scheduling.title: Reminders & automations
reminders_scheduling.description: Schedule reminders in natural language ("Remind me tomorrow at 9am to call Marie"). Plan recurring automatic actions (Monday email summary, morning weather...).

memory.title: Contextual memory
memory.description: LIA remembers your preferences, habits, and important information. She improves with every interaction for increasingly relevant responses.

rich_responses.title: Rich visual responses
rich_responses.description: Choose your display mode: interactive HTML cards, rich HTML rendering or plain Markdown. Emails, events, contacts, weather, routes — everything adapts to your preferences. Syntax-highlighted code blocks, math formulas (LaTeX) and a copy button on every message to grab the content in one click.

multichannel.title: Web, Telegram & push
multichannel.description: Use LIA from your browser, Telegram, or receive push notifications on your mobile. Your conversations synchronized everywhere.

personalities.title: 14 personalities
personalities.description: Professor, Friend, Philosopher, Cynic, Influencer, Enthusiastic, Poet, Coach and many more. Choose the tone that suits you, LIA adapts every response.

psyche.title: Living emotional intelligence
psyche.description: LIA doesn't recite — it feels. 14 moods, 22 emotions, a relationship that deepens message after message. Its vocabulary warms when touched, sentences shorten under tension, humor surfaces when the exchange is light. And you can see it: LIA's mood face animates on the current reply. And it follows you: a floating companion keeps LIA present across the whole dashboard.

mcp.title: Extensible (MCP)
mcp.description: Connect your own MCP servers to extend LIA without limits. Iterative mode available: a dedicated agent reads the server documentation then calls tools correctly — ideal for complex APIs.

mcp_apps.title: Interactive MCP Apps
mcp_apps.description: Interactive widgets right in the conversation: forms, visualizations, mini-applications — all in real time thanks to the MCP Apps protocol.

excalidraw.title: Diagrams & schemas
excalidraw.description: Generate Excalidraw diagrams directly in LIA. Describe what you want, the AI creates the visual: architectures, workflows, org charts and more.

attachments.title: Photos & file attachments
attachments.description: Attach photos and PDF documents to your messages via the 📎 button or by drag and drop. LIA analyzes visual content, extracts text and reasons about documents.

languages.title: Multilingual
languages.description: Interface in 6 languages. LIA understands and responds in 99+ languages, with multilingual voice synthesis for a fully natural experience.

control.title: You stay in control
control.description: Before any sensitive action (sending email, modifying calendar...), LIA shows you her plan and waits for your approval. Nothing happens without your consent. And while LIA writes, a stop button lets you interrupt the answer at any moment — the partial text stays. And after each answer, a discreet line reveals exactly what LIA did — the steps, tools and reasoning behind it.

privacy.title: Protected data
privacy.description: No sharing of your data with third parties. Sensitive information encrypted, isolated sessions, automatic personal data filtering. CSV export of your personal consumption data. GDPR compliant.

simplicity.title: Simple in a few clicks
simplicity.description: No technical skills required. Intuitive interface, guided setup, everything works naturally from the first use.

themes.title: Customizable
themes.description: 5 color themes, dark/light mode, 9 font families. Adapt LIA to your style.

skills.title: Skills with maps & mini-apps
skills.description: Supercharge LIA with custom expert skills that render maps, dashboards and mini-apps right in the chat. Describe them in natural language — LIA creates and installs them instantly — or import your own.

health_metrics.title: Health data
health_metrics.description: Push heart rate and step counts from any source. Visualization by period, automatic deduplication, dedicated revocable token.

sub_agents.title: Sub-Agents
sub_agents.description: Delegate complex tasks to specialized ephemeral experts working in parallel for deeper research, multi-source analysis, and expert synthesis.

rag_spaces.title: Knowledge Spaces
rag_spaces.description: Upload documents in 15+ formats (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, and more) or sync Google Drive folders directly. LIA automatically indexes and enriches its responses via hybrid search (semantic + keyword).

browser_control.title: Browser Control
browser_control.description: Navigate websites autonomously: search products, fill forms, extract data from dynamic pages powered by JavaScript. Follow the navigation in real time with progressive screenshots displayed directly in the conversation.

self_knowledge.title: App Self-Knowledge
self_knowledge.description: LIA can answer questions about itself using its built-in FAQ knowledge base — ask about features, capabilities, setup, or how things work.

journals.title: Personal Journals
journals.description: The assistant develops a stratified perspective over time — observations, directives, transversal patterns, portrait facets — that gets refined through deferred self-evaluation and diffuses a coherent user-model portrait across every channel where LIA speaks.

responsive.title: PWA & Responsive Design
responsive.description: Installable Progressive Web App with a fully optimized interface for desktop, tablet, and smartphone — use LIA anywhere, on any device, even offline-ready

usage_limits.title: Usage Quotas
usage_limits.description: Per-user limits on tokens, messages and cost with real-time monitoring and 5-layer enforcement. Administrators control budgets with instant block/unblock.

image_generation.title: AI Image Generation
image_generation.description: Generate images from text descriptions, refine them, or edit your own photos sent as attachments. Adjustable quality and built-in cost tracking.

devops_cli.title: DevOps CLI (Admin)
devops_cli.description: Administrators diagnose servers in natural language: Docker logs, container health, disk space — Claude Code CLI embedded in the API container.

briefing.title: Today briefing
briefing.description: Every morning, your day at a glance: personalized synthesis, weather, agenda, birthdays, reminders, health, unread emails, your tracked commitments, overdue tasks and freshly edited documents — before you even ask.

use_cases.title: Real requests, not demos.
use_cases.subtitle: One sentence is enough — LIA splits it up, runs the right specialists in parallel, and asks for your approval when it’s sensitive.
use_cases.intro: Every example below is a genuine user request, verbatim.

example1.query: Find the 3 best cafés near my location that are open right now and give me walking directions to get there
example1.description: LIA activates 3 agents in parallel: geolocation for your current position, place search with an "open now" filter, and pedestrian route calculation. Results are displayed as interactive cards with distances and walking times.

example2.query: Send an email to my wife and son to explain I'll be 30 minutes late. Write it in a slightly humorous tone to soften the blow
example2.description: LIA retrieves contacts from memory, drafts an email in the requested tone, and sends it to both recipients after your approval. Personality and writing style adapt to your instructions.

example3.query: What time do I need to leave to arrive at Bastille tomorrow at 9pm by public transport?
example3.description: The route agent calculates travel time by public transit and deduces the optimal departure time. Results displayed as an interactive card with journey steps.

example4.query: Create a reminder the day before at 7pm for each of my appointments this week
example4.description: LIA checks your calendar, identifies all appointments for the week, and creates an evening reminder for each one via automatic FOR_EACH iteration — a single request is all it takes.

example5.query: Which day this week will be best for an outdoor walk and what are 3 places near Strasbourg that would be great for it, ideally near a nice café
example5.description: LIA cross-references 5-day weather forecasts, searches for walking spots near Strasbourg, and filters those near a café. Three agents work in parallel for a complete recommendation.

example6.query: Call the practice and ask if they have a slot on Thursday
example6.description: You approve who she calls and why; she phones, gets the slot, and books it in your calendar with the written summary.

security.title: Security & Privacy
security.subtitle: Powerful by nature. Private by design.
security.intro: LIA was designed from day one with a privacy-by-design approach. Unlike centralized cloud assistants, your credentials never pass through the frontend: the Backend-for-Frontend architecture completely isolates your tokens. Automatic PII filtering prevents personally identifiable data from reaching LLM providers. Your account itself is locked down: passkeys, a second factor and identity confirmation for sensitive actions, with every connected device visible and revocable.

data_control.title: Data control
data_control.description: Your data stays private. No third-party sharing, isolated sessions, access strictly limited to what is needed. "My devices" shows every live session and revokes any of them instantly. Automatic daily backups with a tested restore procedure.

bff.title: Secure architecture
bff.description: BFF pattern with HTTP-only cookies, Redis sessions, tokens never exposed to the frontend. WebAuthn passkeys and TOTP second factor; sensitive actions are guarded by step-up re-authentication. Strict Content-Security-Policy and OWASP Top 10 protection.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.description: Fernet-encrypted credentials, bcrypt passwords, OAuth tokens secured with distributed Redis locks.

gdpr.title: GDPR compliant
gdpr.description: Automatic PII filtering, pseudonymization, data minimization. Full-account export — readable Markdown, structured JSON and your files — with secret material unexportable by construction. European regulations respected.

tech.title: Under the hood
tech.subtitle: An architecture built for performance and scalability
tech.intro:
Not a chatbot: an orchestration system. Every request flows through semantic routing, a planner and agents executed in parallel — instrumented end to end, from token to euro, with email alerts on vital signals.

Behind the interface: Bayesian plan learning, hybrid BM25 + embeddings memory, a LangGraph state machine checkpointed in PostgreSQL. All of it self-hostable — down to a Raspberry Pi.

What it states, it read: every answer is anchored on the data actually retrieved — never on the memory of an earlier phrasing — and information that was never obtained is announced as missing rather than filled in.

langgraph.title: LangGraph
langgraph.description: Agent orchestration with state graphs, wave-based parallel execution, and Bayesian plan pattern learning. A typed semantic layer connects data across domains, under an execution guardrail. Each iteration of a bulk run keeps its own results, including when a run is replayed.

llm_providers.title: 7 LLM providers
llm_providers.description: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Perplexity, Ollama. Dynamic selection of the best model per task type.

bayesian.title: Bayesian learning
bayesian.description: High-confidence planning patterns bypass semantic validation. The system improves with use.

hybrid_search.title: Hybrid search
hybrid_search.description: BM25 + multilingual semantic embeddings. Fast, accurate contextual memory in every language you speak.

realtime.title: Real-time streaming
realtime.description: See each execution step in real time — routing, planning, validation, tool calls — then watch the response stream token by token. No black box, no waiting. Generation itself is detached from the connection: answers keep executing server-side through disconnects, replay on reattach, and stop on demand.

stack.title: Modern stack
stack.description: FastAPI, Next.js, React, TailwindCSS, PostgreSQL, Redis. Strict TypeScript on the frontend, async Python on the backend. Installable PWA: 6 localized manifests, OS share into chat, offline page and smart asset caching — API responses are never cached.

telephony.title: Agentic telephony
telephony.description: Outbound voice calls handled by a goal-directed agent through your own ElevenLabs connector. Data protection is enforced by capability, not by prompt: the call agent can only read free/busy availability — never event titles, attendees or content. No recording, the transcript is never stored; only a short, expiring summary is reinjected asynchronously through a signed per-user webhook.

rich_skills.title: Skills with frames & images
rich_skills.description: SkillScriptOutput contract (text/frame/image) — sandboxed Python scripts, strict sandbox iframes with injected CSP, auto-resize, theme + locale sync via postMessage. One hardened import pipeline for every path (uploads, chat-generated skills, https URL install through the SSRF validator): strict name validation, zip-expansion caps, atomic install with rollback. Gallery with previews and declared output channels.

hitl.title: Human-in-the-Loop
hitl.description: Six approval levels — plan approval, clarification, draft critique, destructive confirm, FOR_EACH confirm, modifier review. Plan-level guardrails before execution rather than rollback after failure. Automatic risk classification and preview of affected items.

multi-agent-orchestration.title: How LIA Orchestrates 16 Specialized AI Agents
multi-agent-orchestration.excerpt: Discover LIA's multi-agent system: an intelligent router directs each request to the right agent using LangGraph, a planner, and a parallel task orchestrator.
multi-agent-orchestration.body:
An 8-node graph at the heart of the system

When you send a message to LIA, it doesn't go directly to a language model. It traverses a LangGraph state machine composed of 8 nodes: compaction, router_v3, planner, task_orchestrator, approval_gate, semantic_validator, clarification and response. Each node is a specialized asynchronous function with conditional transitions.

A unified intelligence router

The router_v3 node uses QueryAnalyzerService.analyze_full() for a unified analysis of each message. The result is a RouterOutput containing: the intent (action or conversation), a confidence score, the list of detected domains and the router's reasoning. If the intent is conversational, the flow passes directly to the response node. If it is actionable, the flow passes to the planner to generate a structured plan.

A rich state with token management

The LangGraph state (MessagesState) is a TypedDict with over 50 fields. It uses a custom add_messages_with_truncate reducer based on tiktoken to handle token-based truncation, message windowing and OpenAI message sequence validation. This state is checkpointed in PostgreSQL via the LangGraph persistence system.

Native parallel execution

For actionable requests ("send an email and create an event"), LIA generates a structured ExecutionPlan via the planner node. The task orchestrator analyzes the dependency graph and executes independent steps in parallel using native asyncio.gather() (Phase 5.2B), significantly reducing response time for multi-domain requests.

Specialized agents per domain

Each domain has its own agent: emails, calendar, contacts, tasks, Drive, weather, routes, web search, Wikipedia, smart home, and more. Each agent has dedicated tools, a specialized prompt and its own context. This separation allows LIA to automatically coordinate multiple agents for cross-cutting requests like "send my next meeting details to all participants".

Persistence and recovery

The complete state of each conversation is checkpointed in PostgreSQL via the LangGraph persistence system. If interrupted, the conversation resumes exactly where it left off, with all context preserved — including plans in progress and pending approvals. Each worker talks to PostgreSQL through a dedicated connection pool, so simultaneous conversations never queue behind one another to save their state — and a dropped connection is detected and replaced automatically.

execution-plans.title: ExecutionPlan: How LIA Plans and Executes Complex Requests
execution-plans.excerpt: LIA decomposes your multi-step requests into structured execution plans, semantically validated and executed in parallel for fast, reliable responses.
execution-plans.body:
A structured plan language

LIA's planner generates an ExecutionPlan: a validated Pydantic object containing a plan_id (UUID), an execution_mode (sequential or parallel), a max_cost_usd, an estimated_cost_usd and a version number. Each plan contains a list of ExecutionStep with the fields: step_id, step_type (TOOL, CONDITIONAL, REPLAN or HUMAN), agent_name, tool_name, parameters, depends_on and timeout_seconds.

For example, for "send a weather summary to John tomorrow morning", the plan would contain: (1) fetch tomorrow's weather, (2) find contact John, (3) compose and send the email — with dependencies 1→3 and 2→3.

The FOR_EACH pattern

For batch operations, steps support a for_each field that iterates over a collection produced by a previous step. The for_each_max parameter limits the number of iterations, and each element error is handled individually without interrupting the entire batch.

Semantic validation with 11 checks

Before any execution, the semantic validator checks 11 types of issues:

  • HALLUCINATED_CAPABILITY — Tool or capability invented by the LLM
  • GHOST_DEPENDENCY — Reference to a non-existent step
  • LOGICAL_CYCLE — Circular dependencies
  • CARDINALITY_MISMATCH — Cardinality incompatibility between steps
  • SCOPE_OVERFLOW / SCOPE_UNDERFLOW — Plan too broad or insufficient
  • WRONG_PARAMETERS — Incorrect parameters for the tool
  • MISSING_STEP — Missing step to fulfill the request
  • DANGEROUS_AMBIGUITY — Ambiguity that could lead to an error
  • IMPLICIT_ASSUMPTION / INSUFFICIENT_CONTENT — Unverified assumptions

Indexable vs Semantic criteria distinction

Beyond the eleven structural checks, the validator enforces a universal planning principle: distinguish indexable criteria (date, identifier, sender, status, location — passed as a tool parameter) from semantic criteria (category, urgency, quality, priority — filtered downstream by the response LLM). When the planner tries to push a conceptual word like « medical » or « urgent » into the search of a literal-search tool (Google Calendar, Gmail, Notion-style stores…), a detection layer flags the leak via word-boundary matching against the hint emitted by the query analyzer. Tool-agnostic mechanism: no current connector or future MCP server requires modification — declarative opt-out via ToolManifest.text_search_mode for stores that expose native semantic search.

Wave-based parallel execution

A DependencyGraph computes execution waves: all steps without dependencies form the first wave and execute in parallel. Subsequent waves wait for their prerequisites to complete. This mechanism handles complex requests involving 3 to 5 different domains with response times comparable to a single request.

Adaptive replanning

If a step fails, the system can dynamically replan via the REPLAN type. For example, if a contact isn't found, LIA can ask the user for clarification rather than abandoning the entire plan.

Self-enriching anti-hallucination registry

LLMs sometimes invent non-existent tools in their plans (e.g. resolve_reference_tool). LIA maintains a persistent registry of hallucinated patterns (hallucinated_tools.json) that auto-updates whenever a new hallucination is detected. During plan validation, every tool is checked against this registry — hallucinated steps are removed and the planner is forced to replan with real catalogue tools. This mechanism eliminates an entire class of execution failures without human intervention.

human-in-the-loop.title: Human-in-the-Loop: 6 Approval Levels to Keep You in Control
human-in-the-loop.excerpt: LIA never takes critical actions without your consent. Its 6-level HITL system protects you against errors and hallucinations.
human-in-the-loop.body:
Why human validation is essential

Language models can hallucinate or misinterpret intent. LIA solves this by placing humans at the center of every critical decision. No email is sent, no event created, no data modified without your explicit validation.

The 6 approval levels

LIA's HITL system classifies each action into 6 levels:

  • Plan Approval — Before executing a multi-step plan, LIA generates a PlanApprovalRequest containing a plan summary and modifiable parameters, then waits for your go-ahead.
  • Clarification — If intent is ambiguous, LIA asks for details rather than guessing.
  • Draft Critique — For emails or messages, LIA submits a draft for approval before sending.
  • Destructive Confirmation — Any deletion or irreversible modification requires explicit confirmation.
  • FOR_EACH Confirmation — For batch operations, each item can be validated individually.
  • Modifier Review — Parameter changes are presented for verification.

5 possible decisions with confidence

The HITL classifier produces a ClassificationResult with 5 possible decisions, each accompanied by a confidence score between 0.0 and 1.0:

  • APPROVE — The action is validated and passes to the task_orchestrator
  • REJECT — The action is refused, the flow is redirected to the response node
  • EDIT — The user modifies parameters via edited_params, a PlanEditor applies the changes
  • REPLAN — The user reformulates their intent via reformulated_intent, the flow returns to the planner
  • AMBIGUOUS — The system asks a clarification_question to resolve the ambiguity

Native LangGraph interruption

Technically, the approval_gate node uses LangGraph's interrupt() function to suspend graph execution and wait for the user's response. The state is persisted in PostgreSQL, allowing asynchronous resumption even after a disconnection.

You always have the last word

At each validation point, classification strategies are composable: based on tool manifests, estimated cost, data sensitivity, and user role. LIA never bypasses this step.

And that last word is honored to the letter: review loops follow a replay-safe pattern (one interrupt() per node execution, checkpointed loop state — ADR-092), so a resume never replays a past LLM or API call. What you approve, after as many edits as you need, is exactly what gets executed.

llm-providers.title: Multi-Provider AI: choose the right model for every task
llm-providers.excerpt: LIA supports many language model providers and lets you configure a different model for each task type: routing, planning, response, agents.
llm-providers.body:
Many providers, one assistant

LIA natively integrates many LLM providers — from proprietary cloud models to locally-run open-source models. Each provider is managed by a dedicated adapter in the LLM factory, and you can add new ones.

56 individually configurable LLM types

LIA defines over 50 LLM types that can be configured separately: router, response, planner, each domain agent, and more. For each type, you can set: provider, model, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens, timeout and reasoning_effort.

For example:

  • A fast, economical model for routing
  • A powerful model for planning
  • A creative model for responses
  • A local model for privacy

Configuration resolution chain

Each LLM configuration follows a 3-level resolution chain: Admin UI (stored in the database) → Environment variables → Code defaults. An LLMConfigOverrideCache provides O(1) lookups without database queries at runtime. Changes made via the admin interface take immediate effect thanks to cache invalidation.

The multi-provider LLM factory

A single entry point for all providers:

def get_llm(
    llm_type: LLMType,
    config_override: LLMAgentConfig | None = None,
) -> BaseChatModel:
    if config_override is None:
        agent_config = get_llm_config_for_agent(
            settings, llm_type
        )
    else:
        agent_config = config_override

    return ProviderAdapter.create_llm(agent_config)

# Each task type uses the model you configured
router_llm = get_llm("router")
planner_llm = get_llm("planner")
response_llm = get_llm("response")

API key security

Provider API keys are encrypted with Fernet (AES-128 CBC + HMAC) before database storage. No key is ever exposed in plaintext in logs or API responses.

Reasoning models

LIA supports reasoning models with 5 levels of reasoning_effort: none, low, medium, high and xhigh. This activates deep reasoning only where needed, optimizing the cost/performance ratio.

100% local deployment

LIA can run entirely locally with open-source models. No data leaves your infrastructure. Just point configuration variables to your local instance.

google-workspace.title: Google Workspace Integration: Gmail, Calendar, Contacts, Drive, Tasks
google-workspace.excerpt: LIA connects to your Google Workspace via OAuth 2.0 to manage your emails, calendar, contacts, Drive files and tasks in natural language.
google-workspace.body:
7 Google APIs, one conversation

LIA integrates 7 Google APIs covering your workspace and beyond: Gmail API, Calendar API, People API v1 (contacts), Drive API, Tasks API, Routes API and Places API. You manage everything from a single interface in natural language.

Complete operations per service

Each service exposes a full set of CRUD operations:

  • Gmail — Search, read, send, reply, forward, label management. Scope: gmail.modify
  • Calendar — Search, create, update, delete events, attendee management. Scope: calendar.events
  • Contacts — Search, create, update, delete via People API v1. Scope: contacts. Field projections optimized to 110 tokens per contact in list mode to minimize LLM consumption
  • Drive — Search, list, download, share files. Scope: drive.readonly
  • Tasks — List, create, update, complete, delete. Scope: tasks

Routes and Places: global APIs

Beyond the Workspace, LIA integrates Google Routes API for route calculation (car, transit, bike, walking) and Google Places API for searching locations, businesses and points of interest. These APIs enrich the assistant's contextual responses.

ConnectorTool architecture

Each service uses a ConnectorTool base class that automatically handles OAuth authentication, token refresh, API client caching, and error handling. Field projections (field masks) are optimized per operation to reduce API response size and token consumption.

OAuth 2.0 security

Access tokens are encrypted in the database via Fernet (AES-128 CBC + HMAC). Token refresh is transparent: if a token expires during an operation, LIA renews it automatically. Requested OAuth scopes are strictly limited to the minimum necessary per service, following the principle of least privilege.

apple-microsoft.title: Apple iCloud and Microsoft 365: Multi-Platform Connectors
apple-microsoft.excerpt: Beyond Google, LIA supports Apple iCloud (Mail, Calendar, Contacts) and Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Calendar, Contacts, To Do) for total flexibility.
apple-microsoft.body:
One assistant, three ecosystems

LIA doesn't lock you into a single ecosystem. Beyond Google Workspace, you can connect Apple iCloud and Microsoft 365 to access your emails, calendars, contacts, and tasks regardless of your provider.

Apple iCloud

Apple does not offer OAuth for third-party applications. LIA therefore uses App-Specific Passwords, generated from appleid.apple.com. This mechanism provides secure access without exposing the main Apple account password:

  • Apple Mail — Email reading and sending via IMAP/SMTP with App-Specific Password authentication
  • Apple Calendar — Event management via the CalDAV protocol
  • Apple Contacts — Search and management via the CardDAV protocol

Microsoft 365

Microsoft integration uses OAuth 2.0 via Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) with the Authorization Code + PKCE flow. Calls go through the unified Microsoft Graph API:

  • Outlook — Emails: read, send, search via Graph API /me/messages
  • Calendar — Events: full CRUD via Graph API /me/events
  • Contacts — Address book via Graph API /me/contacts
  • To Do — Task management via Graph API /me/todo/lists

Provider abstraction: resolve_active_connector()

LIA's architecture relies on a functional category abstraction. The resolve_active_connector() function dynamically determines which provider (Google, Apple or Microsoft) is active for each category: email, calendar, contacts and tasks.

Mutual exclusivity per domain

Only one connector can be active per functional category. This mutual exclusivity is enforced at the database level: activating a Microsoft email connector automatically deactivates the Google or Apple email connector. This guarantees a single source of truth per domain. However, you can mix providers across categories: Gmail for emails, Apple Calendar for your agenda and Microsoft To Do for tasks, for example.

mcp-protocol.title: Model Context Protocol: Extend LIA Infinitely
mcp-protocol.excerpt: Using Anthropic's MCP protocol, LIA can connect to any external service: databases, business APIs, internal tools, and more.
mcp-protocol.body:
What is MCP?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard developed by Anthropic that enables AI assistants to connect to external tool servers. LIA implements this protocol with per-user MCP servers, offering unlimited and personalized extensibility.

Tool discovery and integration

You configure your MCP servers in the LIA interface. On connection, LIA calls list_tools() on each server to dynamically discover available tools. Each MCP tool is wrapped via MCPToolAdapter which extends LangChain's BaseTool, enabling seamless integration into the agent's tool catalog. MCP tools are then usable exactly like native tools.

Secure transport

LIA exclusively uses Streamable HTTP transport for MCP servers. The stdio transport is disabled for security reasons (risk of arbitrary process execution). Each server is subject to individual rate limiting via asyncio.Lock to prevent overload.

4 authentication types

Each MCP server supports one of 4 authentication types:

  • NONE — No authentication (public or internal servers)
  • API_KEY — API key transmitted in headers
  • BEARER — Bearer token for standard REST APIs
  • OAUTH2 — Full OAuth 2.0 with PKCE

All credentials are encrypted with Fernet (AES-128 CBC + HMAC) before database storage. No secret is exposed in plaintext.

Multi-layer security

MCP security relies on several mechanisms:

  • Mandatory HITL — All MCP tools are subject to Human-in-the-Loop validation by default
  • SSRF protection — The validate_http_endpoint() function blocks URLs pointing to internal networks (127.0.0.1, 10.x, 192.168.x, etc.)
  • Health checks — Each MCP server's status is monitored via a dedicated Prometheus gauge
  • Configurable limits — Number of servers (10), tools per server (20), timeout per call (30s)

Iterative mode (ReAct)

Some MCP servers have complex APIs where the static planner can't generate correct parameters upfront. With iterative mode, a dedicated ReAct agent reads the server's documentation first, understands the expected format, then calls tools with correct parameters. This is powered by a generic ReactSubAgentRunner — the same engine used by browser control. Enable it per-server with the iterative_mode toggle.

skills-system.title: Skills: Expert Instructions to Customize LIA
skills-system.excerpt: Import or create specialized skills so LIA masters new domains — with interactive maps, mini-dashboards, and images on top of text.
skills-system.body:
What is a skill?

A skill is a set of structured instructions that enables LIA to master a specific domain. Unlike tools that execute actions, skills enrich the reasoning and behavior of the assistant. The architecture relies on a key principle: the disk is the source of truth for skill content, while the database only manages metadata (activation, owner, statistics).

Five skill archetypes

  • Prompt Expert — Detailed instructions for a domain (e.g., professional writing, financial analysis)
  • Advisory — Tips and best practices (e.g., style guide, quality checklist)
  • Plan Template — Execution plan templates for recurring scenarios
  • Visualizer (v1.16.8) — Python script that emits an interactive iframe (map, dashboard, calendar)
  • Generator (v1.16.8) — Python script that emits an image artifact (QR code, chart)

Sandboxed execution

Executable skills run in a sandboxed environment via subprocess (never shell=True). The execution environment is filtered: only the PATH, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL and TZ variables are passed to the child process. On Linux, network isolation is ensured via unshare to prevent any network access from a skill script.

Structured result

Each skill execution returns a standardized ScriptResult object containing: success (boolean), output (stdout), error (stderr), exit_code and execution_time_ms. This format allows the system to uniformly handle successes and errors.

Rich outputs (v1.16.8)

Since v1.16.8, a Python script can return — on top of text — an interactive HTML frame (Google Maps view, weather dashboard, Pomodoro timer...) and/or an image (QR code, chart). The contract is simple: the script writes a JSON object on stdout (SkillScriptOutput) with text (required), frame, and image fields — independent and combinable. Frames run in a strict sandbox iframe (allow-scripts allow-popups; allow-same-origin is reserved for trusted system-skill embeds such as the interactive map, which need it to load their own data), with a Content Security Policy auto-injected for user-imported skills — system skills are exempt (trusted admin). Theme and locale sync live via postMessage: flipping dark mode propagates instantly inside every frame without a reload. Seven new built-in skills showcase the mechanism: interactive-map, weather-dashboard, calendar-month, qr-code, pomodoro-timer, unit-converter, dice-roller.

SkillBypassStrategy: bypassing the planner

When a deterministic skill exactly matches the request, the SkillBypassStrategy short-circuits the LLM planner. The skill is executed directly without going through the planner → validator → orchestrator chain, reducing latency and token consumption.

Planner skill guard

The planner has an early detection feature that asks for clarification when required parameters are missing. However, multi-domain deterministic skills (e.g., daily briefing = events + tasks + weather + emails) can trigger false-positive clarifications. The skill guard detects when a deterministic skill has high domain overlap with the query and lets the full planner pipeline decide instead of short-circuiting to clarification.

The Skill Generator

LIA includes a built-in skill generator. Describe the desired domain expertise in natural language, and LIA automatically generates a structured skill in SKILL.md format compatible with the agentskills.io standard — including the new Visualizer and Generator archetypes with their runtime conventions (theme, locale, auto-resize). The finished skill is validated and installed directly into your skills — announced by name, active immediately, no manual upload.

User management

Each user can activate, deactivate, import, or delete their skills in the Settings interface — now a gallery with preview images and declared output channels (text, interactive frame, image). Importing accepts a file or an https URL validated server-side (same hardened pipeline), and every skill imported from outside carries a provenance warning. Administrators can also define global skills available to all users.

Interactive widgets are built to last: they are stored with the conversation and reopen after a reload or on another device, and a frame that cannot load shows an actionable error state — explanation, retry, open in a new tab — instead of a blank rectangle.

voice-mode.title: Voice Mode: Talk to LIA Like a Personal Assistant
voice-mode.excerpt: LIA's voice domain combines a free local STT (Sherpa-onnx Whisper, opt-in remote ElevenLabs Scribe for higher accuracy) and a catalogue-driven TTS (Edge / OpenAI / ElevenLabs). Sentence-level streaming brings the first audio chunk in ~1 second. Per-message cost attribution makes paid voice calls fully auditable.
voice-mode.body:
Three activation modes

LIA supports three ways to interact by voice:

  • Wake word — say "OK Guy" to start listening hands-free. Detection runs entirely in the browser via Sherpa-onnx WASM (English-only model). No audio leaves the browser for wake-word detection.
  • Push-to-talk — hold the microphone button to speak. Optimized for mobile.
  • Automatic end-of-speech detection (VAD) — listening stops automatically after ~0.75 s of silence.

Speech-to-text: local default, remote opt-in

Each user picks an STT mode in Settings → Voice mode:

  • Local (default, free) — Sherpa-onnx Whisper running on the LIA server in 16 kHz mono with INT8 quantization. Supports 99+ languages. Audio never leaves the LIA server.
  • Remote (opt-in) — ElevenLabs Scribe at $0.22/h, billed by audio duration. Higher accuracy on conversational speech, especially in noisy environments. A discreet 🎤 badge on each user message bubble surfaces the duration and EUR cost; the cost flows into your usual Cost dashboard tile and your usage limits — no separate quota.

Two admin-side safety levers protect against cost spikes when remote is enabled: a global kill switch (ELEVENLABS_STT_ENABLED) and a per-clip duration cap (ELEVENLABS_STT_MAX_AUDIO_DURATION_SECONDS, default 300 s) verified before any provider call.

Catalogue-driven text-to-speech

Voice synthesis is now configured from a single admin form (Configuration LLM → Voice TTS), with three providers seeded from day one:

  • Edge TTS — Microsoft neural voices, free, default. SSML rate / pitch / volume tuning.
  • OpenAI TTS — tts-1 or tts-1-hd, premium voices (alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer). Speed + response_format tuning.
  • ElevenLabs — eleven_multilingual_v2, eleven_turbo_v2_5, eleven_flash_v2_5. Stability, similarity_boost, style and use_speaker_boost tuning. Live voice picker pulls custom and library voices from the configured account.

For paid providers, a 🔊 badge on the assistant message shows the character count and the EUR cost; Edge stays free with no badge. Audio formats supported: MP3, Opus, AAC, FLAC, WAV, PCM — selected per provider.

Sentence-level streaming for sub-second latency

The voice pipeline now dispatches TTS synthesis per complete sentence in parallel, instead of waiting for the full LLM response. The first sentence starts playing in about one second while the assistant is still composing the rest of the answer. A persistent HTTP keep-alive on ElevenLabs saves another ~100–300 ms per sentence on calls #2…N. In-order delivery is enforced via a buffered queue — failed slots are skipped without stalling the stream.

Voice comments and exports

LIA can attach short voice comments (a TTS narrative aside) to its responses. Audio streams over WebSocket with a single-use BFF ticket (60-second TTL) for security. Two new CSV exports — stt-usage and tts-usage — list every paid voice call with its conversation, message ID, provider, duration / characters and EUR cost. The existing consumption-summary export gains STT and TTS columns so totals stay in one place.

knowledge-spaces.title: Knowledge Spaces: Turn Your Documents into AI Intelligence
knowledge-spaces.excerpt: Import your PDFs, Word, Excel and other documents. LIA indexes them with hybrid semantic + BM25 search to answer your questions.
knowledge-spaces.body:
15+ supported formats

LIA's Knowledge Spaces accept over 15 file formats with dedicated parsers:

  • PDF via PyMuPDF (fast and accurate extraction)
  • Documents — DOCX, RTF, ODT
  • Spreadsheets — XLSX, CSV, ODS
  • Presentations — PPTX, ODP
  • Web and text — HTML, Markdown, JSON, XML, EPUB

Intelligent chunking

Documents are split by a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter with optimized parameters: 1000 characters per chunk, 200 characters of overlap to preserve context between segments. Safety limit: 500 chunks maximum per document, maximum size 20 MB per file.

Hybrid search: best of both worlds

LIA combines two search approaches:

  • Semantic search — Embeddings via pgvector. Finds results by meaning similarity, even when words differ.
  • BM25 search — Keyword matching. Ideal for technical terms, proper names, and identifiers.

The final score is weighted with alpha = 0.7 (70% semantic, 30% BM25). The minimum relevance score is 0.5 — results below are filtered out. By default, 5 chunks are retrieved per query (configurable maximum: 20).

Limits and quotas

Each user has: 10 spaces maximum, 50 documents per space, 20 MB per file. These limits ensure optimal search performance while offering sufficient capacity for most use cases.

Google Drive sync

You can connect a Google Drive folder to a Knowledge Space. Documents are automatically synced and re-indexed when they change. Synchronization detects additions, modifications, and deletions.

Built-in FAQ

LIA has a system Knowledge Space containing its own documentation (18 FAQ files). This allows it to answer questions about its own features with precision.

personal-journals.title: Personal Journals: When Your AI Assistant Develops Its Own Memory
personal-journals.excerpt: LIA keeps stratified journals where it notes raw observations, operational directives, transversal patterns, and portrait facets. They get refined turn after turn through a deferred self-evaluation loop, and feed a coherent user-model portrait diffused everywhere LIA speaks.
personal-journals.body:
An introspective, stratified memory

Personal Journals are a defining LIA feature: the assistant keeps a thematic personal journal where it notes reflections, observations about the user, ideas, and learnings. But unlike a flat notepad, these notes are organized along four abstraction levels, each entry carries an epistemic status (confidence + evidence/contradiction counters), and the journal as a whole compiles a living user-model portrait that travels with LIA across every channel.

4 themes

Each entry is classified into one of 4 themes:

  • SELF_REFLECTION — Reflections on its own functioning and interactions
  • USER_OBSERVATIONS — Stable signals about your preferences, habits, communication style
  • IDEAS_ANALYSES — Cross-cutting patterns, hypotheses, recurring contradictions
  • LEARNINGS — Concrete lessons anchored in past corrections or successful approaches

4 abstraction levels (since v1.20.0)

Each entry also carries a level that captures how distilled it is:

  • L0 — raw observation: a weak signal worth tracking, before it can be turned into a directive ("User just laughed at my reply but I can't tell if warm or ironic — track").
  • L1 — operational directive: the format WHEN [context] → DO [action] (BECAUSE [evidence]). The default at extraction.
  • L2 — transversal pattern: a synthesis of several convergent L1 directives. Produced exclusively at consolidation, by topic clustering.
  • L3 — portrait facet: a piece of the user model — traits, current phase, contexts, contradictions, blind spots, evolution. Consolidation only.

Epistemic status — hypothesis, observed, validated

Each entry exposes a confidence dot (low / medium / high) plus two counters: evidence (times the user confirmed) and contradiction (times the user pushed back). LIA can now distinguish entries that are still being tested from those validated across many turns — and quietly demote directives the user keeps contradicting.

Deferred self-evaluation: T → T+1

The most striking mechanism: at every turn, LIA looks at the directives it injected on the previous turn and reads your reaction in the current message. If you confirmed (smooth engagement, thanks, visible benefit), the evidence counter ticks up. If you pushed back, reformulated, or corrected, contradiction ticks up. The journal therefore measures its own usefulness — and at zero added LLM cost: same extraction call, just an enriched prompt with the previous turn's directives.

The user-model portrait, diffused everywhere

The same consolidation call now also compiles a portrait of you in two formats: a full version (~200 tokens) used in conversation and planner prompts, and a brief version (~60 tokens) diffused across the secondary flows — ReAct, voice, reminders, heartbeat notifications, proactive interest pings, fallback responses. The same nuanced model of you, carried everywhere LIA speaks. Your assistant doesn't "forget who you are" depending on the surface it speaks through.

Three corrective levers (no direct portrait edit)

The portrait is a synthesis voice — never directly editable. Three levers replace direct editing:

  • Edit L3 source entries — standard CRUD on entries flagged level=L3. The portrait recompiles on the next consolidation.
  • 🚩 Signal a problem — opens a free-text dialog. Submitting it creates a special user_correction entry and triggers a synchronous re-consolidation (~5–10 s) that re-weights L3 entries with your signal pinned at the top of the prompt.
  • 🔄 Consolidate now — runs the full consolidation cycle on demand, bypassing the cooldown.

Smart filters, badges, group-by

The Settings panel now shows badges for confidence, level, and usage count on every entry. A toggle lets you group by Theme or by Level, and a filter surfaces only entries that have never been used (zero uses, no last-injection date) — instant visibility on directives that never proved useful, ready to be reformulated or pruned at the next consolidation.

Data integrity: four anti-hallucination layers

LLMs can hallucinate UUIDs and counter values when updating entries. LIA defends with four layers: prompt-level guidance with ID reference tables, schema-level UUID validation that rejects malformed IDs, runtime filtering that drops actions referencing non-existent entries, and atomic counter increments — the LLM only signals an outcome (evidence or contradiction), the service owns the integers.

User control and privacy

You can read, edit (level + confidence included), export, and delete your journals in Settings > Features. The export now includes the compiled portrait. When you delete your account, the portrait is scrubbed alongside the entries. The feature is fully disableable per user — when off, data is preserved but never used.

proactive-notifications.title: Proactive Intelligence: Notifications & Initiative
proactive-notifications.excerpt: LIA anticipates your needs: push notifications via Heartbeat, and conversational initiative that cross-references related information in real time.
proactive-notifications.body:
An assistant that anticipates your needs

LIA's Heartbeat system periodically analyzes your personal context to decide if it has something useful to share. It only interrupts when it's relevant.

9 context sources

Each cycle, Heartbeat aggregates in parallel:

  • Calendar — Events in the next 6 hours
  • Tasks — Pending tasks over the next 2 days
  • Emails — Up to 5 recent unread emails
  • Weather — Current conditions with alert thresholds (rain, extreme temperature, strong wind)
  • Interests — A varied sample of your favourite topics (one per theme, least recently covered first), so suggestions rotate instead of circling back to the same passion
  • Memories — Up to 5 relevant long-term memories
  • Activity — Last message timestamp (inactivity detection)
  • Time — Temporal context with user timezone
  • Recent heartbeats — The content of the last notifications (10 over 7 days) for anti-redundancy: a topic, activity or product already suggested is never proposed again, even from another source

Two-phase LLM decision

Heartbeat uses a two-phase LLM pipeline:

  • select_target() — Analyzes the full context and decides whether to notify, and if so, which topic is most relevant.
  • generate_content() — Generates the message in the style of the assistant's active personality.

Scheduling and guardrails

The Heartbeat scheduler runs every 30 minutes and processes users in batches of 50. Guardrails are strict:

  • Maximum 3 notifications per day, minimum 1 per day
  • Allowed time range: 9am-10pm (user's local time)
  • 2-hour cooldown between two notifications
  • Automatic deactivation after 7 days of inactivity

Conversational initiative

Beyond scheduled notifications, LIA is also proactive during conversations. After executing your request, an Initiative Agent analyzes the results and checks related information across domains — entirely on its own. If the weather forecast shows rain on Saturday and you have an outdoor hike planned, LIA will mention it. If an email proposes a meeting on Thursday and you already have a conflict, LIA will flag it. This is 100% prompt-driven (no hardcoded rules), limited to read-only actions, and enriched by your memory and interests.

reminders-scheduling.title: Reminders and Scheduled Actions: Automate Your Daily Life
reminders-scheduling.excerpt: Create reminders in natural language and schedule recurring actions. LIA handles timing, timezones, and push notifications.
reminders-scheduling.body:
Natural language reminders

Creating a reminder with LIA is as simple as saying:

  • "Remind me to call Marie tomorrow at 9am"
  • "Reminder in 30 minutes: check the oven"
  • "Remember to buy bread tonight"

LIA automatically interprets time expressions and creates the reminder with the correct timezone.

Reminder lifecycle

Each reminder follows a precise lifecycle: PENDING → PROCESSING → deleted after notification. Reminders are one-shot: once successfully delivered, they are automatically deleted. Each reminder contains three key fields:

  • content — The content understood by LIA (reformulated if needed)
  • original_message — The user's exact text
  • trigger_at — The trigger time in UTC

Timezone management

All reminders are stored in UTC in the database. The user's IANA timezone (e.g., Europe/Paris, America/New_York) is tracked and used to convert relative time expressions ("tomorrow at 9am") into absolute UTC timestamps. Display is always converted to the user's local timezone.

Push notifications

Reminders are delivered via Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for browser and mobile notifications. Notifications arrive even when the app isn't open.

Scheduled actions

Scheduled Actions constitute a separate domain that goes beyond simple reminders. They integrate with APScheduler to schedule recurring tasks that LIA executes automatically:

  • Weather summary every morning at 7am
  • Important email check every 2 hours
  • Weekly task report every Monday

Reasonable limits

To prevent abuse, each user can have up to 20 active scheduled actions simultaneously. Retry logic with backoff handles temporary failures.

sub-agents.title: Sub-Agents: Ephemeral Experts for Complex Questions
sub-agents.excerpt: For questions requiring parallel research, LIA delegates to specialized sub-agents that work simultaneously and synthesize results.
sub-agents.body:
True graph invocations

LIA's sub-agents are not simple tool calls: they are true separate LangGraph graph invocations. Each sub-agent has its own state, context, and tool set. The pipeline is direct: instruction → SmartPlannerService.plan() → execute_plan_parallel() → LLM synthesis.

Automatic or on-demand

Delegation can be:

  • Automatic — The planner detects that a multi-domain search would benefit from parallelization
  • Manual — You explicitly ask: "Delegate to experts a comparison of trains/planes/carpooling from Paris to Lyon"

Sub-agents operate with auto_approve_plan=True: no intermediate HITL validation, which significantly speeds up execution.

V1: read-only

In the current version (V1), sub-agents are limited to read operations (search, lookup). No destructive operations (deletion, modification, sending) are allowed. This restriction will be gradually lifted in future versions.

Configurable execution limits

Each sub-agent is bounded by strict limits:

  • Iterations — From 1 to 15 (default: 5)
  • Timeout — From 10 to 600 seconds (default: 120s)

3 levels of guardrails

The sub-agent system is protected by 3 security levels:

  • Static limits — Maximum number of iterations and timeout configured in advance
  • Real-time monitoring — SubAgentTokenGuard monitors token consumption during execution and can interrupt a sub-agent that exceeds its budget
  • Manual control — Manual kill possible + automatic deactivation in case of repeated overruns

Daily budget per user

Sub-agent token consumption is tracked daily per user. This tracking helps detect abuse, adjust limits, and ensure fair use of LLM resources. Statistics are visible in the dashboard.

security-architecture.title: Defense in Depth: LIA's 5 Security Principles
security-architecture.excerpt: Defense in depth, least privilege, rate limiting, encryption, and validation: discover how LIA protects your data at every layer.
security-architecture.body:
5 fundamental principles

LIA's security rests on five principles applied at every application layer:

  • Defense in depth — Multi-layer controls (authentication, rate limiting, validation, encryption)
  • Least privilege — Minimal permissions by default
  • Fail securely — On error, the system denies rather than allows
  • Don't trust input — Pydantic validation + systematic sanitization
  • Security by default — HTTPS, HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, strict CORS

Hashing and encryption

Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (with automatic salt). Sensitive data (OAuth tokens, connector credentials, PII, MCP server credentials) is encrypted with Fernet (AES-128 CBC + HMAC-SHA256), ensuring confidentiality and integrity. Encryption keys are managed separately from data.

JWT and session management

JWT tokens use the HS256 algorithm with a JTI (JWT ID) blacklist system in Redis. Single-use tokens (email verification, password reset) are invalidated after first use. This mechanism prevents any reuse of sensitive tokens.

Strong authentication and device control

Signing in goes beyond the password. WebAuthn passkeys let you authenticate with Face ID, a fingerprint or your device code — phishing-resistant by design, with single-use server challenges and clone detection via signature counters. A TOTP second factor adds a 6-digit step to password sign-in, backed by ten single-use backup codes hashed at rest. Sensitive actions — managing credentials, exporting data, signing out other devices — sit behind a step-up re-authentication: a fresh 5-minute confirmation window with a typed API contract, never a silent redirect. And My devices lists every live session with deliberately bounded metadata (browser and OS families, truncated IP), revokes any of them instantly — a revoked session loses its live streams within seconds — and pushes an alert when the account signs in from an unrecognized device.

Configurable rate limiting

Rate limiting operates at two levels:

  • HTTP — Via nginx upstream
  • Tools — Per-user, per-tool sliding window with settings-driven thresholds, covering every paid external API (image generation, web search, browser, DevOps CLI)
  • External connectors — Distributed Redis sliding window shared across instances (Google, Apple, API-key providers)

API limits are strict: 10 items maximum per request, with per-domain defaults (10 by default, 50 maximum).

Rendering & network hardening

The chat renders LLM output — which can relay third-party HTML (email bodies, fetched pages, tool results) — through a strict sanitization boundary (rehype-sanitize with an audited schema): <script>, <iframe>, <form> and event handlers are dropped, while legitimate cards, buttons and math survive. Interactive MCP/Skill apps never go through markdown — they mount only inside a sandboxed iframe widget. On the network side, the production API sits behind Cloudflare as the single entry point, with the container ports loopback-bound and uvicorn trusting only the reverse-proxy headers, so request.client.host is the real visitor IP: per-IP rate limits apply per visitor rather than to one shared internal address.

Prompt injection protection

External content (emails, web pages, documents) is encapsulated in configurable UNTRUSTED tags before injection into prompts. This explicit wrapping prevents malicious content from hijacking the assistant's behavior by clearly separating user data from system instructions.

Resource ownership verification

Every resource access goes through check_resource_ownership() with a hide_existence parameter: public resources return 403 (access denied), private resources return 404 (resource not found) to avoid revealing their existence to an attacker.

Per-User Usage Quotas

LIA enables administrators to set per-user quotas on tokens, messages, and costs. Enforcement uses a 5-layer defense-in-depth architecture: router-level check (HTTP 429), service-level (SSE error), LLM invocation guard (centralized in invoke_with_instrumentation), proactive runner skip, and direct call migration. If infrastructure (Redis/DB) fails, the system fails open (allows access) since this is cost control, not security. An admin kill switch enables instant blocking/unblocking of any user.

Software supply chain

Every release is built from a locked dependency graph: universal lockfiles pin the ~200 packages actually installed, each verified by SHA256 fingerprint at build time — the same version always yields the same, integrity-checked image. All dependencies, transitive ones included, are continuously audited against known-vulnerability databases, and the software inventory (SBOM) published with each release lists exactly what runs in production.

privacy-by-design.title: Privacy by Design: GDPR, Encryption, and Data Control
privacy-by-design.excerpt: LIA encrypts your sensitive data, minimizes collection, gives you full control, and respects GDPR principles.
privacy-by-design.body:
Privacy by design

LIA is designed from the ground up with data protection as a founding principle, not an afterthought.

Fernet symmetric encryption

All sensitive data is encrypted with Fernet (AES-128 CBC + HMAC-SHA256) via the encrypt_data() function. This covers OAuth tokens, connector credentials, PII, and MCP server credentials. OAuth credentials are encrypted before database writes and decrypted on-the-fly during retrieval. Encryption keys are managed separately from data.

Collection minimization

LIA only collects data strictly necessary for its operation:

  • Profile information (name, email, preferences)
  • Conversation history (encrypted)
  • Service connection tokens (encrypted)
  • Anonymized usage metrics

Deletion and cascading

Deleting a user account triggers a complete cascading delete: connectors, conversations, settings, sessions, memories, and all associated data are irreversibly deleted. No orphaned data persists in the database.

Secure sessions and cookies

Session cookies are configured with HttpOnly, Secure (in production), and SameSite=lax attributes. Session duration is 7 days by default, extendable to 30 days with the "Remember me" option. Single-use tokens are invalidated after first use via a Redis blacklist.

External content protection

Content retrieved from external sources (emails, web pages, documents) is tagged as UNTRUSTED with configurable wrapping before injection into prompts. The web_fetch tool is rate limited to 10 calls per 60-second window per user to prevent abuse.

PII filtering in logs

The logging system applies OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet recommendations to automatically filter personal data from application logs. No sensitive data appears in logs.

Data portability (v1.9.1)

LIA allows each user to export their own consumption data as CSV from Settings > Features. Three export types: LLM consumption (tokens and costs per call), Google API consumption, and aggregated summary. Security: the user_id is forced server-side — no parameter is exposed, preventing access to other users' data (IDOR protection).

Backups with a proven restore

Protecting data also means making sure it survives incidents. The production database is backed up automatically every night, with 7 days, 4 weeks and 6 months of history kept, in a dedicated directory with restrictive permissions. And because a backup only counts once a restore has been proven, the procedure is tested for real: the latest dump is restored into a disposable container and compared against the live database (schema revision, row counts) — a drill that ships with the stack.

observability.title: 419 Prometheus Metrics, 25 Grafana Dashboards, and Langfuse Tracing
observability.excerpt: LIA offers enterprise-grade observability with 419 metrics, dedicated Grafana dashboards, LLM tracing via Langfuse, and email alerting with runbooks.
observability.body:
The three pillars of observability

LIA implements the three pillars of modern observability:

  • Metrics — 419 Prometheus metrics covering HTTP, agents, tokens, costs, OAuth, and performance
  • Logs — Structured JSON logging via structlog, centralized in Loki with PII filtering
  • Traces — Distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry (Tempo) and LLM tracing via Langfuse

23 specialized metrics files

Each domain has its own declarative metrics file. The 23 modules cover: HTTP, agents (SSE/router/LLM/HITL/planner), database, LangGraph, Langfuse, voice, RAG spaces, OAuth, channels, errors, sub-agents, Redis, attachments, browser, compaction, briefing, business, registry, heartbeat, health metrics, journals, telephony, and usage limits. Each file defines domain-specific Prometheus Counter, Histogram, and Gauge metrics.

Prometheus metrics definition

Each domain defines its metrics declaratively:

from prometheus_client import Counter, Histogram, Gauge

http_requests_total = Counter(
    "http_requests_total",
    "Total HTTP requests",
    ["method", "endpoint", "status"],
)

http_request_duration_seconds = Histogram(
    "http_request_duration_seconds",
    "HTTP request duration in seconds",
    ["method", "endpoint"],
)

router_confidence_score = Histogram(
    "router_confidence_score",
    "Router confidence score distribution",
    ["intention"],
    buckets=[0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0],
)

25 Grafana dashboards

LIA provides 25 Grafana dashboards numbered 01 to 25: app-overview, slo-tracking, infra-resources, http-api, llm-tokens-cost, logs-traces, agents-pipeline, hitl, conversations-users, oauth-connectors-mcp, voice-websocket, channels, proactive-heartbeat, registry-checkpoints, langgraph-deep, meta-health, user-analytics-geo, rag-spaces, subagents-skills, react-browser, health-metrics, compaction, journals-user-model, telephony, and briefing. Each dashboard offers views filterable by user, time period, and environment.

Target KPIs from code

LIA monitors precise indicators defined in source code: streaming TTFT (Time To First Token), router latency between 0.1 and 2 seconds, agent tool execution duration between 0.1 and 10 seconds, router confidence p50 > 0.8, LLM cost per request < €0.05, HTTP 5xx error rate < 1%.

Email alerts with runbooks

Supervision doesn't stop at dashboards: a core of 13 vital alerts — API, PostgreSQL or Redis down, disk, container memory, 5xx error rate, streaming latency, failed nightly backup, unreachable public URL, TLS certificate close to expiry — is continuously evaluated by Prometheus and delivered by email through Alertmanager. Every alert references its runbook (step-by-step resolution procedure), thresholds are set per environment in .env files, and promtool unit tests guarantee that the thresholds displayed in notifications match the firing expressions exactly. A blackbox probe even tests the whole chain end to end, from the Cloudflare edge to the frontend, exactly like a user would.

Langfuse: dedicated LLM tracing

The Langfuse integration has 8 dedicated metrics to trace every LLM call: consumed tokens (input/output/cache), response time, model used, estimated cost, and request context. This identifies inefficient prompts, compares LLM models against each other, and optimizes token consumption over time.

DevOps Claude CLI: Natural Language Diagnostics (v1.13.0)

Latest evolution of the observability stack: administrators can now diagnose servers directly from the LIA conversation. By simply asking "Check the logs to see if everything is working", Claude Code CLI — installed in the API Docker container — independently inspects logs, checks container health, analyzes resource usage and reports its findings. Persistent sessions for multi-turn investigations, configurable permissions per environment (prod read-only, dev full access), and real-time streaming of investigation steps via SSE.

prompt-engineering.title: Versioned Prompt System: 78 Prompts Managed as Code
prompt-engineering.excerpt: LIA manages its 78 prompts like source code: versioned, cached, hash-validated, and dynamically loaded for each system component.
prompt-engineering.body:
Prompts managed as code

LIA uses a versioned prompt system where each prompt is a text file stored in src/domains/agents/prompts/v1/. This approach offers versioning, code review, and traceability.

78 specialized prompts by category

The system includes 78 prompt files organized by category:

  • Pipeline core — query_analyzer (routing), smart_planner, response, semantic_validator, semantic_pivot, compaction
  • Domain agents (17) — brave, browser, calendar, contacts, drive, emails, health, hue, perplexity, places, query, routes, tasks, weather, web_fetch, web_search, wikipedia
  • ReAct loops — react_agent, subagent_react, skill_react, mcp_react
  • HITL — classifier (with per-action-type examples), draft_critique, plan_approval, question_generator, draft_modifier
  • Memory & psyche — extraction, reference resolution, behavioral directives, psyche self-report and embodiment
  • Proactivity — heartbeat decision/message, initiative, interests, reminders
  • Journals & briefing — introspection, consolidation, daily greeting and synthesis
  • Identity & translations — app_identity, default_personality, broadcast/skill/personality translation

Smart loading and dynamic detection

Prompts are loaded via load_prompt() and load_prompt_with_fallback() which enables gradual migration between versions. The system dynamically detects available versions by scanning the filesystem for directories matching the v[0-9]+ pattern. The LRU cache with SHA256 hash validation detects modifications. Versions are configurable via environment variables (e.g., ROUTER_PROMPT_VERSION=v1).

The prompt loader in practice

The system uses an LRU cache and SHA256 hash validation:

@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
def load_prompt(
    name: PromptName,
    version: PromptVersion = "v1",
    validate_hash: bool = False,
    expected_hash: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    prompt_file = PROMPTS_DIR / version / f"{name}.txt"
    content = prompt_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    if validate_hash and expected_hash:
        actual_hash = hashlib.sha256(
            content.encode("utf-8")
        ).hexdigest()
        if actual_hash != expected_hash:
            raise PromptIntegrityError(...)

    return content

Provider-agnostic prompt caching

Every dynamic system prompt separates its static prefix (role, rules, examples, output format) from per-request content with a canonical --- DYNAMIC CONTEXT --- marker. Templates stay model-neutral: the infrastructure layer translates this single convention into each provider's caching dialect — Anthropic cache_control blocks, OpenAI prompt_cache_key routing, implicit prefix caches elsewhere — cutting billed tokens and latency on repeated requests. The planner, the pipeline's most expensive prompt, exposes a ~77% byte-stable cacheable prefix, and shrink-only CI guards (marker required, no placeholder before it, byte stability asserted) keep the convention from regressing.

Prompt injection: security principles

External content injected into prompts (emails, web pages) is encapsulated in security tags to prevent prompt injection attacks. Prompts are also designed to be robust against manipulation attempts.

smart-services.title: Smart Services: Pattern Learning and Token Optimization
smart-services.excerpt: LIA learns from your interactions through Smart Services: LRU cache, Bayesian learning, and semantic routing to reduce token consumption by 96%.
smart-services.body:
Three intelligent services

LIA integrates three services that learn from your interactions to optimize performance:

  • QueryAnalyzerService — Unified analysis of intent, domain, and routing in a single pass, with a P95 under 800 ms thanks to caching
  • SmartPlannerService — Reduces token consumption by 89% (from ~14,100 tokens in 3 steps to ~1,500 tokens). Applies 4 strategies by priority: ReferenceBypass, CrossDomainBypass, SingleDomain (LLM) and MultiDomain (LLM). A PANIC mode retries with an expanded catalog on failure
  • SmartCatalogueService — Reduces the tool catalog by 96% (from ~5,500 tokens for the full catalog to ~200 filtered tokens). Uses a NormalFilteringStrategy in standard mode and a PanicFilteringStrategy on retry

The ToolResponse pattern

Every tool returns a standardized format for the orchestrator:

class ToolResponse(BaseModel):
    success: bool
    data: Any | None = None
    error: str | None = None
    error_code: ToolErrorCode | None = None
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    timestamp: datetime = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC)
    )

# Usage in a tool
async def my_tool(...) -> dict:
    try:
        result = await do_something()
        return ToolResponse(
            success=True, data=result
        ).model_dump()
    except Exception as e:
        return ToolErrorModel.from_exception(
            e, context={"tool": "my_tool"}
        ).to_response()

Bayesian learning

The Pattern Learner uses Bayesian learning to recognize recurring request patterns. Golden patterns are trained to accelerate routing of the most frequent requests.

Token optimization: up to 96% reduction

The combination of the three services produces considerable savings. SmartCatalogueService reduces the catalog by 96% (from ~5,500 to ~200 tokens). SmartPlannerService reduces planning by 89% (from ~14,100 to ~1,500 tokens) by short-circuiting single-domain and cross-domain requests. QueryAnalyzerService unifies analysis into a single pass instead of three separate calls.

Adaptive replanning and PANIC mode

When a step fails, the system activates PANIC mode with exponential backoff. SmartPlannerService retries with an expanded catalog via PanicFilteringStrategy, SmartCatalogueService includes additional tools, and full replanning is triggered if necessary. The user always receives the best possible response.

multilingual.title: 6 Languages, a Complete i18n Architecture
multilingual.excerpt: LIA speaks French, English, German, Spanish, Italian, and Chinese. Internationalization covers the UI, AI responses, and documentation.
multilingual.body:
6 natively supported languages

LIA is fully available in French, English, German, Spanish, Italian, and Chinese. Internationalization isn't limited to the interface: it covers assistant responses, notifications, FAQ, and documentation.

Frontend i18n architecture

The frontend uses react-i18next with per-language JSON files and language choice persistence via a NEXT_LOCALE cookie (1-year TTL). Next.js routing uses a dynamic [lng] segment to serve each language at its dedicated URL. Language flags are displayed as Unicode emojis. The locale mapping associates each short code with its full variant (fr-FR, en-US, de-DE, es-ES, it-IT, zh-CN). Pages are statically pre-generated for each language at build time.

Hreflang and multilingual SEO

Each public page declares hreflang alternates for all 6 languages, with an x-default value pointing to French. The XML sitemap includes multilingual alternates for each URL.

Multilingual AI responses

The assistant responds in the user's configured language. Supported languages are configurable on the backend via the SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES environment variable. System prompts are written in English to maximize LLM reasoning quality, but an explicit language instruction guides response generation in the target language. Three prompts are specifically adapted per language: journal_introspection_personality_addon, memory_extraction_personality_addon and broadcast_translation_prompt.

Multilingual voice recognition

The Whisper model used for voice transcription natively supports 99+ languages in offline mode, allowing you to speak to LIA in virtually any language without additional configuration or cloud service dependency.
